paras.zh: 他注意到了，便小心翼翼、煞费苦心地重新摆弄，好几次往后退开，估量效果，直到把它弄得合了自己的心意。

w.m: v. 重新摆放；重新整理

paras.en: Then he gave it a light finishing pat or two with his hand, and said: “She always does that.
paras.zh: 然后，他用手在上面轻轻拍了一两下作为收尾，说道：“她总是这么弄。

paras.en: You can’t tell just what it lacks, but it does lack something until you’ve done that—you can see it yourself after it’s done, but that is all you know; you can’t find out the law of it.
paras.zh: 你说不清它究竟缺了什么，可在你这么弄之前，它确实就是缺点什么——弄好之后，你自己也看得出来，可你也就知道这么多；其中的道理你是弄不清的。

paras.en: It’s like the finishing pats a mother gives the child’s hair after she’s got it combed and brushed, I reckon.
paras.zh: 依我看，这就好比当妈的给孩子把头发梳好、刷顺以后，最后再轻轻拍上的那几下。

paras.en: I’ve seen her fix all these things so much that I can do them all just her way, though I don’t know the law of any of them.
paras.zh: 她摆弄这些东西我见得太多了，所以样样都能完全照她的法子来弄，虽说哪一样的道理我都不懂。

paras.en: But she knows the law.
paras.zh: 可她懂得其中的道理。

paras.en: She knows the why and the how both; but I don’t know the why; I only know the how.”
paras.zh: 为什么这么弄、怎么弄，她两样都懂；可我不懂为什么，我只知道怎么弄。”

paras.en: He took me into a bedroom so that I might wash my hands; such a bedroom as I had not seen for years: white counterpane, white pillows, carpeted floor, papered walls, pictures, dressing-table, with mirror and pin-cushion and dainty toilet things; and in the corner a wash-stand, with real china-ware bowl and pitcher, and with soap in a china dish, and on a rack more than a dozen towels—towels too clean and white for one out of practice to use without some vague sense of profanation.
paras.zh: 他领我进了一间卧室，好让我洗洗手；这样的卧室我已经多年没见过了：白色的床罩，白色的枕头，铺着地毯的地板，糊着墙纸的墙壁，一幅幅图画，还有梳妆台，台上有镜子、针插和精巧的梳妆用品；墙角里有一个脸盆架，上面摆着货真价实的瓷脸盆和瓷水罐，瓷碟里放着肥皂，架子上搭着十几条毛巾——这些毛巾太干净、太白了，一个久疏此道的人拿来用，难免隐隐有种亵渎之感。

w.m: adj. 精巧的；小巧玲珑的
n. 梳妆；（作定语）梳妆用的
n. 瓷器；（作定语）瓷制的

paras.en: So my face spoke again, and he answered with gratified words: “All her work; she did it all herself—every bit.
paras.zh: 于是我的脸又替我说了话，他便满心欣慰地答道：“全是她的手艺；全是她亲手做的——每一点每一滴都是。

paras.en: Nothing here that hasn’t felt the touch of her hand.
paras.zh: 这儿没有一样东西没经过她的手。

paras.en: Now you would think—But I mustn’t talk so much.”
paras.zh: 你会以为——不过我可不能再说这么多了。”

paras.en: By this time I was wiping my hands and glancing from detail to detail of the room’s belongings, as one is apt to do when he is in a new place, where everything he sees is a comfort to his eye and his spirit; and I became conscious, in one of those unaccountable ways, you know, that there was something there somewhere that the man wanted me to discover for myself.
paras.zh: 这时，我一边擦手，一边扫视房里的陈设，目光从一处细节移到另一处；人到了一个新地方，眼前的一切都能慰藉眼睛和心灵，往往就会这样。而且，我还意识到——就是那种说不清道不明的感觉，你知道的——屋里某个地方有样东西，那人想让我自己去发现。

w.m: n. 慰藉；令人舒适的事物
adj. 无法解释的；说不清的

paras.en: I knew it perfectly, and I knew he was trying to help me by furtive indications with his eye, so I tried hard to get on the right track, being eager to gratify him.
paras.zh: 这一点我心里十分清楚；我也知道，他正偷偷用眼神暗示我，想帮我一把，于是我竭力要找对方向，一心想让他高兴。

w.m: adj. 偷偷的；鬼鬼祟祟的

paras.en: I failed several times, as I could see out of the corner of my eye without being told; but at last I knew I must be looking straight at the thing—knew it from the pleasure issuing in invisible waves from him.
paras.zh: 我好几次都没找对，这一点不用人说，我用眼角的余光就看得出来；但最后，我知道自己一定是在直直地看着那样东西了——我是从他的喜悦中知道的，那喜悦正一波波无形地从他身上涌出来。

w.h: out of the corner of one's eye

paras.en: He broke into a happy laugh, and rubbed his hands together, and cried out: “That’s it!
paras.zh: 他突然开心地大笑起来，搓着双手，高声叫道：“就是它！

paras.en: You’ve found it.
paras.zh: 你找到了。

paras.en: I knew you would.
paras.zh: 我就知道你会找到的。

paras.en: It’s her picture.”
paras.zh: 是她的照片。”

paras.en: I went to the little black-walnut bracket on the farther wall, and did find there what I had not yet noticed—a picture case.
paras.zh: 我走到远处那面墙上的黑胡桃木小托架前，果然在那里找到了一样我还没注意到的东西——一个照片匣。

w.m: n. 黑胡桃木；（作定语）黑胡桃木制的

paras.en: It contained the sweetest girlish face, and the most beautiful, as it seemed to me, that I had ever seen.
paras.zh: 匣里装着一张少女的面庞，是我平生所见最甜美的，在我看来也是最美丽的。

paras.en: The man drank the admiration from my face, and was fully satisfied.
paras.zh: 那人从我脸上饮下了这份赞叹，心满意足。

paras.en: “Nineteen her last birthday,” he said, as he put the picture back; “and that was the day we were married.
paras.zh: “她上个生日满十九岁，”他一边把照片放回原处，一边说，“就在那一天，我们结了婚。

paras.en: When you see her—ah, just wait till you see her!”
paras.zh: 等你见到她——啊，等你见到她就知道了！”

w.m: （口）就等着……吧（暗示到时定会惊叹）

paras.en: “Where is she?
paras.zh: “她在哪儿？

paras.en: When will she be in?”
paras.zh: 她什么时候回家？”

paras.en: “Oh, she’s away now.
paras.zh: “哦，她这会儿不在家。

paras.en: She’s gone to see her people.
paras.zh: 她回娘家看家里人去了。

paras.en: They live forty or fifty miles from here.
paras.zh: 他们住在离这儿四五十英里的地方。

paras.en: She’s been gone two weeks today.”
paras.zh: 到今天她已经走了两个星期了。”

paras.en: “When do you expect her back?”
paras.zh: “你估计她什么时候回来？”

paras.en: “This is Wednesday.
paras.zh: “今天是星期三。

paras.en: She’ll be back Saturday, in the evening—about nine o’clock, likely.”
paras.zh: 她星期六回来，晚上到——多半是九点钟左右。”

paras.en: I felt a sharp sense of disappointment.
paras.zh: 我感到一阵强烈的失望。

paras.en: “I’m sorry, because I’ll be gone then,” I said, regretfully.
paras.zh: “真遗憾，到时候我已经走了，”我惋惜地说。

paras.en: “Gone?
paras.zh: “走了？

paras.en: No—why should you go?
paras.zh: 不——你为什么要走呢？

paras.en: Don’t go.
paras.zh: 别走。

paras.en: She’ll be disappointed.”
paras.zh: 她会失望的。”

paras.en: She would be disappointed—that beautiful creature!
paras.zh: 她会失望的——那个美丽的人儿！

w.m: n. 人儿；（带感情色彩）人

paras.en: If she had said the words herself, they could hardly have blessed me more.
paras.zh: 即便这话是她亲口说的，也很难让我更幸福了。

paras.en: I was feeling a deep, strong longing to see her—a longing so supplicating, so insistent, that it made me afraid.
paras.zh: 我心里涌动着一股深切而强烈的渴望，想见到她——这渴望那样苦苦哀求，那样纠缠不休，竟让我害怕起来。

w.m: adj. 一再要求的；纠缠不休的；迫切的

paras.en: I said to myself: “I will go straight away from this place, for my peace of mind’s sake.”
paras.zh: 我对自己说：“为了求得内心的安宁，我要马上离开这个地方。”

paras.en: “You see, she likes to have people come and stop with us—people who know things, and can talk—people like you.
paras.zh: “你瞧，她喜欢有人来我们这儿住住——那些有见识、能聊天的人——像你这样的人。

paras.en: She delights in it; for she knows—oh, she knows nearly everything herself, and can talk, oh, like a bird—and the books she reads, why, you would be astonished.
paras.zh: 她以此为乐；因为她懂——噢，她自己差不多什么都懂，而且能说会道，噢，就像小鸟一样——还有她读的那些书，嘿，你会大吃一惊的。

paras.en: Don’t go; it’s only a little while, you know, and she’ll be so disappointed.”
paras.zh: 别走；你知道，也没多久了，而且她会非常失望的。”

paras.en: I heard the words, but hardly noticed them, I was so deep in my thinkings and strugglings.
paras.zh: 我听见了这些话，却几乎没有在意，我实在太沉浸于自己的思虑与挣扎之中了。

paras.en: He left me, but I didn’t know.
paras.zh: 他从我身边走开了，我却浑然不知。

paras.en: Presently he was back, with the picture case in his hand, and he held it open before me and said: “There, now, tell her to her face you could have stayed to see her, and you wouldn’t.”
paras.zh: 不一会儿，他回来了，手里拿着那个照片匣；他把匣子打开，举到我面前，说：“喏，好了，你当着她的面告诉她，你本来可以留下来见她，可你偏不肯。”

w.m: 好啦；喏（口语，用于引起注意）
本来可以（做，实际却没做）

passages.name: 2022年 Passage One
passages.title: 巴克的王者生活与酝酿中的麻烦
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 动物与命运
passages.summary: 巴克不看报纸，所以不知道麻烦正在酝酿：有人在北极发现了一种黄色金属，成千上万的人正涌入北国，他们需要肌肉强健、皮毛浓密的大块头狗。巴克生在阳光明媚的圣克拉拉谷米勒法官的大宅里，四年来一直统治着这片领地；他生活优裕，有点自高自大，却没有沦为仅仅养在屋里、娇生惯养的狗，打猎等户外乐趣使他没长赘肉、肌肉结实。他也不知道，园丁的帮工曼纽尔是个不该结交的人：曼纽尔爱赌彩票，笃信一套赌法，这注定了他要万劫不复，因为按一套赌法下注需要钱，而他的工钱满足妻儿所需之后并无富余。

paras.en: Buck did not read the newspapers, or he would have known that trouble was brewing, not alone for himself, but for every tidewater dog, strong of muscle and with warm, long hair, from Puget Sound to San Diego.
paras.zh: 巴克不看报纸，否则他就会知道，麻烦正在酝酿，要遭殃的不单是他自己，还有从普吉特湾到圣迭戈每一条肌肉强健、毛又长又暖和的沿海狗。

w.m: 不仅……而且（= not only…but also）
普吉特湾（美国华盛顿州西北部海湾）

paras.en: Because men, groping in the Arctic darkness, had found a yellow metal, and because steamship and transportation companies were booming the find, thousands of men were rushing into the Northland.
paras.zh: 由于有人在北极的黑暗中摸索时发现了一种黄色的金属，又由于轮船公司和运输公司正在大肆宣扬这一发现，成千上万的人正纷纷涌入北国。

w.m: n. 发现；（矿藏等）被发现之物

paras.en: These men wanted dogs, and the dogs they wanted were heavy dogs, with strong muscles by which to toil, and furry coats to protect them from the frost.
paras.zh: 这些人需要狗，而他们需要的是大块头的狗，要有强健的肌肉来干苦活，还要有毛茸茸的皮毛来保护它们免受严寒。

w.m: 借以；用来（介词 + 关系代词 + 不定式）

paras.en: Buck lived at a big house in the sun-kissed Santa Clara Valley.
paras.zh: 巴克住在阳光明媚的圣克拉拉谷中一座大宅子里。

w.m: adj. 阳光充足的；阳光明媚的

paras.en: Judge Miller’s place, it was called.
paras.zh: 人们管这里叫“米勒法官府”。

paras.en: It stood back from the road, half hidden among the trees, through which glimpses could be caught of the wide cool veranda that ran around its four sides.
paras.zh: 宅子离大路有一段距离，半掩在树丛中，透过树木，可以瞥见那条环绕房子四面、宽敞凉爽的游廊。

paras.en: The house was approached by gravelled driveways which wound about through wide-spreading lawns and under the interlacing boughs of tall poplars (杨树).
paras.zh: 通往宅子的是几条碎石车道，蜿蜒曲折，穿过大片大片的草坪，又从高大杨树交错的枝杈下经过。

w.m: adj. 宽广舒展的；大片的

paras.en: At the rear things were on even a more spacious scale than at the front.
paras.zh: 宅子后面的一切，规模比前面还要宏大开阔。

paras.en: There were great stables, where a dozen grooms and boys held forth, rows of vine-clad servants’ cottages, an endless and orderly array of outhouses, long grape arbors, green pastures, orchards, and berry patches.
paras.zh: 这里有宽大的马厩，十几个马夫和小伙计在那里高谈阔论；有一排排爬满藤蔓的仆人小屋，有一长溜整整齐齐、望不到头的附属房屋，有长长的葡萄架、青翠的牧场、果园，还有浆果地。

w.m: 滔滔不绝地讲；高谈阔论
adj. 无尽的；望不到头的
n. （整齐排列的）一大批；一长串

paras.en: Then there was the pumping plant for the artesian well, and the big cement tank where Judge Miller’s boys took their morning plunge and kept cool in the hot afternoon.
paras.zh: 再就是自流井的抽水设备，以及那个大水泥池，米勒法官的儿子们早晨到池里扎猛子，炎热的午后泡在里面消暑。

paras.en: And over this great demesne (自用地) Buck ruled.
paras.zh: 而统治这片偌大领地的，正是巴克。

w.m: n. 领地；（庄园主的）自用地

paras.en: Here he was born, and here he had lived the four years of his life.
paras.zh: 他在这里出生，有生以来的四年也都是在这里度过的。

w.m: v. 度过（一段岁月）；过（……的生活）

paras.en: It was true, there were other dogs.
paras.zh: 诚然，这里也有别的狗。

paras.en: There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count.
paras.zh: 这么大的地方，不可能没有别的狗，但它们都算不上什么。

w.m: 如此……的（一个）（so + 形容词 + a + 名词）

paras.en: They came and went, resided in the populous kennels, or lived obscurely in the recesses of the house after the fashion of Toots, the Japanese pug, or Ysabel, the Mexican hairless,—strange creatures that rarely put nose out of doors or set foot to ground.
paras.zh: 它们来来去去，有的住在狗口众多的狗舍里，有的像日本哈巴狗图茨或墨西哥无毛犬伊莎贝尔那样，默默无闻地待在宅子深处的角落里——这些古怪的家伙难得把鼻子探出门外，脚也难得沾地。

w.m: adj. 人口稠密的；（此处）狗多的
adv. 默默无闻地；不引人注意地

paras.en: On the other hand, there were the fox terriers, a score of them at least, who yelped fearful promises at Toots and Ysabel looking out of the windows at them and protected by a legion of housemaids armed with brooms and mops.
paras.zh: 另一方面，还有那些猎狐梗，少说也有二十条，它们冲着图茨和伊莎贝尔尖声狂吠，放出种种吓人的狠话；图茨和伊莎贝尔则从窗户里往外望着它们，身边有一大群手持扫帚和拖把的女仆护着。

w.m: n. 许诺；（此处为反语）威胁；狠话

paras.en: But Buck was neither house-dog nor kennel-dog.
paras.zh: 但巴克既不是养在屋里的狗，也不是养在狗舍里的狗。

w.m: n. 养在屋里的狗；室内犬

paras.en: The whole realm was his.
paras.zh: 整个王国都归他所有。

paras.en: He plunged into the swimming tank or went hunting with the Judge’s sons; he escorted Mollie and Alice, the Judge’s daughters, on long twilight or early morning rambles; on wintry nights he lay at the Judge’s feet before the roaring library fire; he carried the Judge’s grandsons on his back, or rolled them in the grass, and guarded their footsteps through wild adventures down to the fountain in the stable yard, and even beyond, where the paddocks were, and the berry patches.
paras.zh: 他跳进游泳池，或者跟法官的儿子们去打猎；法官的女儿莫莉和艾丽斯在黄昏或清晨长时间漫步，他一路护送；冬夜里，他躺在法官脚边，面前是书房里熊熊燃烧的炉火；他把法官的孙子们驮在背上，或者推着他们在草地上打滚；孩子们一路狂野冒险，他就一路守护着他们的脚步，直到马厩院子里的喷泉边，甚至更远，一直到围场和浆果地那边。

paras.en: Among the terriers he stalked imperiously, and Toots and Ysabel he utterly ignored, for he was king,—king over all creeping, crawling, flying things of Judge Miller’s place, humans included.
paras.zh: 他在那些猎狐梗中间昂首阔步，一副盛气凌人的样子；对图茨和伊莎贝尔，他根本不理睬，因为他是王——是米勒法官府上一切匍匐的、爬行的、飞翔的生灵之王，连人类也包括在内。

w.m: n. 梗犬（此处指上文的猎狐梗）
v. 高视阔步地走；昂首阔步
adv. 专横地；盛气凌人地
adj. 匍匐的；缓慢爬动的

paras.en: His father, Elmo, a huge St. Bernard, had been the Judge’s inseparable companion, and Buck bid fair to follow in the way of his father.
paras.zh: 他的父亲埃尔莫是一条硕大的圣伯纳犬，曾是法官形影不离的伙伴；巴克看来很有希望追随父亲的足迹。

w.m: adj. 形影不离的；分不开的

paras.en: He was not so large,—he weighed only one hundred and forty pounds,—for his mother, Shep, had been a Scotch shepherd dog.
paras.zh: 他个头没有父亲那么大——体重只有一百四十磅——因为他的母亲谢普是一条苏格兰牧羊犬。

paras.en: Nevertheless, one hundred and forty pounds, to which was added the dignity that comes of good living and universal respect, enabled him to carry himself in right royal fashion.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，一百四十磅的体重，再加上生活优裕、受人普遍尊敬而生出的那份威严，使他举止之间尽显十足的王者气派。

w.m: 被加到……之上（此处倒装：再加上）

paras.en: During the four years since his puppyhood he had lived the life of a sated (饱享的) aristocrat; he had a fine pride in himself, was even a trifle egotistical, as country gentlemen sometimes become because of their insular situation.
paras.zh: 从幼年算起的这四年里，他一直过着心满意足、饱享一切的贵族生活；他对自己十分自豪，甚至有点自高自大，乡绅们因为处境闭塞，有时也会变成这样。

w.m: adj. （欲望）得到充分满足的；饱享的
adj. 自高自大的；自我中心的
adj. 闭塞的；与世隔绝的

paras.en: But he had saved himself by not becoming a mere pampered house-dog.
paras.zh: 但他没有沦为一条仅仅养在屋里、娇生惯养的狗，从而保全了自己。

w.m: 保全自己；使自己免于（沉沦）
adj. 娇生惯养的；被宠坏的
n. 养在屋里的狗；室内犬

paras.en: Hunting and kindred outdoor delights had kept down the fat and hardened his muscles; and to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water had been a tonic and a health preserver.
paras.zh: 打猎以及类似的户外乐趣使他没长赘肉，肌肉也变得结实；而且对他来说，正如对那些洗冷水浴的民族一样，爱水一直是一剂补药，也是保持健康的良方。

w.m: 保持健康之物；保健良方

paras.en: And this was the manner of Buck in the fall of 1897, when the Klondike strike dragged men from all the world into the frozen North.
paras.zh: 1897年秋天，巴克就是这副样子；那时，克朗代克发现的金矿正把世界各地的人拖进冰封的北国。

w.m: n. 克朗代克（加拿大育空地区，1896年在此发现金矿）

paras.en: But Buck did not read the newspapers, and he did not know that Manuel, one of the gardener’s helpers, was an undesirable acquaintance.
paras.zh: 但巴克不看报纸，也不知道园丁的一个帮工曼纽尔是个不该结交的人。

w.m: adj. 不受欢迎的；不宜结交的

paras.en: Manuel had one besetting sin.
paras.zh: 曼纽尔有一个改不掉的恶习。

paras.en: He loved to play the lottery.
paras.zh: 他爱赌彩票。

paras.en: Also, in his gambling, he had one besetting weakness—faith in a system; and this made his damnation certain.
paras.zh: 而且，他赌博时还有一个改不掉的弱点——笃信一套赌法；这就注定了他要万劫不复。

w.m: adj. 不断困扰的；难以摆脱的
n. （赌博中的）一套赌法；下注方法
n. 毁灭；（宗教）罚入地狱

paras.en: For to play a system requires money, while the wages of a gardener’s helper do not lap over the needs of a wife and numerous progeny.
paras.zh: 因为按一套赌法下注是需要钱的，而一个园丁帮工的工钱，满足妻子和一大群儿女的需要之后，并无富余。

passages.name: 2022年 Passage Two
passages.title: 珠峰登山安全背后的经济账
passages.genre: 议论文 · 旅游与安全
passages.summary: 尼泊尔近年来不断发布登山新规，看似在改善管理，但作者认为，这些规定即便得到执行，也无助于减轻攀登珠峰的危险，何况尼泊尔既没有资源，也没有决心执行。借鉴其他名山的做法、推行真正的改革（如限制每季登山人数），可以让珠峰更安全，但由于低价向导公司的兴起，这类改革付诸实行的可能性比以往任何时候都小。这些公司让珠峰的登山人群更加多元，但在缺乏政府实质性监管的情况下，一些低价公司让大批新手跟着缺乏经验的向导上山，使珠峰变得更加危险。作者指出，最大的危险往往源于经济因素而非自然力量，许多旅游官员和登山服务商首要考虑的不是安全，而是利润。

paras.en: Early this winter, the hundreds of climbers making plans for spring-summit attempts on Mount Qomolangma suddenly faced a new set of rules.
paras.zh: 今冬之初，数百名正在筹划春季冲顶珠穆朗玛峰的登山者突然面临一套新规定。

paras.en: In December, the Nepalese government decreed that it would no longer issue permits to blind, solo, or double-amputee mountaineers for any of its high peaks.
paras.zh: 12月，尼泊尔政府颁布法令，规定今后不再向盲人登山者、单人登山者或双侧截肢的登山者发放该国任何一座高峰的登山许可证。

w.m: v. 颁布法令；下令规定
n. 登山者；登山运动员

paras.en: Furthermore, all expeditions would have to employ at least one Sherpa (夏尔巴人向导) and would be forbidden from using helicopters to reach high camps.
paras.zh: 此外，所有登山队都必须至少雇用一名夏尔巴人向导，并且不得乘直升机抵达高海拔营地。

w.m: n. 夏尔巴人（常受雇担任高山向导）

paras.en: The regulations fit a pattern established by Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism, which in the past few years has issued a series of proclamations—climbers must announce plans to set records, trekkers must carry location beacons—that suggest improved management of its high-altitude peaks.
paras.zh: 这些规定符合尼泊尔旅游部确立的一贯做法：过去几年里，该部发布了一系列公告——登山者若打算创纪录，必须公布计划；徒步旅行者必须携带定位信标——这些公告让人觉得该国高海拔山峰的管理有所改善。

paras.en: Each new declaration generates a rush of international news reports about authorities making strides toward addressing safety at the top of the world.
paras.zh: 每一项新声明都会引发一波国际新闻报道，称当局在解决世界之巅的安全问题上取得了长足进展。

paras.en: The truth is a lot more complicated.
paras.zh: 真实情况要复杂得多。

paras.en: Mountaineering is big business in Nepal.
paras.zh: 登山在尼泊尔是一门大生意。

paras.en: Industry experts estimate that it generates some $26.5 million in tourism income each year, with around $11 million of that coming from Qomolangma climbers alone.
paras.zh: 据业内专家估计，登山每年带来约2650万美元的旅游收入，其中仅攀登珠峰的登山者就贡献了约1100万美元。

paras.en: The enduring obsession of the Western media with tragic deaths on these far-off snowy peaks has resulted in a lot of free marketing.
paras.zh: 西方媒体长久以来一直热衷于报道这些遥远雪峰上的悲惨死亡事件，由此带来了大量免费宣传。

w.m: adj. 持久的；经久不衰的
adj. 积雪的；被雪覆盖的

paras.en: Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism, perhaps concerned that all the morbid tales might drive climbers to Qomolangma’s less used Chinese side, has gained some control of that narrative by broadcasting more positive developments through the Nepalese press.
paras.zh: 尼泊尔旅游部或许是担心种种骇人的死亡故事可能会把登山者赶到珠峰较少有人走的中国一侧，便通过尼泊尔新闻界播报更多积极进展，在一定程度上掌控了这种叙事。

w.m: adj. 阴森可怖的；（对死亡等）病态的

paras.en: But the rules announced to date would do nothing to mitigate the dangers of climbing Qomolangma even if Nepal had the resources and conviction to enforce them, which it doesn’t.
paras.zh: 但迄今公布的这些规定，即便尼泊尔有资源、有决心执行，也丝毫无助于减轻攀登珠峰的危险，而尼泊尔并没有这样的资源和决心。

w.m: 丝毫无助于；对……毫无作用

paras.en: Making a huge, hugely popular mountain safer is possible.
paras.zh: 让一座体量巨大、又极受欢迎的山峰变得更安全，是可以做到的。

paras.en: On Alaska’s Denali, full-time climbing rangers conduct safety checks of many teams and are mobilized for rescue operations.
paras.zh: 在阿拉斯加的德纳里峰，全职登山巡护员会对许多登山队实施安全检查，还会被调派执行救援行动。

paras.en: On Argentina’s Aconcagua, rangers patrol all high camps, and until recently, permit fees included the cost of helicopter rescues.
paras.zh: 在阿根廷的阿空加瓜峰，巡护员在所有高海拔营地巡逻，而且直到不久前，许可证费用中还包含直升机救援的开销。

paras.en: Adopting similar policies in Nepal would be a good start.
paras.zh: 在尼泊尔采取类似的政策，会是一个良好的开端。

paras.en: A longer list of true reforms would include ordering all climbers to have previously summited a 7,000-meter peak, requiring non-guides working above Base Camp to take a course at the Khumbu Climbing Center (hundreds have done so since it was founded in 2003), and capping the total number of climbers on the mountain at 500 per season, including support staff.
paras.zh: 若把真正的改革措施列得更全一些，还会包括：规定所有登山者此前必须登顶过一座7000米级的山峰；要求在大本营以上工作的非向导人员到昆布攀登中心参加培训课程（自该中心2003年成立以来，已有数百人参加过）；以及把每个登山季山上的登山者总数限制在500人，后勤保障人员也计算在内。

w.m: v. 命令；规定（某人做某事）

paras.en: That last policy would both reduce dangerous crowding and help keep the mountain clean.
paras.zh: 最后这项政策既能减少危险的拥堵，又有助于保持山上的清洁。

paras.en: Unfortunately, these kinds of rules are less likely than ever to be instituted on Qomolangma, owing to the rise of budget guiding companies.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，由于低价向导公司的兴起，这类规定在珠峰付诸实行的可能性比以往任何时候都小。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是
（与比较级连用）比以往任何时候都……

paras.en: Beginning in the early 1990s, Western outfitters established commercial mountaineering on the Nepal side of the peak by attracting clients willing to pay as much as $65,000 to be guided to the summit.
paras.zh: 从20世纪90年代初开始，西方登山服务商招揽愿意花多达65000美元请向导带领自己登顶的客户，由此在珠峰的尼泊尔一侧开创了商业登山。

w.m: n. 登山服务商；户外探险服务公司

paras.en: That business model dominated for more than two decades, bringing an estimated 9,000 paying climbers to Base Camp.
paras.zh: 这种商业模式在二十多年里一直占据主导地位，据估计把9000名付费登山者带到了大本营。

paras.en: Consequently, Qomolangma earned a reputation as a magnet for the rich, ambitious, and inexperienced.
paras.zh: 因此，珠峰有了这样一个名声：它像磁石一样，吸引着有钱、有雄心又缺乏经验的人。

w.m: 吸引……的人或地方；……的磁石
adj. 有雄心的；野心勃勃的

paras.en: As in many markets, savvy entrepreneurs saw opportunities for disruption.
paras.zh: 和许多市场的情况一样，精明的创业者看到了颠覆现有格局的机会。

w.m: n. （对行业现有格局的）颠覆；扰乱

paras.en: Lower-cost guiding companies, some founded by Westerners and others by Nepalese, slowly gained traction by offering Qomolangma climbs for as little as a third of the going rate among high-end outfitters.
paras.zh: 收费较低的向导公司有的由西方人创办，有的由尼泊尔人创办，它们提供珠峰攀登服务，价格低至高端登山服务商现行价格的三分之一，由此慢慢站稳了脚跟。

w.m: adj. 收费较低的；低成本的

paras.en: Then came 2014, when 16 Sherpas died after a serac (冰塔) collapsed onto the Khumbu Icefall, part of the main route from Base Camp to Camp I.
paras.zh: 接着就到了2014年：一座冰塔崩塌，砸落在昆布冰瀑上，16名夏尔巴人遇难；昆布冰瀑是大本营通往一号营地这条主路线上的一段。

paras.en: In the wake of that tragedy, a small group of Sherpas demanded that the Nepalese government establish regulations that would improve working conditions, increase pay, boost life-insurance coverage, and provide a funeral stipend.
paras.zh: 那场悲剧发生后，一小群夏尔巴人要求尼泊尔政府制定规章，以改善工作条件、增加薪酬、提高人寿保险的保障额度，并提供丧葬补助。

paras.en: Ultimately, Sherpas received a bit more insurance—the minimum payout was doubled from $5,500 to $11,000—but not much else.
paras.zh: 最终，夏尔巴人多得到了一点保险——最低赔付额从5500美元翻了一番，达到11000美元——但除此之外就没得到多少了。

paras.en: Partly in response to media attention to these events, Nepali-owned guiding companies have continued to gain influence and market share on Qomolangma.
paras.zh: 部分是因为媒体关注这些事件，尼泊尔人拥有的向导公司在珠峰的影响力和市场份额持续扩大。

paras.en: The shift away from foreign control of the mountain is welcomed by many in the climbing community.
paras.zh: 这座山正逐渐摆脱外国人的掌控，这一转变受到登山界许多人的欢迎。

paras.en: Another positive development: lower-cost operators are increasing diversity on Qomolangma, attracting climbers from China’s and India’s burgeoning middle classes with aggressive pricing.
paras.zh: 另一个积极的进展是：收费较低的运营商正在让珠峰上的登山人群更加多元，它们以低价攻势吸引来自中国和印度日益壮大的中产阶层的登山者。

w.m: adj. 迅速发展的；日益壮大的

paras.en: According to numbers from the Himalayan Database, in 2010, four Indian and eight Chinese climbers attempted the mountain, just 6 percent of the total.
paras.zh: 根据喜马拉雅数据库的数据，2010年有4名印度登山者和8名中国登山者尝试攀登珠峰，仅占总人数的6%。

paras.en: Last year, Chinese and Indian clients accounted for 60 of the 199 Nepal-side summits.
paras.zh: 去年，在尼泊尔一侧的199人次登顶中，中国和印度客户占了60人次。

paras.en: Unfortunately, in the absence of substantive government oversight, some of the budget companies are making Qomolangma more dangerous by flooding the already overcrowded route with novice climbers led by inexperienced guides.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，由于缺乏政府的实质性监管，一些低价公司把大批新手登山者塞进本已过度拥挤的路线，带领他们的向导也缺乏经验，这让珠峰变得更加危险。

paras.en: Any operators charging less for guided climbs are prone to bolster profits through scale, booking dozens of clients on expeditions.
paras.zh: 凡是在向导攀登服务上收费较低的运营商，往往都会靠扩大规模来增加利润，在登山队里安排几十名客户。

w.m: 为（某人）预订（行程、航班等）；安排……参加

paras.en: (The most respected outfitters set a maximum of ten.)
paras.zh: （最受尊敬的登山服务商把上限定为十人。）

paras.en: Putting aside 2014’s tragedy and 2015’s earthquake-induced avalanche, which killed at least 17 people at Base Camp, 12 of the 17 climbers who died on the South Col route between 2011 and 2017 appear to have been clients of budget outfitters.
paras.zh: 撇开2014年的悲剧和2015年地震引发的雪崩（这场雪崩在大本营造成至少17人死亡）不谈，2011年至2017年间在南坳路线上遇难的17名登山者中，似乎有12人是低价登山服务商的客户。

paras.en: During last year’s peak season, Kathmandu-based Seven Summit Treks, known for bringing large groups of climbers to Qomolangma, allegedly promoted a young support staffer named Sange to guide Qomolangma and assigned him to an older Pakistani client.
paras.zh: 去年登山旺季期间，总部位于加德满都、以带大批登山者前往珠峰而闻名的七峰探险公司，据称把一名叫桑格的年轻后勤人员提拔为珠峰向导，并派他带一名年纪较大的巴基斯坦客户。

w.m: adj. 总部设在加德满都的

paras.en: The pair reached the summit late in the day and got into trouble on their descent.
paras.zh: 两人当天很晚才登顶，下山途中遇险。

paras.en: They had to be rescued by experienced Sherpas from another Nepalese outfitter.
paras.zh: 他们只得靠另一家尼泊尔登山服务商经验丰富的夏尔巴人前来营救。

paras.en: Sange later had all his fingers amputated due to severe frostbite.
paras.zh: 桑格后来因严重冻伤，手指全部被截除。

paras.en: Veteran guides are reacting to all this in different ways.
paras.zh: 资深向导们正以各自不同的方式应对这一切。

w.m: adj. 经验丰富的；资深的

paras.en: Adrian Ballinger, founder of the California outfitter Alpenglow, has abandoned the Nepal side of Qomolangma and is instead leading teams from China.
paras.zh: 加州登山服务商Alpenglow的创始人阿德里安·巴林杰已经放弃了珠峰的尼泊尔一侧，转而从中国一侧带队。

paras.en: As he explained it, the higher risk from natural dangers (avalanches, seracs, crevasses), the low standards of other outfitters, and Nepal’s mismanagement add up to an unacceptable environment.
paras.zh: 按他的解释，自然危险（雪崩、冰塔、冰裂缝）带来的更高风险、其他登山服务商的低标准以及尼泊尔的管理不善，加在一起，使那里的环境令人无法接受。

paras.en: Several other prominent guides have come to the same conclusion, including Austrian Lukas Furtenbach.
paras.zh: 其他几位知名向导也得出了同样的结论，其中包括奥地利人卢卡斯·富尔滕巴赫。

paras.en: Others are staying put.
paras.zh: 另一些人则留在原地。

paras.en: International Mountain Guides co-owner Eric Simonson, whose first expedition on Qomolangma was in 1982, insists that upgrades in route-making through the Khumbu Icefall, and the establishment of dual ropes in areas prone to bottlenecks, have made the Nepal side safer, even as the crowds have grown.
paras.zh: 国际登山向导公司的共同所有人埃里克·西蒙森1982年首次到珠峰探险，他坚称，穿越昆布冰瀑的修路工作有所改进，加上在容易出现瓶颈的路段设置了双绳，尽管登山人群越来越多，这些举措还是让尼泊尔一侧更加安全了。

w.m: n. 共同所有人；合伙人
n. 修路（开辟攀登路线）

paras.en: Qomolangma remains the ultimate conquest for many climbers.
paras.zh: 对许多登山者来说，珠峰仍然是终极的征服目标。

paras.en: And while most embrace the risk of high-altitude mountaineering, few understand that the biggest dangers are all too often the result of economics, not the forces of nature.
paras.zh: 而且，虽然大多数人都欣然接受高海拔登山的风险，但很少有人明白，最大的危险往往是经济因素造成的，而不是自然力量造成的。

w.m: v. 欣然接受；乐于承担

paras.en: Ultimately, the top priority of many tourism officials and outfitters isn’t safety.
paras.zh: 说到底，许多旅游官员和登山服务商的头等大事并不是安全。

paras.en: It’s the bottom line.
paras.zh: 利润才是。

w.m: （账目上的）最终盈亏；利润（引申：最重要的考虑）

passages.name: 2022年 Passage Three
passages.title: 中亚古代牧民与文明的诞生
passages.genre: 说明文 · 考古与历史
passages.summary: 中亚大片地区看上去荒无人烟，大多数考古学家对这里仍知之甚少；过去一个世纪里，学者们往往把这里的游牧民族看作破坏者或无足轻重的边缘群体。考古学家弗拉切蒂则认为，公元前三千纪的中亚牧民建立了一个绵延数千英里的网络，传递着对城市生活至关重要的商品、技术和思想，帮助创造了文明。他的团队在哈萨克斯坦的别加什遗址发现了中亚已知最古老的驯化谷物等证据；他设想，牧民夏季在高山牧场与其他山谷的邻人相遇，思想和技术可能由此经中亚南部的山地走廊逐渐传播。

paras.en: Vast stretches of Central Asia feel eerily uninhabited.
paras.zh: 中亚的大片地区给人一种荒无人烟的诡异之感。

w.m: adv. 诡异地；令人不安地
adj. 无人居住的；荒无人烟的

paras.en: Fly at 30,000 feet over the southern part of the former Soviet Union and there are long moments when no town or road or field is visible from your window.
paras.zh: 在30,000英尺的高空飞越前苏联南部，从舷窗望出去，时常会有很长一段时间看不到任何城镇、道路或农田。

paras.en: The landscape of stark desert, trackless steppe (大草原), and rugged mountains seems to swallow up anything human.
paras.zh: 这里的地貌由荒凉的沙漠、无路可循的草原和崎岖的群山构成，似乎会吞没一切与人类有关的东西。

w.m: adj. 无路的；人迹罕至的
adj. 崎岖的；起伏不平的

paras.en: It is little surprise, then, that this region remains largely unknown to most archaeologists.
paras.zh: 因此，大多数考古学家对这一地区至今仍知之甚少，也就不足为奇了。

w.m: adv. 基本上；在很大程度上

paras.en: Wandering bands and tribes roamed this immense area for 5,000 years, herding goats, sheep, cattle, and horses across immense steppes, through narrow valleys, and over high snowy passes.
paras.zh: 在长达5,000年的时间里，四处漂泊的游群和部落在这片广袤的土地上游荡，赶着山羊、绵羊、牛和马，穿越辽阔的草原，穿过狭窄的山谷，翻过白雪覆盖的高山隘口。

w.m: adj. 积雪的；白雪覆盖的

paras.en: They left occasional tombs that survived the ages, and on rare occasions settled down and built towns or even cities.
paras.zh: 他们零星留下了一些历经漫长岁月保存至今的墓葬，在极少数情况下还会定居下来，建造城镇乃至城市。

paras.en: But for the most part, these peoples left behind few physical traces of their origins, beliefs, or ways of life.
paras.zh: 但总体而言，这些民族留下的有关自身起源、信仰或生活方式的实物痕迹寥寥无几。

paras.en: What we know of these nomadic pastoralists comes mainly from their periodic forays into India, the Middle East, and China, where they often wreaked havoc and earned a fearsome reputation as enemies of urban life.
paras.zh: 我们对这些游牧民的了解，主要来自他们不时对印度、中东和中国发动的侵袭；他们在那些地方常常大肆破坏，落下了城市生活之敌的可怕名声。

w.m: adj. 周期性的；时而发生的
大肆破坏；造成严重破坏
adj. 可怕的；令人生畏的

paras.en: In the past century, scholars criticized these people as destructive, dismissed them as marginal, or, at best, cast them as a harsh tonic for restoring vigor to decaying and soft agricultural societies from ancient Mesopotamia to Imperial Rome to Han China.
paras.zh: 在过去的一个世纪里，学者们批评这些人具有破坏性，把他们贬为无足轻重的边缘群体，或者往好里说，把他们看作一剂猛烈的补药，能让从古代美索不达米亚到罗马帝国再到汉代中国的那些日渐衰败、柔弱萎靡的农业社会重振活力。

w.m: adj. 边缘的；无足轻重的
n. 美索不达米亚（西亚两河流域的古代文明地区）

paras.en: In the 1950s, the British archaeologist Mortimer Wheeler blamed the aggressive, chariot-driving Aryans who swept in from the steppes for the demise of the peaceful Indus River civilization after 1800 B.C., though later archaeologists dismissed that claim.
paras.zh: 20世纪50年代，英国考古学家莫蒂默·惠勒把爱好和平的印度河文明在公元前1800年后的消亡，归咎于从草原席卷而来、驾着战车的好战雅利安人，不过后来的考古学家否定了这一说法。

w.m: adj. 好战的；有攻击性的
adj. 爱好和平的；和平的

paras.en: But Michael Frachetti, a young archaeologist at Washington University in St. Louis, takes the radical view that Central Asians were early midwives in the birth of civilization rather than a destructive force.
paras.zh: 但圣路易斯华盛顿大学的年轻考古学家迈克尔·弗拉切蒂持有一种激进的观点：中亚人是文明诞生之初的助产士，而不是一股破坏性力量。

paras.en: Frachetti argues that ancient pastoralists living in the third millennium B.C., at the time of the first great cities of Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Indus, created a network stretching across thousands of miles that passed along goods, technologies, and ideas central to urban life.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂认为，公元前三千纪正值美索不达米亚、埃及和印度河流域第一批大城市出现之时，生活在那个时期的古代牧民建立了一个绵延数千英里的网络，传递着对城市生活至关重要的商品、技术和思想。

w.m: n. 美索不达米亚（西亚两河流域的古代文明地区）

paras.en: He believes they helped create civilization rather than hindering it.
paras.zh: 他认为，这些牧民帮助创造了文明，而不是阻碍了文明。

paras.en: Most archaeological work in Central Asia during the past century has focused on the open and rolling plains that stretch from the Black Sea to Manchuria.
paras.zh: 过去一个世纪里，中亚的考古工作大多集中在从黑海一直延伸到中国东北的那片开阔起伏的平原上。

w.m: adj. 起伏的；绵延起伏的
n. 中国东北（旧称满洲）

paras.en: These steppes only came to life after 2000 B.C., when horse domestication and riding suddenly turned a forbidding landscape for pedestrians into a natural highway of grass.
paras.zh: 这些草原直到公元前2000年以后才焕发生机：那时，人们驯化了马，又学会了骑马，这片令徒步者望而生畏的土地便一下子变成了一条天然的青草大道。

w.m: adj. 令人生畏的；险恶的

paras.en: By contrast, the areas to the south of the steppes have long been dismissed as backwaters of history.
paras.zh: 相比之下，草原以南的地区长期以来一直被贬为远离历史主流的闭塞之地。

w.m: 被贬为；被认为……而不受重视
n. 闭塞落后之地；远离主流的地方

paras.en: In the past, these southern mountains and deserts were considered too remote, rugged, and inhospitable to have played a role in early migrations or the emergence of urban life.
paras.zh: 过去，人们认为南部这些山脉和沙漠太过偏远、崎岖，又不适宜居住，不可能在早期的迁徙或城市生活的兴起中发挥过作用。

w.m: adj. 不适宜居住的；荒凉的

paras.en: The Karakum Desert, where it might rain once in a decade, covers nearly two-thirds of today’s Turkmenistan, while the perpetually snow-covered Tian Shan Mountains of western China and eastern Kyrgyzstan soar 24,000 feet into the thin air.
paras.zh: 卡拉库姆沙漠可能十年才下一场雨，覆盖了今天土库曼斯坦近三分之二的国土；而中国西部和吉尔吉斯斯坦东部终年积雪的天山山脉则高达24,000英尺，直插空气稀薄的高空。

paras.en: It is there that Frachetti and a new generation of archaeologists from the United States and Central Asian nations are discovering evidence of a network of pastoralists who thrived centuries before hooves resounded on the steppes to the north.
paras.zh: 正是在那里，弗拉切蒂和来自美国及中亚各国的新一代考古学家不断发现证据，表明曾存在一个由牧民组成的网络；早在北面草原上响起马蹄声的几个世纪之前，这些牧民就已兴旺发达。

paras.en: These forgotten peoples may have carried such markers of civilization as ceramics and grains across thousands of miles, two millennia before the Silk Road linked the Roman Empire with Han China.
paras.zh: 这些被遗忘的民族可能曾带着陶器和谷物这类文明的标志跨越数千英里，比丝绸之路连通罗马帝国与汉代中国还要早两千年。

paras.en: Frachetti argues that the new data emerging from the region force archaeologists to rethink their ideas about trade across Eurasia during the Bronze Age, when the first civilizations were taking form to the east, south, and west.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂认为，这一地区不断涌现的新数据迫使考古学家重新审视自己对青铜时代欧亚大陆贸易往来的看法；那时，最早的一批文明正在东面、南面和西面逐渐成形。

w.m: v. 重新思考；重新审视

paras.en: Frachetti, who has studied modern-day pastoralists in such unforgiving landscapes as the Sahara and Scandinavia, was drawn to the southern region of Central Asia for its environmental diversity of desert, grassland, and meadows.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂曾在撒哈拉和斯堪的纳维亚等条件严酷的地带研究过现代牧民，他之所以被中亚南部吸引，是因为那里环境多样，既有沙漠，也有草地和草甸。

paras.en: Instead of a wasteland, he saw an ideal landscape for enterprising herders who wanted to pasture their animals in all seasons.
paras.zh: 他看到的不是一片荒原，而是一处理想之地，适合那些富有进取心、希望一年四季都能放牧牲畜的牧人。

w.m: adj. 有进取心的；有事业心的

paras.en: Together with his colleagues, Frachetti began digging a decade ago in the Dzhungar Mountains of Kazakhstan.
paras.zh: 十年前，弗拉切蒂与同事们一起开始在哈萨克斯坦的准噶尔山脉发掘。

paras.en: Covering nearly 500 square miles, this region lies between the Tian Shan and Altai mountain ranges, and boasts sharp peaks topping 12,000 feet, as well as harsh desert.
paras.zh: 这一地区面积近500平方英里，位于天山山脉和阿尔泰山脉之间，既有高度超过12,000英尺的险峻山峰，也有环境恶劣的沙漠。

w.m: v. 拥有（值得夸耀的东西）

paras.en: At a site near a village called Begash, on a flat terrace enclosed by steep canyon walls alongside a small stream, the team uncovered the foundations of simple stone structures along with an array of potsherds (陶瓷碎片) and bronze and stone artifacts in stone-lined oval and rectangular tombs.
paras.zh: 在一个名叫别加什的村庄附近，有一处遗址坐落在小溪旁的一块平坦台地上，四周是陡峭的峡谷崖壁；考古队在这里发掘出了简易石头建筑的地基，还在用石块砌边的椭圆形和长方形墓葬中发现了一批陶片以及青铜器和石器。

paras.en: The earliest layers at Begash date to at least as early as 2500 B.C., based on accelerator mass spectrometry dating of organic remains, says Frachetti.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂说，根据对有机遗存的加速器质谱测年，别加什最早的地层至少可以追溯到公元前2500年。

paras.en: One woman was laid to rest with a bell-shaped hooked bronze earring around 1700 B.C., according to electron spin resonance dating.
paras.zh: 根据电子自旋共振测年，大约在公元前1700年，一名女子带着一只钟形带钩的青铜耳环下葬。

paras.en: Similar earrings are only found several centuries later some 600 miles to the north on the Siberian steppes, hinting at styles that moved north over time.
paras.zh: 类似的耳环直到几个世纪之后，才见于北面约600英里外的西伯利亚草原，暗示这些样式随着时间推移向北传播。

paras.en: More surprisingly, the excavators found wheat, which was first domesticated in the Fertile Crescent of the Middle East, and broomcorn millet that was first widely grown in northern China.
paras.zh: 更令人意外的是，发掘者发现了小麦和黍：小麦最早是在中东的新月沃地驯化的，而黍最早是在中国北方广泛种植的。

w.m: adv. 令人意外地；出人意料地

paras.en: The grains were used ritually in a burial, and radiocarbon dating of the remains dates them to about 2200 B.C., making them the oldest known domesticated grains in Central Asia.
paras.zh: 这些谷物曾在一处墓葬中用于仪式；对遗存的放射性碳测年表明，它们的年代约为公元前2200年，因而成为中亚已知最古老的驯化谷物。

w.m: adv. 在仪式上；作为仪式

paras.en: The people of Begash may not have grown either grain—there are no grinding stones, a sign of grain preparation—but instead received it via trade networks stretching from the Near East to China.
paras.zh: 别加什人可能两种谷物都没种过——那里没有磨石，而磨石是加工谷物的标志——而是通过从近东一直延伸到中国的贸易网络得到了谷物。

paras.en: Dorian Fuller, a leading expert in ancient grains based at University College London, calls the finds “important and well dated.”
paras.zh: 伦敦大学学院的多里安·富勒是研究古代谷物的权威专家，他称这些发现“意义重大，年代测定可靠”。

paras.en: He adds that Chinese crops such as millet began to appear in southwest Asia around 1900 B.C., a few centuries after they reached Begash, which could mean the passage through the mountain regions was a means of gradual transmission from east to west.
paras.zh: 他还说，黍等中国作物在公元前1900年左右开始出现在西南亚，比它们到达别加什晚了几个世纪，这可能意味着，穿越这些山区的通道是由东向西逐步传播的一种途径。

paras.en: Frachetti speculates that the grains may have been acquired from other tribes and used for ritual purposes, and then perhaps were passed on in turn to other pastoral peoples.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂推测，这些谷物可能是从其他部落那里得来、用于仪式的，之后或许又辗转传给了其他畜牧民族。

paras.en: What makes the Begash discoveries so important is that previously this region was assumed to have been a land of scattered foragers (狩猎者) until steppe peoples trickled down into the area’s valleys and mountain ranges after 2000 B.C. But it is becoming evident that the people of Begash were not simple foragers, but sophisticated pastoralists who tended their flocks, much as people in the area still do today.
paras.zh: 别加什的发现之所以如此重要，是因为过去人们认为，在公元前2000年以后草原民族陆续南下、进入该地区的山谷和山脉之前，这里是零散的狩猎采集者生活的地方。但越来越明显的是，别加什人并非简单的狩猎采集者，而是成熟老练的牧民，他们照料着自己的畜群，就像如今这一带的人依然在做的那样。

w.m: n. 觅食者；狩猎采集者
v. 陆续来到；缓慢流动
adj. 成熟老练的；复杂精密的

paras.en: The inhabitants did not begin to use horses until well into the second millennium B.C., and the varieties of sheep and goat found here today appear to be related to the varieties first domesticated thousands of years before in western Iran, near ancient Mesopotamia.
paras.zh: 直到进入公元前二千纪很久以后，这里的居民才开始使用马匹；而如今在这里见到的绵羊和山羊品种，似乎与此前数千年在古代美索不达米亚附近的伊朗西部最早驯化的品种有亲缘关系。

w.m: n. 美索不达米亚（西亚两河流域的古代文明地区）

paras.en: This indicates that Begash was “at the crossroads of extremely wide networks among Eurasian communities by the third millennium B.C.,” asserts Frachetti.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂断言，这表明别加什“到公元前三千纪时，已处于欧亚大陆各族群间极为广泛的网络交汇之处”。

w.m: 处于……的十字路口（交汇处）

paras.en: That doesn’t mean that traders traversed thousands of miles in this early period.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着早在这一时期，商人就已跋涉数千英里。

paras.en: Instead, the archaeologist envisions pastoralists taking their flocks to higher pastures in the summer, where they encountered neighbors from other valleys doing the same.
paras.zh: 这位考古学家设想的情形则是：牧民夏天把畜群赶到地势更高的牧场，并在那里遇到来自其他山谷、同样赶着畜群上山的邻人。

paras.en: Thus, ideas and technologies might have passed gradually through the mountain corridor of southern Central Asia.
paras.zh: 因此，思想和技术可能是经由中亚南部的山地走廊逐渐传播的。

paras.en: This corridor, Frachetti believes, may have been a key conduit for Bronze Age developments farther into East Asia and Mongolia.
paras.zh: 弗拉切蒂认为，这条走廊可能曾是青铜时代各项发展成果进一步传入东亚和蒙古的关键通道。

passages.name: 2021年 Passage One
passages.title: 看似熟悉却知之甚少的大猩猩
passages.genre: 说明文 · 动物与自然
passages.summary: 人们以为很了解大猩猩，事实上却对它知之甚少：至今没有一张真正令人满意的野生大猩猩照片，也没有哪位动物学家能在丛林里密切而持续地观察它。已知的少量情况显示，大猩猩身上颇有几分“人性”：曾有幼年大猩猩用手指描画自己影子的轮廓，也有人见过雄性扶雌性登上陡峭的岩阶；家庭一旦组建起来，成员之间就紧紧相依，每晚各自用竹子的枝叶搭窝。雄性遇到危险时会做出吓人的示威举动，但一般说来那不过是虚张声势；大猩猩性情温和，凶残好斗的名声纯属虚构。

paras.en: The gorilla is something of a paradox on the African scene.
paras.zh: 在非洲这片天地里，大猩猩可以说是个矛盾体。

w.m: 可以说是；在某种程度上算是
n. 天地；舞台（指某一地区或领域的情形）

paras.en: One thinks one knows him very well.
paras.zh: 人们以为自己对它非常了解。

paras.en: For a hundred years or more he has been killed, captured and imprisoned in zoos.
paras.zh: 一百多年来，大猩猩一直遭人猎杀、捕捉，被囚禁在动物园里。

paras.en: His bones have been mounted in natural history museums everywhere, and he has always exerted a strong fascination upon scientists and romantics alike.
paras.zh: 各地的自然历史博物馆里都装架陈列着它的骨骼；无论对科学家还是对富于浪漫幻想的人，它也一向都有着强烈的吸引力。

w.m: v. 施加（影响等）；发挥（作用）
n. 浪漫主义者；富于浪漫幻想的人

paras.en: He is the stereotyped monster of horror films and adventure books, and an obvious (though not perhaps strictly scientific) link with our ancestral past.
paras.zh: 它是恐怖片和冒险读物中模式化的怪物形象，也是我们与远祖时代之间一条显而易见的纽带（尽管严格说来，这种联系或许并不科学）。

w.m: adj. 模式化的；老一套的
adj. 明显的；显而易见的

paras.en: Yet the fact is we know very little about gorillas.
paras.zh: 然而事实是，我们对大猩猩知之甚少。

paras.en: No really satisfactory photograph has ever been taken of one in a wild state; no zoologist, however intrepid, has been able to keep the animal under close and constant observation in the dark jungles in which it lives.
paras.zh: 至今还没有人拍到过一张真正令人满意的野生大猩猩照片；动物学家无论多么勇敢无畏，都没能在大猩猩栖身的幽暗丛林里密切而持续地观察它。

paras.en: Carl Akeley, the American naturalist, led two expeditions to Uganda in the 1920s and now lies buried there among the animals he loved so well; but even he was unable to discover how long the gorilla lives, or how or why it dies, nor was he able to define the exact social pattern of the family groups, or indicate the final extent of their intelligence.
paras.zh: 美国博物学家卡尔·埃克利在20世纪20年代曾两次率领考察队前往乌干达，如今就长眠在那里，与他深爱的动物们为伴；但即便是他，也没能查明大猩猩能活多久、怎样死去或为何死去，也没能界定大猩猩家庭群体确切的社会模式，或指明它们的智力最终能达到何种程度。

w.m: 卡尔·埃克利（美国博物学家）
conj. 也不（后接倒装语序）

paras.en: All this and many other things remain almost as much a mystery as they were when the French explorer Du Chaillu first described the animal to the civilized world a century ago.
paras.zh: 所有这一切以及其他许多事情，至今几乎仍和一个世纪前法国探险家杜·沙伊鲁首次向文明世界描述这种动物时一样，是个谜。

paras.en: The Abominable Snowman who haunts the imagination of climbers in the Himalayas is hardly more elusive.
paras.zh: 就连萦绕在喜马拉雅山登山者想象中的雪怪，也几乎不比大猩猩更难以捉摸。

w.m: v. 萦绕；（思想、记忆等）缠绕
adj. 难以捉摸的；难觅踪迹的

paras.en: The little that is known about gorillas certainly makes you want to know more.
paras.zh: 关于大猩猩已知的那一点点情况，无疑会让人想知道得更多。

paras.en: Sir Julian Huxley has recorded that thrice in the London Zoo he saw an eighteen-month-old specimen trace the outline of its own shadow with its finger.
paras.zh: 朱利安·赫胥黎爵士曾记述，他在伦敦动物园三次看到一只十八个月大的大猩猩用手指描画自己影子的轮廓。

paras.en: “No similar artistic initiative,” he writes, “has been recorded for any other anthropoid (类人猿), though we all know now that young chimpanzees will paint ‘pictures’ if provided with the necessary materials.”
paras.zh: 他写道：“在其他任何类人猿身上，都还没有记录到类似的自发艺术行为，不过如今我们都知道，只要给幼年黑猩猩提供必要的材料，它们就会画‘画’。”

w.m: n. 自发的行为；主动性

paras.en: Huxley speaks too of a traveler seeing a male gorilla help a female up a steep rock-step, and gallantry of that kind is certainly not normal among animals.
paras.zh: 赫胥黎还提到，有位旅行者看见一只雄性大猩猩扶一只雌性大猩猩登上一级陡峭的岩阶；这种殷勤体贴之举在动物中无疑并不寻常。

w.m: n. （男子对女子的）殷勤；侠义风度

paras.en: It is this “human-ness” of the gorilla that is so beguiling.
paras.zh: 正是大猩猩身上的这种“人性”，才如此令人着迷。

w.m: adj. 迷人的；令人着迷的

paras.en: According to some observers he courts and makes love the same way as humans do.
paras.zh: 据一些观察者说，大猩猩求爱和交配的方式与人类相同。

paras.en: Once the family is established it clings together.
paras.zh: 家庭一旦组建起来，成员之间就会紧紧相依。

paras.en: It feeds in a group in the thick bamboo jungles on the mountainside in the daytime, each animal making a tidy pile of its food—wild celery, bamboo shoots, and other leaves—and squatting down to eat it; and by night each member of the family makes its own bed by bending over and interlacing the bamboo fronds so as to form a kind of oval-shaped nest which is as comfortable and springy as a mattress.
paras.zh: 白天，全家在山坡上茂密的竹林里一起觅食，每只大猩猩都把自己的食物——野芹菜、竹笋和其他叶子——整整齐齐地堆成一堆，再蹲下来吃；到了夜里，每个家庭成员都会给自己搭床：把竹子的枝叶压弯、交织起来，形成一种椭圆形的窝，像床垫一样舒适而富有弹性。

w.m: n. （竹子、棕榈、蕨类等的）枝叶；叶子

paras.en: The father tends to make his bed just a foot or two from the ground, the mother a little higher, and the children are safely lodged in the branches up above.
paras.zh: 父亲往往把床搭在离地面仅一两英尺的地方，母亲的床稍高一些，孩子们则安稳地待在上方的树枝间。

paras.en: When he walks, the gorilla takes the main weight on his short legs and rests lightly on the knuckles of his hands at the end of his very long arms.
paras.zh: 大猩猩走路时，主要由两条短腿承重，而它的两臂很长，臂端的双手以指关节轻轻撑地。

paras.en: When he stands upright a full-grown male rises to six feet, but with that immense chest he is far heavier than any normal man could ever be.
paras.zh: 成年雄性大猩猩站直时，身高达六英尺，但它胸膛那样硕大，体重之大远非任何正常男子所能及。

w.m: adj. 发育完全的；成年的

paras.en: Six hundred pounds is not uncommon.
paras.zh: 六百磅的体重并不少见。

paras.en: His strength is incredible—certainly great enough to take a man in his arms and wrench his head off.
paras.zh: 它的力气大得令人难以置信，肯定足以把一个人搂在怀里，把他的脑袋拧下来。

paras.en: Gorillas appear to talk to one another in high-pitched voices, not unlike those of women, or by smacking their lips or striking their cheeks, and the female, if alarmed, will scream.
paras.zh: 大猩猩似乎会用尖细的嗓音（与女人的嗓音颇为相似），或以咂嘴、拍打脸颊的方式彼此交谈；雌性大猩猩受到惊吓时会尖叫。

paras.en: The male is capable of making a frightening demonstration in the face of danger.
paras.zh: 面对危险时，雄性大猩猩能做出令人胆寒的示威举动。

w.m: adj. 吓人的；令人恐惧的

paras.en: He stays behind while his family gets away, rising to his feet and uttering a terrifying roar.
paras.zh: 家人逃走时，它会留在后面，站起身来，发出骇人的咆哮。

paras.en: Sometimes he will drum on his chest and shake the trees around him with every appearance of uncontrollable fury.
paras.zh: 有时，它还会捶打胸膛，摇撼周围的树木，看上去完全是一副怒不可遏的样子。

w.m: 看上去完全是；俨然一副……的样子

paras.en: In extremity he will charge.
paras.zh: 到了危急关头，它会猛冲过来。

w.m: 在危急关头；万不得已时

paras.en: But all this is no more than shadow boxing as a general rule, for the gorilla is a gentle, kindly creature, a most forgiving ape who lives at peace with all the other animals, and his reputation for savagery and belligerence is nothing but a myth.
paras.zh: 但一般说来，这一切不过是虚张声势，因为大猩猩是一种温和、善良的动物，是非常宽容的猿类，与其他所有动物都和平相处；它那凶残好斗的名声纯属虚构。

w.m: n. 不实之说；虚构的说法

paras.en: When the animal charges, the thing to do is to stand your ground and look him in the eye.
paras.zh: 大猩猩冲过来时，你该做的就是寸步不让，直视它的眼睛。

paras.en: Then he will turn aside and slip away through the undergrowth.
paras.zh: 这时，它就会转向一旁，穿过灌木丛悄悄溜走。

w.m: n. （大树下的）灌木丛；矮树丛

passages.name: 2021年 Passage Two
passages.title: 镇上形影不离的两个哑巴
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与友谊
passages.summary: 镇上有两个形影不离的哑巴：肥胖、贪吃的希腊人安东尼帕罗斯在表兄的水果店里干活，高瘦整洁的辛格在珠宝店当银器雕刻工。在家里，辛格总是用双手比画，把白天发生的一切都讲给朋友听，却从不知道对方究竟懂了多少；安东尼帕罗斯则很少比画，即便比画，也只是表示想吃、想睡或想喝。两人除了彼此没有别的朋友，每一天都和别的日子十分相像；街上的人常常面带饥饿与孤独的绝望神情，他们却一点也不孤独。就这样过了十年，辛格到了三十二岁。

paras.en: In the town there were two mutes, and they were always together.
paras.zh: 镇上有两个哑巴，他们总是形影不离。

paras.en: Early every morning they would come out from the house where they lived and walk arm in arm down the street to work.
paras.zh: 每天一大早，他们都会从住处出来，手挽着手沿街走去上班。

paras.en: The one who always steered the way was an obese and dreamy Greek.
paras.zh: 总在前面领路的那个，是个肥胖而迷迷糊糊的希腊人。

w.m: adj. 迷迷糊糊的；恍惚的

paras.en: In the summer he would come out wearing a yellow or green polo shirt stuffed sloppily into his trousers in front and hanging loose behind.
paras.zh: 夏天，他出门时会穿一件黄色或绿色的马球衫，前面胡乱塞在裤子里，后面松松垮垮地耷拉着。

paras.en: When it was colder, he wore over this a shapeless gray sweater.
paras.zh: 天冷一些的时候，他就在外面套一件走了样的灰毛衣。

w.m: adj. 不成形的；走了样的

paras.en: His face was round and oily, with half-closed eyelids and lips that curved in a gentle, stupid smile.
paras.zh: 他的脸圆圆的，油光光的，眼皮半闭着，嘴唇弯出一抹温和而傻乎乎的笑。

paras.en: The other mute was tall.
paras.zh: 另一个哑巴个子很高。

paras.en: His eyes had a quick, intelligent expression.
paras.zh: 他的眼睛透着机敏、聪慧的神情。

paras.en: He was always immaculate and very soberly dressed.
paras.zh: 他总是收拾得一尘不染，穿着十分素净。

w.m: adj. 一尘不染的；整洁的

paras.en: Every morning the two friends walked silently together until they reached the main street of the town.
paras.zh: 每天早上，这两个朋友都默默地一起走，一直走到镇上的大街。

paras.en: Then when they came to a certain fruit and candy store, they paused for a moment on the sidewalk outside.
paras.zh: 接着，来到某家水果糖果店时，他们会在店外的人行道上停一会儿。

paras.en: The Greek, Spiros Antonapoulos, worked for his cousin, who owned this fruit store.
paras.zh: 那个希腊人叫斯皮罗斯·安东尼帕罗斯，在他表兄手下干活，这家水果店就是表兄开的。

paras.en: His job was to make candies and sweets, uncrate the fruits, and keep the place clean.
paras.zh: 他的活儿是做糖果和甜食，把水果从板条箱里取出来，还要保持店里干净。

paras.en: The thin mute, John Singer, nearly always put his hand on his friend’s arm and looked for a second into his face before leaving him.
paras.zh: 那个瘦哑巴叫约翰·辛格，分开之前，他几乎每次都把手搭在朋友的胳膊上，注视他的脸片刻。

paras.en: Then after this goodbye Singer crossed the street and walked on alone to the jewelry store where he worked as a silverware engraver.
paras.zh: 这样道别之后，辛格便穿过马路，独自继续往前走，一直走到那家珠宝店，他在那里当银器雕刻工。

paras.en: In the late afternoon the friends would meet again.
paras.zh: 傍晚时分，两个朋友又会碰面。

paras.en: Singer came back to the fruit store and waited until Antonapoulos was ready to go home.
paras.zh: 辛格回到水果店，一直等到安东尼帕罗斯准备好回家。

paras.en: The Greek would be lazily unpacking a case of peaches or melons, or perhaps looking at the funny paper in the kitchen behind the store where he cooked.
paras.zh: 这时，那个希腊人往往正懒洋洋地拆一箱桃子或甜瓜，也可能正在店后面他做饭的厨房里看报上的连环漫画。

w.m: v. 打开（箱子）取出东西

paras.en: Before their departure Antonapoulos always opened a paper sack he kept hidden during the day on one of the kitchen shelves.
paras.zh: 临走前，安东尼帕罗斯总要打开一个纸袋，白天他一直把它藏在厨房的一层架子上。

paras.en: Inside were stored various bits of food he had collected—a piece of fruit or samples of candy.
paras.zh: 袋子里存放着他攒下的各种零碎吃食——一个水果，或几块糖果样品。

paras.en: Usually before leaving Antonapoulos waddled gently to the glassed case in the front of the store where some meats and cheeses were kept.
paras.zh: 离开前，安东尼帕罗斯通常会轻轻地、一摇一摆地走到店堂前部的玻璃柜跟前，柜子里放着一些肉和奶酪。

paras.en: He glided open the back of the case and his fat hand groped lovingly for some particular dainty inside which he had wanted.
paras.zh: 他轻轻地滑开柜子背面的门，胖手满怀爱意地伸进去摸索，寻找他早就想要的某样精致小吃。

w.m: adv. 满怀爱意地；深情地

paras.en: Sometimes his cousin who owned the place did not see him.
paras.zh: 有时候，开这家店的表兄没看见他。

paras.en: But if he noticed he stared at his cousin with a warning in his tight, pale face.
paras.zh: 可要是表兄发现了，就会紧盯着这个表弟，紧绷而苍白的脸上带着警告的神色。

paras.en: Sadly, Antonapoulos would shuffle the morsel from one corner of the case to the other.
paras.zh: 安东尼帕罗斯就会难过地把那一小块吃的从柜子的这一角挪到另一角。

paras.en: During these times Singer stood very straight with his hands in his pockets and looked in another direction.
paras.zh: 每逢这种时候，辛格就把手插在口袋里，站得笔直，眼睛望向别处。

paras.en: He did not like to watch this little scene between the two Greeks.
paras.zh: 他不喜欢看两个希腊人之间的这个小场面。

paras.en: For, except drinking and a certain solitary secret pleasure, Antonapoulos loved to eat more than anything else in the world.
paras.zh: 因为，除了喝酒和某种独自享受的隐秘乐趣，安东尼帕罗斯在这世上最爱的就是吃。

paras.en: In the dusk the two mutes walked slowly home together.
paras.zh: 暮色中，两个哑巴一起慢慢走回家。

paras.en: At home Singer was always talking to Antonapoulos.
paras.zh: 在家里，辛格总是在跟安东尼帕罗斯说话。

w.m: 总是（老是）在做（表示频繁）

paras.en: His hands shaped the words in a swift series of designs.
paras.zh: 他的双手飞快地比画出一连串图形，打出一个个词。

paras.en: His face was eager and his gray-green eyes sparkled brightly.
paras.zh: 他满脸热切，一双灰绿色的眼睛闪闪发亮。

paras.en: With his thin, strong hands he told Antonapoulos all that had happened during the day.
paras.zh: 他用那双瘦削有力的手，把白天发生的一切都讲给安东尼帕罗斯听。

paras.en: When back at home, Antonapoulos sat back lazily and looked at Singer.
paras.zh: 回到家里，安东尼帕罗斯便懒洋洋地往后一靠，看着辛格。

paras.en: It was seldom that he ever moved his hands to speak at all—and then it was to say that he wanted to eat or to sleep or to drink.
paras.zh: 他难得动一动手来说话——即便动了，也只是说他想吃，或者想睡，或者想喝。

paras.en: These three things he always said with the same vague, fumbling signs.
paras.zh: 这三件事，他总是用同样含糊、笨拙的手势来表示。

paras.en: At night, if he were not too drunk, he would kneel down before his bed and pray awhile.
paras.zh: 夜里，要是醉得不太厉害，他会跪在床前祈祷一会儿。

paras.en: Then his plump hands shaped the words Holy Jesus, or God, or Darling Mary.
paras.zh: 接着，他那双胖乎乎的手比画出“圣耶稣”，或“上帝”，或“亲爱的玛利亚”。

paras.en: These were the only words Antonapoulos ever said.
paras.zh: 安东尼帕罗斯说过的词，就只有这几个。

w.m: adv. 曾经；（用于强调）从来

paras.en: Singer never knew just how much his friend understood of all the things he told him.
paras.zh: 辛格告诉朋友的种种事情，朋友究竟懂了多少，他从来都不知道。

paras.en: But it did not matter.
paras.zh: 但这并不要紧。

paras.en: They shared the upstairs of a small house near the business section of the town.
paras.zh: 他们合住在镇上商业区附近一座小房子的楼上。

paras.en: There were two rooms.
paras.zh: 楼上共有两个房间。

paras.en: On the oil stove in the kitchen Antonapoulos cooked all of their meals.
paras.zh: 他们的饭全是安东尼帕罗斯在厨房的油炉上做的。

paras.en: There were straight, plain kitchen chairs for Singer and an overstuffed sofa for Antonapoulos.
paras.zh: 屋里给辛格准备的是几把直背的简朴厨房椅，给安东尼帕罗斯准备的是一张塞得鼓鼓囊囊的沙发。

paras.en: The bedroom was furnished mainly with a large double bed covered with an eiderdown comforter for the big Greek and a narrow iron cot for Singer.
paras.zh: 卧室里主要摆着一张大双人床和一张窄窄的小铁床：双人床铺着鸭绒被，是给那个大块头希腊人睡的；小铁床是给辛格睡的。

paras.en: Dinner always took a long time, because Antonapoulos loved food and he was very slow.
paras.zh: 晚饭总要吃很久，因为安东尼帕罗斯爱吃，吃得又非常慢。

paras.en: After they had eaten, the big Greek would lie back on his sofa and slowly lick over each one of his teeth with his tongue, either from a certain delicacy or because he did not wish to lose the savor of the meal—while Singer washed the dishes.
paras.zh: 吃完饭，那个大块头希腊人会仰靠在沙发上，用舌头慢慢地把每一颗牙齿都舔一遍，要么是出于某种讲究，要么是因为不想让饭菜的余味散去；而辛格这时正在洗碗。

w.m: n. 讲究；（品味上的）精细

paras.en: Sometimes in the evening the mutes would play chess.
paras.zh: 有时候晚上，两个哑巴会下国际象棋。

paras.en: Singer had always greatly enjoyed this game, and years before he had tried to teach it to Antonapoulos.
paras.zh: 辛格一向非常喜爱这种棋，多年前就曾试着教安东尼帕罗斯下。

paras.en: At first his friend could not be interested in the reasons for moving the various pieces about on the board.
paras.zh: 起初，他的朋友对棋盘上各种棋子为什么要那样挪来挪去，怎么也提不起兴趣。

paras.en: Then Singer began to keep a bottle of something good under the table to be taken out after each lesson.
paras.zh: 后来，辛格开始在桌子底下放一瓶好东西，每上完一课就拿出来。

paras.en: The Greek never got on to the erratic movements of the knights and the sweeping mobility of the queens, but he learned to make a few set, opening moves.
paras.zh: 那个希腊人始终没弄懂马那飘忽不定的走法和后那横扫全盘的机动性，不过他学会了几步固定的开局走法。

w.m: adj. 飘忽不定的；不规则的

paras.en: He preferred the white pieces and would not play if the black men were given him.
paras.zh: 他更喜欢执白棋，要是把黑子给他，他就不肯下。

paras.en: After the first moves Singer worked out the game by himself while his friend looked on drowsily.
paras.zh: 走完开头几步后，辛格就自己把这盘棋下完，他的朋友则在一旁昏昏欲睡地看着。

paras.en: If Singer made brilliant attacks on his own men so that in the end the black king was killed, Antonapoulos was always very proud and pleased.
paras.zh: 如果辛格对自己的棋子发起精彩的进攻，结果黑王最终被杀，安东尼帕罗斯总是非常得意、非常高兴。

paras.en: The two mutes had no other friends, and except when they worked, they were alone together.
paras.zh: 两个哑巴没有别的朋友，除了上班的时候，总是只有他们俩待在一起。

paras.en: Each day was very much like any other day, because they were alone so much that nothing ever disturbed them.
paras.zh: 每一天都和别的日子十分相像，因为两人独处得太多，从来没有什么事打扰过他们。

paras.en: Once a week they would go to the library for Singer to withdraw a mystery book and on Friday night they attended a movie.
paras.zh: 他们每周去一次图书馆，好让辛格借一本推理小说；星期五晚上，他们会去看一场电影。

paras.en: Then on payday they always went to the ten-cent photograph shop above the Army and Navy Store so that Antonapoulos could have his picture taken.
paras.zh: 此外，每逢发薪日，他们总要去陆海军商店楼上那家十美分一张的照相馆，好让安东尼帕罗斯拍张照片。

paras.en: These were the only places where they made customary visits.
paras.zh: 他们惯常光顾的地方，就只有这几处。

paras.en: There were many parts in the town that they had never even seen.
paras.zh: 镇上有许多地方，他们连见都没见过。

paras.en: The town was in the middle of the deep South.
paras.zh: 这个镇子地处南方腹地的中部。

paras.en: The summers were long and the months of winter cold were very few.
paras.zh: 这里夏季漫长，冬天寒冷的月份屈指可数。

paras.en: Nearly always the sky was a glassy, brilliant azure and the sun burned down riotously bright.
paras.zh: 天空几乎总是玻璃般明净、灿烂夺目的蔚蓝色，太阳灼灼地照射下来，亮得放肆。

w.m: adj. 玻璃般透亮的；光滑如镜的

paras.en: Then the light, chill rains of November would come, and perhaps later there would be frost and some short months of cold.
paras.zh: 然后，到了十一月，就会下起清冷的小雨，也许再往后会有霜冻，还有短短几个月的寒冷天气。

paras.en: The winters were changeable, but the summers always were burning hot.
paras.zh: 这里的冬天变化无常，夏天却总是酷热难当。

w.m: adj. 多变的；变化无常的

paras.en: The town was a fairly large one.
paras.zh: 这个镇子规模相当大。

paras.en: On the main street there were several blocks of two- and three-story shops and business offices.
paras.zh: 大街上有好几个街区都是两三层的商店和商业办公楼。

paras.en: But the largest buildings in the town were the factories, which employed a large percentage of the population.
paras.zh: 不过，镇上最大的建筑是工厂，这些工厂雇用了全镇很大一部分人口。

w.m: 很大比例的；很大一部分

paras.en: These cotton mills were big and flourishing and most of the workers in the town were very poor.
paras.zh: 这些棉纺厂规模庞大、生意兴隆，而镇上的大多数工人都非常贫穷。

paras.en: Often in the faces along the streets there was the desperate look of hunger and of loneliness.
paras.zh: 街上的一张张面孔，常常流露出饥饿与孤独的绝望神情。

paras.en: But the two mutes were not lonely at all.
paras.zh: 但这两个哑巴一点也不孤独。

paras.en: At home they were content to eat and drink, and Singer would talk with his hands eagerly to his friend about all that was in his mind.
paras.zh: 在家里，他们吃吃喝喝就心满意足了；辛格会用双手热切地向朋友诉说心里想的一切。

paras.en: So, the years passed in this quiet way until Singer reached the age of thirty-two and had been in the town with Antonapoulos for ten years.
paras.zh: 就这样，岁月平静地流逝，直到辛格到了三十二岁，已经和安东尼帕罗斯在这个镇上住了十年。

passages.name: 2021年 Passage Three
passages.title: 《莫扎特传》中的史实与虚构
passages.genre: 议论文 · 电影与历史
passages.summary: 电影《莫扎特传》对史实多有随意改动，但似乎很少有人介意，这在一定程度上要归功于影片的高娱乐价值和莫扎特的音乐。影片取材于萨列里毒杀莫扎特的传闻，把萨列里描绘成长期嫉妒莫扎特的人；而事实上，萨列里当时被视为更有造诣的作曲家，两人虽有竞争，却几乎没有证据表明彼此敌视，若有怨恨，也是出自莫扎特一方。作者认为，影片的戏剧性源于后人所知的事实：莫扎特的音乐和声誉流传了几个世纪，萨列里的名字和作品却很快被人淡忘。

paras.en: Like many historical films, Amadeus is far from a faithful account of what is known about the period and the people that it portrays.
paras.zh: 和许多历史片一样，就其所描绘的时代和人物而言，《莫扎特传》远不是对已知史实的忠实记述。

w.m: adj. 历史的；以历史为题材的

paras.en: Events are exaggerated, condensed and simplified, and the complexity of real characters is reduced to suit the needs of a dramatic contrast between good and evil.
paras.zh: 片中的事件经过了夸大、压缩和简化，真实人物的复杂性也被削减，以满足善恶之间戏剧性对比的需要。

paras.en: Such historical liberties are often bemoaned by experts, but few have seemed to mind the wayward story points of Amadeus.
paras.zh: 专家们常常抱怨这类对历史的随意改动，但对于《莫扎特传》中那些背离史实的情节，似乎很少有人介意。

w.m: adj. 离谱的；偏离常轨的

paras.en: This is no doubt partly attributable to the film’s high entertainment value: it is an unusually lively and funny historical film.
paras.zh: 这无疑在一定程度上要归功于影片娱乐价值很高：它是一部格外活泼、风趣的历史片。

w.m: adv. 部分地；在一定程度上
adj. 历史的；以历史为题材的

paras.en: It revels in the boyish humor and high spirits of its main character, the composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791), played with jubilant gusto by Tom Hulce.
paras.zh: 影片的主人公是作曲家沃尔夫冈·阿马德乌斯·莫扎特（1756—1791），由汤姆·赫尔斯以欢欣饱满的热情饰演；影片尽情展现了他孩子气的幽默和兴高采烈的劲头。

w.m: 陶醉于；尽情展现（某事物）
adj. 孩子气的；男孩似的
adj. 欢欣的；喜气洋洋的

paras.en: But the film’s appeal is also attributable to Mozart’s music.
paras.zh: 不过，影片的魅力也要归功于莫扎特的音乐。

paras.en: The composer’s vulgar hijinks (狂欢作乐) serve as a contrast to the transcendent beauty of his music, beautifully performed on the soundtrack by the Academy of St Martin in the Fields.
paras.zh: 这位作曲家粗俗的狂欢作乐，与他音乐的超凡之美形成了对比；在影片配乐中，田野圣马丁学院乐团把这些音乐演奏得十分优美。

paras.en: Thus, even the most stringent historical purists couldn’t help but find something to enjoy in Amadeus.
paras.zh: 因此，即便是对史实要求最严苛、最不容走样的人，也不禁会在《莫扎特传》中找到值得欣赏之处。

w.m: n. 纯粹主义者（力求纯正、不容走样的人）

paras.en: For all its liberties, the story is actually based on a real rumor that circulated in Vienna in the 1820s.
paras.zh: 尽管有种种随意改动，这个故事其实取材于19世纪20年代在维也纳流传的一则真实传闻。

paras.en: While gravely ill, the rival composer Antonio Salieri (1750–1825) confessed he had murdered Mozart decades earlier by poisoning him.
paras.zh: 莫扎特的竞争对手、作曲家安东尼奥·萨列里（1750—1825）在病重时供认，自己几十年前下毒谋杀了莫扎特。

paras.en: Salieri was suffering from dementia (痴呆) at the time of this confession, and he later withdrew it, but some—including Mozart’s widow Constanze—chose to believe the claim.
paras.zh: 萨列里作出这番供认时正患有痴呆症，后来他又撤回了供认，但仍有一些人——包括莫扎特的遗孀康斯坦策——选择相信这一说法。

paras.en: More than 150 years later, the English playwright Peter Shaffer based the story of Amadeus not just on Salieri’s confession but also on the idea that Salieri had suffered from a deep and bitter jealousy of Mozart throughout the ten years that they both lived and worked as composers in Vienna.
paras.zh: 150多年后，英国剧作家彼得·谢弗创作《莫扎特传》的故事时，不仅以萨列里的供认为依据，还依据了这样一种说法：在两人同为作曲家、在维也纳生活和工作的那十年里，萨列里始终对莫扎特怀着深深的妒恨，饱受其折磨。

w.m: adj. 怨恨的；（情感）强烈而痛苦的

paras.en: In the fun-loving Mozart, the story goes, Salieri saw a true genius—one who made his own talent and accomplishments appear mediocre—and this drove him on a vendetta (宿怨) that ultimately culminated in murder.
paras.zh: 按照故事的说法，萨列里在爱玩爱闹的莫扎特身上看到了一位真正的天才——这位天才让萨列里自己的才华和成就都显得平庸——这驱使他走上了一条积怨复仇之路，最终酿成了谋杀。

w.m: n. 宿怨；长期的报复行动

paras.en: Shaffer’s story makes for great drama, but it is, of course, biased against Salieri.
paras.zh: 谢弗的故事造就了一出精彩的戏剧，但它当然对萨列里抱有偏见。

paras.en: In fact, at the time, Salieri was regarded as the more accomplished musician and composer.
paras.zh: 事实上，在当时，萨列里被视为两人中更有造诣的音乐家和作曲家。

w.m: adj. 有造诣的；技艺高超的

paras.en: From the 1770s through the 1790s, he composed dozens of operas, many of them proving popular and considered innovative.
paras.zh: 从18世纪70年代到90年代，他创作了几十部歌剧，事实证明其中许多部都很受欢迎，而且被认为富有新意。

w.m: adj. 富有新意的；创新的

paras.en: A mark of his prominence was his appointment to the influential post of Kapellmeister, or musical director, to the court of Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II.
paras.zh: 他地位显赫的一个标志，是被任命为神圣罗马帝国皇帝约瑟夫二世宫廷的乐长（即音乐总监），这是一个颇具影响力的职位。

paras.en: Salieri was also a teacher whose pupils included Ludwig van Beethoven, Franz Liszt and Franz Schubert.
paras.zh: 萨列里还是一位老师，他的学生包括路德维希·凡·贝多芬、弗朗茨·李斯特和弗朗茨·舒伯特。

paras.en: In his private life, he may not have had Mozart’s exuberance but nor was he the lonely and celibate man played with such convincing severity by F. Murray Abraham in Amadeus.
paras.zh: 在私生活中，他或许没有莫扎特那样的旺盛活力，但他也不是《莫扎特传》里那个孤独、独身禁欲的男人；F·默里·亚伯拉罕把这个人物演得如此冷峻，如此令人信服。

w.m: n. 充沛的活力；热情洋溢
conj. 也不（用于分句开头，其后主谓倒装）
F·默里·亚伯拉罕（美国演员）
adj. 独身禁欲的；独身的
adj. 令人信服的；逼真的

paras.en: Salieri was married at the time he knew Mozart, and he fathered no fewer than eight children.
paras.zh: 萨列里与莫扎特相识期间已经结婚，而且他育有不下八个子女。

paras.en: If Salieri had little reason to fear or resent Mozart’s success, there was naturally a degree of rivalry between two men working in the same profession and in the same city.
paras.zh: 虽说萨列里几乎没有理由畏惧或怨恨莫扎特的成功，但同在一行、同在一城的两个人之间，自然会存在一定程度的竞争。

paras.en: Salieri (born near Verona) and Mozart (born in Salzburg) belonged to separate musical groups, and Italian and German opera fell into and out of favor during this period.
paras.zh: 萨列里（生于维罗纳附近）和莫扎特（生于萨尔茨堡）分属不同的音乐圈子，而在这一时期，意大利歌剧和德国歌剧时而受宠、时而失宠。

w.h: fall into and out of favor

paras.en: The composers were therefore vying for work, including the prestigious post of musical tutor to the Princess of Württemberg, which Salieri successfully attained.
paras.zh: 因此，两位作曲家一直在争夺工作机会，其中包括声望很高的符腾堡公主音乐教师一职，萨列里成功获得了这一职位。

w.m: adj. 声望高的；有威望的

paras.en: As composers, they saw their operas debut side by side, yet there is little evidence of any animosity between them.
paras.zh: 两人同为作曲家，各自的歌剧曾同台首演，然而几乎没有证据表明他们之间存在任何敌意。

paras.en: Mozart did complain in a letter to his father that Joseph II favored Salieri over all other composers, but that observation was an accurate one.
paras.zh: 莫扎特确实曾在写给父亲的信中抱怨，约瑟夫二世偏爱萨列里胜过其他所有作曲家，不过这一看法倒是准确的。

paras.en: Both Mozart and his father suspected that, behind the scenes, Salieri tried to undermine Mozart’s success, but these were hardly unusual suspicions in a field so reliant on patronage.
paras.zh: 莫扎特和他父亲都怀疑萨列里在幕后企图阻挠莫扎特取得成功，但在一个如此依赖赞助的领域，这类怀疑几乎算不上稀奇。

paras.en: In public, fellow composers reported that Mozart and Salieri were friendly with one another.
paras.zh: 据同行作曲家所述，莫扎特和萨列里在公开场合彼此友好。

paras.en: Shortly after the premiere of Mozart’s The Magic Flute, Salieri attended a performance with Mozart, and applauded warmly and vigorously.
paras.zh: 莫扎特的《魔笛》首演后不久，萨列里和莫扎特一起观看了该剧的一场演出，并热情而卖力地鼓掌。

paras.en: Thus, any ill feeling between Mozart and Salieri was borne by the former rather than the latter—contrary to what is strongly depicted in Amadeus—and it stemmed from Salieri’s status and success rather than his perceived mediocrity.
paras.zh: 因此，莫扎特与萨列里之间若有任何怨恨，心怀怨恨的也是前者而不是后者——这与《莫扎特传》极力描绘的情形相反；而且这种怨恨源于萨列里的地位和成就，而不是他所谓的平庸。

paras.en: Mozart’s resentments were those of a younger man struggling for position in the world.
paras.zh: 莫扎特的怨恨，是年轻后辈的怨恨：他正为在世上谋得一席之地而奋力打拼。

paras.en: Although he had talent, he spent many years struggling to find a suitable post or patronage.
paras.zh: 他虽有才华，却花了许多年苦苦寻找合适的职位或赞助。

w.m: 艰难地（努力）做；苦苦设法

paras.en: He and his father travelled widely during his youth, seeking a distinguished appointment but finding mainly low pay and occasionally humiliating circumstances.
paras.zh: 他年少时与父亲四处游历，想谋求一个显要的职位，得到的却主要是微薄的报酬，偶尔还会陷入令人屈辱的处境。

w.m: adj. 令人屈辱的；丢脸的

paras.en: It was in the period after 1781, when Mozart defied his father and decided to live and work independently in Vienna, that his career flourished.
paras.zh: 1781年，莫扎特违抗父命，决定在维也纳独立生活和工作；正是在此后的那段时期，他的事业蓬勃发展起来。

paras.en: In the space of ten years, he found great success with the operas The Abduction from the Seraglio (1782), The Marriage of Figaro (1786), Don Giovanni (1787) and The Magic Flute (1791).
paras.zh: 在十年的时间里，他凭借歌剧《后宫诱逃》（1782）、《费加罗的婚礼》（1786）、《唐璜》（1787）和《魔笛》（1791）取得了巨大成功。

paras.en: These were composed alongside his piano concertos, symphonies and chamber music, and together with his work as a performer and teacher, his success brought a high income.
paras.zh: 他在创作这些歌剧的同时，还创作了钢琴协奏曲、交响曲和室内乐；创作上的成功，再加上他作为演奏家和教师的工作，为他带来了丰厚的收入。

paras.en: Mozart’s money troubles were the result of excessive spending, and his volatile temperament, rather than any malicious schemes against him.
paras.zh: 莫扎特的经济困难，是他开销过度、性情多变的结果，而不是有人针对他设下了什么恶意阴谋。

w.m: adj. 多变的；反复无常的

paras.en: His death, at the age of 35, was not considered suspicious at the time as he had been ill for weeks with a fever.
paras.zh: 他35岁去世，当时人们并不认为他的死有什么可疑之处，因为此前他已经发烧病了好几个星期。

paras.en: While it is true that he had a commoner’s funeral, in 18th-century Vienna this was not unusual for a man of non-aristocratic standing.
paras.zh: 他的葬礼诚然是平民规格，但在18世纪的维也纳，对一个非贵族身份的人来说，这并不罕见。

paras.en: It certainly was not a mark of his downfall or ignominy, as implied by the film.
paras.zh: 这当然也不像影片所暗示的那样，是他没落或蒙受耻辱的标志。

paras.en: At his death, Mozart was second in stature only to Salieri as Vienna’s most prominent musician and composer.
paras.zh: 莫扎特去世时，在维也纳最杰出的音乐家和作曲家中，他的地位仅次于萨列里。

paras.en: The drama of Amadeus stems not from historical accuracies, but from our contemporary knowledge that Mozart’s music and reputation have survived for centuries—and continued to find new, zesty audiences—while Salieri’s name and work quickly faded.
paras.zh: 《莫扎特传》的戏剧性并非来自对史实的准确呈现，而是来自我们今天所知道的这一事实：莫扎特的音乐和声誉流传了几个世纪——而且不断赢得热情洋溢的新听众——而萨列里的名字和作品却很快被人淡忘。

w.m: adj. 热情洋溢的；充满活力的

paras.en: Mozart’s secondary status during his own lifetime thus appears unjust and unwarranted, and he is invested with the role of the struggling artist and unappreciated genius.
paras.zh: 因此，莫扎特生前屈居次席，就显得既不公正，又毫无道理；他也被赋予了一个角色：苦苦挣扎的艺术家、怀才不遇的天才。

w.m: adj. 居第二位的；次一等的
adj. 毫无道理的；无正当理由的
adj. 未被赏识的；怀才不遇的

paras.en: This may be shaky history, but the film has enough laughter, conflict, romance and tragedy to please any opera lover, except perhaps for Salieri himself, who undoubtedly would have told the tale in an altogether different key.
paras.zh: 这或许是靠不住的历史，但影片的欢笑、冲突、爱情和悲剧足以让任何一位歌剧爱好者满意——也许萨列里本人除外，他无疑会用一种截然不同的调子来讲述这个故事。

w.m: adj. 靠不住的；不可靠的

passages.name: 2019年 Passage One
passages.title: 强打精神的汤米·威廉
passages.genre: 小说节选 · 人物与心理
passages.summary: 汤米·威廉自认为掩饰烦恼的本事不比旁人差。他住在纽约一家住客大多已过退休年龄的饭店里，几个月来没有工作，靠早起来维持士气；但他意识到这种日子难以为继，感到一场早有预感的大麻烦就要到来。这天早上，他照常下楼穿过大堂，在报摊前与衣着讲究的鲁宾一起眺望远处的安索尼亚饭店，又谈起自己的衬衫，显出他至今依然很有魅力。

paras.en: When it came to concealing his troubles, Tommy Wilhelm was not less capable than the next fellow.
paras.zh: 说到掩饰自己的烦恼，汤米·威廉的本事并不比旁人差。

paras.en: So at least he thought, and there was a certain amount of evidence to back him up.
paras.zh: 至少他自己是这么想的，而且也有一定的证据可以支持他这个看法。

paras.en: He had once been an actor—no, not quite, an extra—and he knew what acting should be.
paras.zh: 他曾经当过演员——不，不完全是，是当过临时演员——他知道表演应该是什么样子。

w.m: n. （电影的）临时演员；群众演员

paras.en: Also, he was smoking a cigar, and when a man is smoking a cigar, wearing a hat, he has an advantage; it is harder to find out how he feels.
paras.zh: 再说，他正抽着雪茄；一个人抽着雪茄、戴着帽子，就占了优势：别人更难弄清他心里是什么感受。

paras.en: He came from the twenty-third floor down to the lobby on the mezzanine to collect his mail before breakfast, and he believed—he hoped—that he looked passably well: doing all right.
paras.zh: 早饭前，他从二十三楼下到夹层的大堂去取信件；他相信——他希望——自己看上去还过得去：一副日子过得还不错的样子。

w.m: n. 夹层楼面（底层与二楼之间）
adv. 还过得去地；尚可地

paras.en: It was a matter of sheer hope, because there was not much that he could add to his present effort.
paras.zh: 这全凭希望，因为在眼下这番努力之上，他再也添不了多少了。

paras.en: On the fourteenth floor he looked for his father to enter the elevator; they often met at this hour, on the way to breakfast.
paras.zh: 到了十四楼，他盼着父亲走进电梯来；父子俩常在这个钟点、在去吃早饭的路上碰面。

w.m: 盼着（某人）做；期待（某人）做

paras.en: If he worried about his appearance it was mainly for his old father’s sake.
paras.zh: 他若是为自己的外表操心，那主要是为了年迈的父亲。

paras.en: But there was no stop on the fourteenth, and the elevator sank and sank.
paras.zh: 可电梯在十四楼没有停，一直往下沉，往下沉。

paras.en: Then the smooth door opened and the great dark-red uneven carpet that covered the lobby billowed toward Wilhelm’s feet.
paras.zh: 接着，光滑的电梯门开了，那块铺满大堂、凹凸不平的深红色大地毯朝威廉脚下翻涌过来。

w.m: adj. 不平的；凹凸不平的
v. 像波浪般翻涌；起伏

paras.en: In the foreground the lobby was dark, sleepy.
paras.zh: 近处的大堂光线昏暗，睡意沉沉。

w.m: n. 前景；（视野中的）近处
adj. 昏昏欲睡的；沉寂的

paras.en: French drapes like sails kept out the sun, but three high, narrow windows were open, and in the blue air Wilhelm saw a pigeon about to light on the great chain that supported the marquee of the movie house directly underneath the lobby.
paras.zh: 船帆似的法式帷幔挡住了阳光，但有三扇又高又窄的窗户开着；在湛蓝的空中，威廉看见一只鸽子正要落到那根粗大的链条上，链条吊着大堂正下方那家电影院的遮檐。

w.m: n. （剧院、电影院入口上方的）遮檐；大雨篷

paras.en: For one moment he heard the wings beating strongly.
paras.zh: 有那么一会儿，他听见那对翅膀在有力地扑打。

paras.en: Most of the guests at the Hotel Gloriana were past the age of retirement.
paras.zh: 格洛丽亚纳饭店的住客大多已过了退休年龄。

w.m: prep. 超过；过了（某年龄、时间）

paras.en: Along Broadway in the Seventies, Eighties, and Nineties, a great part of New York’s vast population of old men and women lives.
paras.zh: 纽约数量庞大的老年男女，有很大一部分住在百老汇大街沿线的七十几街、八十几街和九十几街一带。

paras.en: Unless the weather is too cold or wet they fill the benches about the tiny railed parks and along the subway gratings from Verdi Square to Columbia University, they crowd the shops and cafeterias, the dime stores, the tearooms, the bakeries, the beauty parlors, the reading rooms and club rooms.
paras.zh: 只要天气不太冷、雨不太大，从威尔第广场到哥伦比亚大学，那些围着栏杆的小小公园四周和地铁通风栅栏沿线的长椅上就坐满了他们；他们挤满了商店和自助餐馆、廉价杂货店、茶室、面包店、美容院、阅览室和俱乐部活动室。

paras.en: Among these old people at the Gloriana, Wilhelm felt out of place.
paras.zh: 置身于格洛丽亚纳饭店的这些老人之中，威廉觉得自己格格不入。

paras.en: He was comparatively young, in his middle forties, large and blond, with big shoulders; his back was heavy and strong, if already a little stooped or thickened.
paras.zh: 他相对年轻，四十五岁上下，身材高大，一头金发，肩膀宽阔；他的背厚实强壮，只是已经有点驼了，或者说有点变厚了。

paras.en: After breakfast the old guests sat down on the green leather armchairs and sofas in the lobby and began to gossip and look into the papers; they had nothing to do but wait out the day.
paras.zh: 早饭后，那些上了年纪的住客在大堂的绿色皮扶手椅和沙发上坐下，开始闲聊、翻看报纸；他们无事可做，只能熬过这一天。

w.m: 等待（某段时间）过去；熬过

paras.en: But Wilhelm was used to an active life and liked to go out energetically in the morning.
paras.zh: 但威廉过惯了忙碌的生活，喜欢一早就精神抖擞地出门。

w.m: adv. 精力充沛地；劲头十足地

paras.en: And for several months, because he had no position, he had kept up his morale by rising early; he was shaved and in the lobby by eight o’clock.
paras.zh: 而且，几个月来，由于没有工作，他一直靠早起来维持士气；八点钟以前，他就已经刮好胡子，到了大堂。

paras.en: He bought the paper and some cigars and drank a Coca-Cola or two before he went in to breakfast with his father.
paras.zh: 他会买份报纸、几支雪茄，喝上一两瓶可口可乐，然后才进去和父亲一起吃早饭。

paras.en: After breakfast—out, out, out to attend to business.
paras.zh: 早饭以后——出门，出门，出门去办事。

paras.en: The getting out had in itself become the chief business.
paras.zh: 出门这件事本身，已经成了头等大事。

paras.en: But he had realized that he could not keep this up much longer, and today he was afraid.
paras.zh: 但他已经意识到，自己没法把这种日子再维持多久了，而今天他感到害怕。

paras.en: He was aware that his routine was about to break up and he sensed that a huge trouble long presaged (预感) but till now formless was due.
paras.zh: 他心里清楚，自己的日常惯例就要瓦解了；他感觉到，一场早有预感、但至今还没有成形的大麻烦就要来了。

w.m: adj. 预期（到来）的；即将到来的

paras.en: Before evening, he’d know.
paras.zh: 不到傍晚，他就会知道。

paras.en: Nevertheless he followed his daily course and crossed the lobby.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，他还是照每天的惯例，穿过了大堂。

paras.en: Rubin, the man at the newsstand, had poor eyes.
paras.zh: 报摊的鲁宾眼睛不好。

paras.en: They may not have been actually weak but they were poor in expression, with lacy lids that furled down at the corners.
paras.zh: 那双眼睛也许并不是真的视力差，但缺乏神采，眼皮皱得像花边，在眼角处向下卷着。

w.m: adj. 花边似的；蕾丝状的

paras.en: He dressed well.
paras.zh: 他衣着讲究。

paras.en: It didn’t seem necessary—he was behind the counter most of the time—but he dressed very well.
paras.zh: 这似乎没有必要——他大部分时间都待在柜台后面——可他还是穿得非常讲究。

paras.en: He had on a rich brown suit; the cuffs embarrassed the hairs on his small hands.
paras.zh: 他穿着一套浓褐色的西装；袖口让他那双小手上的汗毛都难为情了。

paras.en: He wore a Countess Mara painted necktie.
paras.zh: 他系着一条玛拉伯爵夫人牌的手绘领带。

paras.en: As Wilhelm approached, Rubin did not see him; he was looking out dreamily at the Hotel Ansonia, which was visible from his corner, several blocks away.
paras.zh: 威廉走过来时，鲁宾没有看见他；鲁宾正出神地向外望着安索尼亚饭店，那座饭店在几个街区以外，从他那个角落望得见。

paras.en: The Ansonia, the neighborhood’s great landmark, was built by Stanford White.
paras.zh: 安索尼亚饭店是这一带的著名地标，出自斯坦福·怀特之手。

paras.en: It looks like a baroque palace from Prague or Munich enlarged a hundred times, with towers, domes, huge swells and bubbles of metal gone green from exposure, iron fretwork and festoons.
paras.zh: 它看上去就像把布拉格或慕尼黑的一座巴洛克式宫殿放大了一百倍，有塔楼，有穹顶，有因风吹日晒而发绿的巨大金属凸起和圆泡，还有铁制的回纹装饰和花彩。

w.m: n. 回纹装饰；格子细工
v. 变得；变成（多接表颜色、状态的形容词）

paras.en: Black television antennae are densely planted on its round summits.
paras.zh: 在它那一个个圆圆的顶端上，密密麻麻地竖着黑色的电视天线。

w.m: adv. 密集地；密密麻麻地

paras.en: Under the changes of weather, it may look like marble or like sea water, black as slate in the fog, white as tufa in sunlight.
paras.zh: 随着天气变化，它看上去可能像大理石，也可能像海水；雾中黑如石板，阳光下白如石灰华。

w.m: n. 石灰华（一种多孔的白色石灰岩）

paras.en: This morning it looked like the image of itself reflected in deep water, white and cumulous above, with cavernous distortions underneath.
paras.zh: 今天早上，它就像自己倒映在深水里的影子，上部洁白，如积云层层堆叠，下部则扭曲变形，如洞穴般幽深。

w.m: adj. 积云状的；层层堆积的

paras.en: Together, the two men gazed at it.
paras.zh: 两个人一起凝望着它。

paras.en: Then Rubin said, “Your dad is in to breakfast already, the old gentleman.”
paras.zh: 接着鲁宾说：“你爸已经进去吃早饭了，那位老先生。”

paras.en: “Oh, yes?
paras.zh: “哦，是吗？

w.m: （用升调表示询问）是吗；真的吗

paras.en: Ahead of me today?”
paras.zh: 今天比我还早？”

paras.en: “That’s a real knocked-out shirt you got on,” said Rubin.
paras.zh: 鲁宾说：“你身上这件衬衫真是棒极了。”

w.m: adj. （俚）漂亮极了的；棒极了的

paras.en: “Where’s it from, Saks?”
paras.zh: “哪儿买的？萨克斯百货？”

w.m: 是从哪儿来的（这里指在哪儿买的）

paras.en: “No, it’s a Jack Fagman—Chicago.”
paras.zh: “不是，是杰克·法格曼牌的——芝加哥的。”

w.m: 一件杰克·法格曼牌的衣服（a + 品牌名，指该品牌的一件产品）

paras.en: Even when his spirits were low, Wilhelm could still wrinkle his forehead in a pleasing way.
paras.zh: 即使在情绪低落的时候，威廉依然能把额头皱得讨人喜欢。

w.m: adj. 讨人喜欢的；令人愉快的

paras.en: Some of the slow, silent movements of his face were very attractive.
paras.zh: 他脸上有些缓慢、无声的动作十分迷人。

w.m: adj. 有魅力的；吸引人的

paras.en: He went back a step, as if to stand away from himself and get a better look at his shirt.
paras.zh: 他往后退了一步，仿佛要站得离自己远一点，好把身上的衬衫看得更清楚些。

paras.en: His glance was comic, a comment upon his untidiness.
paras.zh: 他的眼神很滑稽，是在评说自己的不修边幅。

paras.en: He liked to wear good clothes, but once he had put it on each article appeared to go its own way.
paras.zh: 他喜欢穿好衣服，可每件衣服一旦穿上了身，似乎就各行其是了。

paras.en: Wilhelm, laughing, panted a little; his teeth were small; his cheeks when he laughed and puffed grew round, and he looked much younger than his years.
paras.zh: 威廉笑着，有点气喘；他牙齿很小；一笑、一喘，脸颊就鼓得圆圆的，看上去比实际年龄年轻得多。

w.m: v. 喘粗气；呼哧呼哧地喘

paras.en: In the old days when he was a college freshman and wore a raccoon coat and a beanie (无檐小帽) on his large blond head his father used to say that, big as he was, he could charm a bird out of a tree.
paras.zh: 当年他还是大学一年级新生，穿着浣熊皮大衣，大大的金发脑袋上戴一顶无檐小帽，那时他父亲常说，别看他个头这么大，却能把树上的鸟儿都哄下来。

w.m: 尽管他块头大（形容词 + as 引导让步倒装）

w.h: charm a bird out of a tree
w.m: 极有魅力；能把树上的鸟儿都哄下来

paras.en: Wilhelm had great charm still.
paras.zh: 威廉现在依然魅力十足。

paras.en: “I like this dove-gray color,” he said in his sociable, good-natured way.
paras.zh: 他带着惯有的那股爱交际、好脾气的劲儿说：“我喜欢这种鸽灰色。”

paras.en: “It isn’t washable.
paras.zh: “这件不能水洗。

paras.en: You have to send it to the cleaner.
paras.zh: 你得送去干洗店。

paras.en: It never smells as good as washed.
paras.zh: 干洗出来，闻着从来都不如水洗的好闻。

paras.en: But it’s a nice shirt.
paras.zh: 不过这件衬衫是挺好的。

paras.en: It cost sixteen, eighteen bucks.”
paras.zh: 这件花了十六还是十八块钱。”

passages.name: 2019年 Passage Two
passages.title: 纽约报业双雄：贝内特与格里利
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与新闻史
passages.summary: 19世纪40年代的纽约是“新”美国逐渐形成的地方，现代报纸也诞生于此。本·戴的《太阳报》内容单薄，如今很少有人认为它称得上报纸；贝内特和格里利这两位编辑则彻底变革了新闻业，他们的报纸是当时美国数一数二的报纸。两人截然不同、互相鄙视，却又出奇地相似：都游离于上流社会之外，都是无可救药的怪人，也都经历过漫长的学徒生涯才登上顶峰。

paras.en: By the 1840s New York was the leading commercial city of the United States.
paras.zh: 到19世纪40年代，纽约已是美国首屈一指的商业城市。

w.m: adj. 首屈一指的；一流的

paras.en: It had long since outpaced Philadelphia as the largest city in the country, and even though Boston continued to be venerated as the cultural capital of the nation, its image had become somewhat languid and effete; it had not kept up with the implications of the newly industrialized economy, of a diversified ethnic population, or of the rapidly rising middle class.
paras.zh: 纽约早已超过费城，成为全国最大的城市；波士顿尽管仍被尊为全国的文化之都，形象却已变得有些慵懒乏力、萎靡颓废；它没能适应新近工业化的经济、多元化的族裔人口以及迅速崛起的中产阶级所带来的种种影响。

w.m: adj. 慵懒的；无精打采的
adj. 萎靡颓废的；衰弱无力的
adj. 多元化的；多样化的

paras.en: New York was the place where the “new” America was coming into being, so it is hardly surprising that the modern newspaper had its birth there.
paras.zh: 纽约是“新”美国正在形成的地方，所以现代报纸诞生于此，也就不足为奇了。

paras.en: The penny paper had found its first success in New York.
paras.zh: 便士报最初就是在纽约取得成功的。

w.m: 便士报（售价一美分的大众化廉价报纸）

paras.en: By the mid-1830s Ben Day’s Sun was drawing readers from all walks of life.
paras.zh: 到19世纪30年代中期，本·戴的《太阳报》已经吸引着各行各业的读者。

w.m: adj. 中期的（mid-1830s：19世纪30年代中期）
来自各行各业的；来自社会各阶层的

paras.en: On the other hand the Sun was a skimpy sheet providing little more than minor diversions; few today would call it a newspaper at all.
paras.zh: 另一方面，《太阳报》只是一份内容单薄的小报，提供的不过是些无关紧要的消遣；如今很少有人会认为它称得上是报纸。

w.m: adj. 单薄的；内容贫乏的
n. 报纸；（印刷品的）一张
adj. 次要的；无关紧要的

paras.en: Day himself was an editor of limited vision, and he did not possess the ability or the imagination to climb the slopes to loftier heights.
paras.zh: 戴本人是个眼界有限的编辑，既没有能力，也没有想象力沿着山坡攀向更高处。

paras.en: If real newspapers were to emerge from the public’s demand for more and better coverage, they would have to come from a youthful generation of editors for whom journalism was a totally absorbing profession, an exacting vocational ideal rather than a mere offshoot of job printing.
paras.zh: 真正的报纸若要因公众对更多、更好报道的需求而诞生，就得出自年轻一代的编辑之手：对他们来说，新闻业是一项令人全身心投入的职业，是一种要求严苛的职业理想，而不只是零活印刷的一个分支。

w.m: adj. 令人全神贯注的；引人入胜的
adj. 要求严格的；苛刻的
零活印刷（承印名片、传单等杂件的印刷业务）

paras.en: By the 1840s two giants burst into the field, editors who would revolutionize journalism, would bring the newspaper into the modern age, and show how it could be influential in the national life.
paras.zh: 到19世纪40年代，两位巨擘闯入了这一领域，这两位编辑后来彻底变革了新闻业，把报纸带入了现代，并展示了报纸可以怎样在国家生活中发挥影响力。

w.m: v. 彻底变革；使发生革命性变化

paras.en: These two giants, neither of whom has been treated kindly by history, were James Gordon Bennett and Horace Greeley.
paras.zh: 这两位巨擘都没有得到历史的善待，他们就是詹姆斯·戈登·贝内特和霍勒斯·格里利。

paras.en: Bennett founded his New York Herald in 1835, less than two years after the appearance of the Sun.
paras.zh: 贝内特于1835年创办了《纽约先驱报》，距《太阳报》问世还不到两年。

paras.en: Horace Greeley founded his Tribune in 1841.
paras.zh: 霍勒斯·格里利于1841年创办了《论坛报》。

paras.en: Bennett and Greeley were the most innovative editors in New York until after the Civil War.
paras.zh: 直到南北战争结束以后，贝内特和格里利一直是纽约最具创新精神的编辑。

w.m: adj. 富有创新精神的；创新的

paras.en: Their newspapers were the leading American papers of the day, although for completely different reasons.
paras.zh: 他们的报纸是当时美国数一数二的报纸，不过各自的原因完全不同。

w.m: adj. 首屈一指的；一流的

paras.en: The two men despised each other, although not in the ways that newspaper editors had despised one another a few years before.
paras.zh: 两人互相鄙视，不过与几年前报纸编辑之间互相鄙视的方式不同。

paras.en: Neither was a political hack shackled to a political party.
paras.zh: 两人都不是受某个政党束缚的御用文人。

w.m: 政治雇佣文人；（为政党卖命的）御用文人

paras.en: Greeley fancied himself a public intellectual.
paras.zh: 格里利自命为公共知识分子。

paras.en: He had strong political views, and he wanted to run for office himself, but party factotum he could never be; he bristled with ideals and causes of his own devising.
paras.zh: 他政治观点鲜明，也想亲自竞选公职，但永远不可能当政党的听差杂役；他满脑子都是自己构想出来的理想和主张。

w.m: n. 杂役；（什么杂事都干的）听差
n. 主张；（为之奋斗的）事业

paras.en: Officially he was a Whig (and later a Republican), but he seldom gave comfort to his chosen party.
paras.zh: 名义上他是辉格党人（后来又成了共和党人），但他很少让自己选定的政党宽心。

w.m: n. 辉格党人（美国19世纪政党成员）

paras.en: Bennett, on the other hand, had long since cut his political ties, and although his paper covered local and national politics fully and he went after politicians with hammer and tongs, Bennett was a cynic, a distruster of all settled values.
paras.zh: 相比之下，贝内特早已斩断了自己的政治关系；尽管他的报纸对地方和全国政治报道得十分全面，他本人也对政客们猛烈抨击，但贝内特是个愤世嫉俗的人，不信任一切既定的价值观。

w.m: n. 愤世嫉俗者；怀疑一切的人
adj. 既定的；固定不变的
