paras.en: He did not regard himself as an intellectual, although in fact he was better educated than Greeley.
paras.zh: 他并不认为自己是知识分子，尽管实际上他受的教育比格里利更好。

paras.en: He thought himself only a hard-boiled newspaperman.
paras.zh: 他觉得自己只是个冷峻老练的报人。

w.m: adj. 冷峻老练的；不动感情的

paras.en: Greeley was interested in ideas and in what was happening to the country.
paras.zh: 格里利感兴趣的是各种思想，以及这个国家正在经历的一切。

paras.en: Bennett was only interested in his newspaper.
paras.zh: 贝内特感兴趣的只有他的报纸。

paras.en: He wanted to find out what the news was, what people wanted to read.
paras.zh: 他想弄清楚新闻是什么，人们想读的是什么。

paras.en: And when he found out he gave it to them.
paras.zh: 而他一弄清楚，就把这些提供给人们。

paras.en: As different as Bennett and Greeley were from each other, they were also curiously alike.
paras.zh: 贝内特和格里利尽管彼此截然不同，却也出奇地相似。

w.m: （as 引导让步）尽管……如此不同

paras.en: Both stood outside the circle of polite society, even when they became prosperous, and in Bennett’s case, wealthy.
paras.zh: 即便后来两人都已发达——就贝内特而言，更是成了富豪——他们也依然游离于上流社会的圈子之外。

w.m: adj. 发达的；兴旺富足的

paras.en: Both were incurable eccentrics.
paras.zh: 两人都是无可救药的怪人。

w.m: adj. 无可救药的；不可救药的

paras.en: Neither was a gentleman.
paras.zh: 两人都不是绅士。

paras.en: Neither conjured up the picture of a successful editor.
paras.zh: 两人都不会让人联想到成功编辑的形象。

w.m: 使人想起；使浮现于脑海

paras.en: Greeley was unkempt, always looking like an unmade bed.
paras.zh: 格里利不修边幅，看上去总像一张没整理过的床铺。

w.m: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的

paras.en: Even when he was nationally famous in the 1850s he resembled a clerk in a third-rate brokerage house, with slips of paper—marked-up proofs perhaps—hanging out of his pockets or stuck in his hat.
paras.zh: 即便在19世纪50年代已经名满全国，他看上去仍像三流经纪行里的小职员，一张张纸条（也许是批改过的校样）不是从衣袋里耷拉出来，就是插在帽子上。

paras.en: He became fat, was always nearsighted, always peering over spectacles.
paras.zh: 他后来发了福，一向近视，总是从眼镜上方眯眼往外瞧。

w.m: v. 费力地看；（因看不清而）眯眼细看

paras.en: He spoke in a piping, high-pitched whine (哀号).
paras.zh: 他说起话来尖声细气，调门很高，像在哀号。

paras.en: Not a few people suggested that he looked exactly like the illustrations of Charles Dickens’s Mr. Pickwick.
paras.zh: 不少人说，他看起来跟查尔斯·狄更斯笔下匹克威克先生的插图一模一样。

w.m: 匹克威克先生（狄更斯小说《匹克威克外传》的主人公）

paras.en: Greeley provided a humorous description of himself, written under the pretense that it had been the work of his long-time adversary James Fenimore Cooper.
paras.zh: 格里利对自己作过一番幽默的描述，假称是出自他的多年宿敌詹姆斯·费尼莫尔·库珀之手。

paras.en: The editor was, according to this little pastiche, a half-bald, long-legged, slouching individual “so rocking in gait (步态) that he walks down both sides of the street at once.”
paras.zh: 按这篇小小仿作的说法，这位编辑是个半秃顶、长腿、弓腰驼背的人，“走起路来左摇右晃，竟能同时走在街道的两侧”。

w.m: n. 仿作；（模仿他人风格的）模仿之作
adj. 弓腰驼背的；没精打采的

paras.en: The appearance of Bennett was somewhat different but hardly more reassuring.
paras.zh: 贝内特的外表有些不同，但也很难说更让人放心。

w.m: adj. 令人放心的；让人安心的

paras.en: A shrewd, wiry (瘦而结实) Scotsman, who seemed to repel intimacy, Bennett looked around at the world with a squinty glare of suspicion.
paras.zh: 贝内特是个精明、瘦而结实的苏格兰人，似乎排斥与人亲近；他眯着眼，带着怀疑的神色怒视着周围的世界。

w.m: v. 排斥；使人不敢接近

paras.en: His eyes did not focus right.
paras.zh: 他的眼睛无法正常聚焦。

paras.en: They seemed to fix themselves on nothing and everything at the same time.
paras.zh: 那双眼睛似乎什么都没盯着，同时又什么都在盯着。

paras.en: He was as solitary as an oyster, the classic loner.
paras.zh: 他像牡蛎一样孤僻，是个典型的独行侠。

w.m: adj. 孤僻的；独来独往的
n. 不合群的人；独来独往的人

paras.en: He seldom made close friendships and few people trusted him, although nobody who had dealings with him, however brief, doubted his abilities.
paras.zh: 他很少与人深交，也很少有人信任他，不过凡是同他打过交道的人，无论交往多么短暂，都没有怀疑过他的能力。

paras.en: He, too, could have come out of a book of Dickensian eccentrics, although perhaps Ebenezer Scrooge or Thomas Gradgrind comes to mind rather than the kindly old Mr. Pickwick.
paras.zh: 他也满可以是从一本狄更斯式怪人录里走出来的人物，不过让人想到的或许是埃比尼泽·斯克鲁奇或托马斯·葛擂硬，而不是和蔼的老匹克威克先生。

w.m: adj. 狄更斯式的；狄更斯作品中的
匹克威克先生（狄更斯小说《匹克威克外传》的主人公）

paras.en: Greeley was laughed at but admired; Bennett was seldom laughed at but never admired; on the other hand, he had a hard professional competence and an encyclopedic knowledge of his adopted country, an in-depth learning uncorrupted by vague idealisms.
paras.zh: 格里利受人嘲笑，却也受人钦佩；贝内特很少受人嘲笑，却从未受人钦佩；但另一方面，他有着过硬的专业能力，对自己移居的这个国家有着百科全书般的了解，这是一种未受空泛理想主义侵蚀的深厚学识。

w.m: adj. 百科全书式的；知识渊博的
adj. 未受侵蚀的；未被败坏的

paras.en: All of this perfectly suited him for the journalism of this confusing age.
paras.zh: 凭着这一切，他在那个纷乱的时代从事新闻业，再合适不过。

w.m: adj. 令人困惑的；纷乱的

paras.en: Both Greeley and Bennett had served long, humiliating and disappointing apprenticeships in the newspaper business.
paras.zh: 格里利和贝内特都曾在报业度过漫长、屈辱而又令人失望的学徒生涯。

paras.en: They took a long time getting to the top, the only reward for the long years of waiting being that when they had their own newspapers, both knew what they wanted and tenaciously set about getting it.
paras.zh: 他们花了很长时间才登上顶峰，多年等待换来的唯一回报是：等到有了自己的报纸，两人都清楚自己想要什么，并锲而不舍地着手去争取。

w.m: adv. 锲而不舍地；顽强地

paras.en: Bennett, older by sixteen years, found solid commercial success first, but with no one to offer a word of encouragement, whereas when Greeley founded the Tribune in 1841 he had the strong support of the Whig party and had already had a short period of modest success as an editor.
paras.zh: 贝内特比格里利年长十六岁，率先在商业上取得了稳固的成功，却没有任何人给过他一句鼓励；而格里利1841年创办《论坛报》时，有辉格党的大力支持，此前做编辑时也已小有成就，只是为时不长。

paras.en: When Bennett started up the Herald in 1835 in a dingy cellar room at 20 Wall Street he had no one behind him except himself.
paras.zh: 1835年，贝内特在华尔街20号一间昏暗的地下室里创办《先驱报》时，除了他自己，背后没有任何人支持。

paras.en: Fortunately, this turned out to be quite enough.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，结果证明这就已经完全足够了。

passages.name: 2019年 Passage Three
passages.title: 盗匪传奇为何令人着迷
passages.genre: 议论文 · 历史与文化
passages.summary: 本文从一部关于澳大利亚盗匪内德·凯利的电影说起，探讨人们为何总会迷上盗匪。作者指出，“社会盗匪”忠于并认同自己出身的农民，传说中的“侠盗”劫富济贫、只与地方上的压迫者为敌，不过没有哪个盗匪完全符合这一形象。“侠盗”代表着一种极其原始的社会抗议形式，他们无法消除压迫，却证明了正义是可以实现的。现实中的盗匪植根于农民社会，会随着这种社会的农业体系一同成为过去，但关于盗匪的故事和电影仍不断问世，观众依然能从对盗匪的钦佩中得到支撑。

paras.en: Why make a film about Ned Kelly?
paras.zh: 为什么要拍一部关于内德·凯利的电影？

paras.en: More ingenious crimes than those committed by the reckless Australian bandit are reported every day.
paras.zh: 每天见诸报道的罪案中，都有比这个鲁莽的澳大利亚盗匪所犯罪行更巧妙的。

w.m: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的

paras.en: What is there in Ned Kelly to justify dragging the mesmeric Mick Jagger so far into the Australian bush and away from his natural haunts?
paras.zh: 内德·凯利身上有什么，值得把摄人心魄的米克·贾格尔大老远拖进澳大利亚丛林、让他远离平日出没的地方？

w.m: v. 成为……的正当理由；证明……有理
adj. 有催眠般魅力的；令人着迷的
那么远（此处非“迄今为止”）
adj. 惯常的；（某人）本来所处的
n. 常去的地方；出没之处

paras.en: The answer is that the film makers know we always fall for a bandit, and Jagger is set to do for bold Ned Kelly what Brando once did for the arrogant Emiliano Zapata.
paras.zh: 答案是：电影制作人知道我们总会迷上盗匪；白兰度当年为傲慢的埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔所做的，贾格尔也将为大胆的内德·凯利再做一次。

paras.en: The bandit inhabits a special realm of legend where his deeds are embroidered by others; where his death rather than his life is considered beyond belief; where the men who bring him to “justice” are afflicted with doubts about their role.
paras.zh: 盗匪栖身于一个特殊的传奇国度：在那里，他的事迹经别人添枝加叶；在那里，人们觉得难以置信的不是他的一生，而是他的死；在那里，将他“绳之以法”的人，会为自己所扮演的角色饱受疑虑困扰。

w.m: v. 渲染；添枝加叶（本义“刺绣”）

paras.en: The bandits had a role to play as definite as that of the authorities who condemned them.
paras.zh: 盗匪要扮演的角色，和给他们定罪的当局所扮演的角色一样明确。

w.m: 有角色要扮演；要发挥作用

paras.en: These were men in conflict with authority, and, in the absence of strong law or the idea of loyal opposition, they took to the hills.
paras.zh: 这些人与当局相冲突；在既没有强有力的法律、也没有忠诚反对派这种观念的情况下，他们便遁入了山林。

w.m: 在缺乏……的情况下；没有……时
忠诚反对派（效忠国家、在现有体制内合法反对的反对派）

paras.en: Even there, however, many of them obeyed certain unwritten rules.
paras.zh: 然而，即便在山里，他们中的许多人仍遵守着某些不成文的规矩。

paras.en: These robbers, who claimed to be something more than mere thieves, had in common, firstly, a sense of loyalty to and identity with the peasants they came from.
paras.zh: 这些强盗自称不只是区区小偷，他们的共同之处，首先是对自己出身的农民怀有忠诚感和认同感。

paras.en: They didn’t steal the peasant’s harvest; they did steal the lord’s.
paras.zh: 他们不偷农民的收成，领主的收成却照偷不误。

paras.en: And certain characteristics seem to apply to “social bandits” whether they were in Sicily or Peru.
paras.zh: 而且，无论是在西西里还是在秘鲁，某些特征似乎都适用于“社会盗匪”。

paras.en: They were generally young men under the age of marriage, predictably the best age for dissidence.
paras.zh: 他们一般是未到婚龄的年轻男子，可想而知，这是最适合反叛的年纪。

w.m: adv. 可想而知；不出所料

paras.en: Some were simply the surplus male population who had to look for another source of income; others were runaway serfs or ex-soldiers; a minority, though the most interesting, were outstanding men who were unwilling to accept the meek and passive role of peasant.
paras.zh: 有些人只不过是过剩的男性人口，不得不另谋收入来源；另一些人是逃亡的农奴或退伍士兵；还有少数人——却也是最有意思的一类——是些出众的人物，不甘接受农民那种逆来顺受、消极被动的角色。

w.m: adj. 温顺的；逆来顺受的

paras.en: They usually operated in bands between ten and twenty strong and relied for survival on difficult terrain and bad transport.
paras.zh: 他们通常结成十到二十人的团伙活动，靠地形险恶、交通不便来求生存。

paras.en: And bandits prospered best where authority was merely local—over the next hill and they were free.
paras.zh: 而在当局的权力仅及于本地的地区，盗匪最为兴旺——翻过下一座山，他们就自由了。

paras.en: Unlike the general run of peasantry they had a taste for flamboyant dress and gesture; but they usually shared the peasants’ religious beliefs and superstitions.
paras.zh: 与一般农民不同，他们喜爱张扬的衣着和举止；不过，他们通常与农民有着相同的宗教信仰和迷信观念。

w.m: adj. 张扬的；艳丽夸张的

paras.en: The first sign of a man caught up in the Robin Hood syndrome was when he started out, forced into outlawry as a victim of injustice; and when he then set out to “right wrongs”, first his own and then other people’s.
paras.zh: 一个人陷入罗宾汉综合征，最初的迹象是：起步时，他身为不公的受害者，被迫沦为法外之徒；随后，他着手“讨回公道”，先为自己，再为他人。

w.m: n. 被剥夺法律保护；亡命生涯

paras.en: The classic bandit then “takes from the rich and gives to the poor” in conformity with his own sense of social justice; he never kills except in self-defense or justifiable revenge; his people admire and help to protect him; he dies through the treason of one of them; he behaves as if invisible and invulnerable; he is a “loyalist”, never the enemy of the king but only of the local oppressors.
paras.zh: 典型的盗匪随后会依照自己的社会正义观“劫富济贫”；除非出于自卫或正当的复仇，他从不杀人；他的乡亲钦佩他，并帮着保护他；他死于某个乡亲的背叛；他行事仿佛自己能隐身、刀枪不入；他是“忠君者”，从不与国王为敌，只与地方上的压迫者为敌。

w.h: take from the rich and give to the poor

w.m: adj. 正当的；情有可原的
adj. 刀枪不入的；不会受伤的

paras.en: None of the bandits lived up fully to this image of the “noble robber” and for many the claim of larger motives was often a delusion.
paras.zh: 没有哪个盗匪完全符合这种“侠盗”形象；对许多盗匪来说，自称怀有更远大的动机，往往只是他们自己的妄想。

paras.en: Yet amazingly, many of these violent men did behave at least half the time in accordance with this idealist pattern.
paras.zh: 然而令人惊讶的是，这些暴戾之徒中有许多人确实至少有一半时间是按照这种理想主义模式行事的。

paras.en: Pancho Villa in Mexico and Salvatore Giuliano in Italy began their careers harshly victimized.
paras.zh: 墨西哥的潘乔·比利亚和意大利的萨尔瓦托雷·朱利亚诺，在生涯之初都曾惨遭迫害。

w.m: 潘乔·比利亚（墨西哥革命将领，早年为盗匪）

paras.en: Many of their charitable acts later became legends.
paras.zh: 他们的许多善举后来都成了传奇。

w.m: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的

paras.en: Far from being defeated by death, bandits’ reputation for invincibility was often strengthened by the manner of their dying.
paras.zh: 盗匪不可战胜的名声非但没有败给死亡，反而常常因他们的死法而更加牢固。

paras.en: The “dirty little coward” who shot Jesse James in the back is in every ballad about him, and the implication is that nothing else could have brought Jesse down.
paras.zh: 从背后向杰西·詹姆斯开枪的那个“卑鄙的小懦夫”，出现在每一首唱他的民谣里，言下之意是：除此之外，再没有什么能把杰西打倒。

paras.en: Even when the police claimed the credit, as they tried to do at first with Giuliano’s death, the local people refused to believe it.
paras.zh: 即便警方把功劳揽到自己头上——朱利亚诺死后，警方起初就曾试图这么做——当地百姓也拒绝相信。

paras.en: And it is not just the bandit’s vitality that prompts the people to refuse to believe that their hero has died; his death would be in some way the death of hope.
paras.zh: 而且，促使百姓拒绝相信自己的英雄已死的，不只是盗匪的生命力；他要是死了，在某种意义上就等于希望也死了。

w.m: 在某种意义上；在某种程度上

paras.en: For the traditional “noble robber” represents an extremely primitive form of social protest, perhaps the most primitive there is.
paras.zh: 因为传统的“侠盗”代表着一种极其原始的社会抗议形式，或许是所有形式中最原始的一种。

paras.en: He is an individual who refuses to bend his back, that is all.
paras.zh: 他是一个拒绝折腰的个人，仅此而已。

paras.en: Most protesters will eventually be bought over and persuaded to come to terms with the official power.
paras.zh: 大多数抗议者最终都会被收买，被说服与官方权力妥协。

paras.en: That is why the few who do not, or who are believed to have remained uncontaminated, have so great and passionate a burden of admiration and longing laid upon them.
paras.zh: 正因如此，那少数没有就范的人，或者被认为始终未受玷污的人，才会背负着如此沉重而炽热的钦佩与渴盼。

w.m: 正因如此；这就是……的原因
adj. 未受玷污的；未受污染的
adj. 炽热的；充满激情的

paras.en: They cannot abolish oppression.
paras.zh: 他们无法消除压迫。

paras.en: But they do prove that justice is possible, that poor men need not be humble, helpless and meek.
paras.zh: 但他们确实证明了：正义是可以实现的，穷人不必卑微、无助、逆来顺受。

w.m: adj. 温顺的；逆来顺受的

paras.en: The bandit in the real world is rooted in peasant society and when its simple agricultural system is left behind, so is he.
paras.zh: 现实世界中的盗匪植根于农民社会；一旦这种社会的简单农业体系成为过去，盗匪也就随之成为过去。

w.m: 他也一样（so＋助动词＋主语，倒装；此处指他也随之成为过去）

paras.en: But the tales and legends, the books and films continue to appear for an audience that is neither peasant nor bandit.
paras.zh: 但那些故事和传说、书籍和电影仍在不断问世，面向的受众既不是农民，也不是盗匪。

paras.en: In some ways the characters and deeds of the great bandits could so readily be the stuff of grand opera—Don Jose in “Carmen” is based on the Andalusian bandit El Tempranillo.
paras.zh: 在某些方面，那些著名盗匪的性格和事迹很容易就能成为大歌剧的素材——《卡门》中的唐·何塞，就是以安达卢西亚盗匪埃尔·坦普拉尼略为原型的。

w.m: adv. 容易地；轻而易举地
大歌剧（严肃题材、全剧演唱的歌剧）
n. 《卡门》（法国作曲家比才的歌剧）

paras.en: But they are perhaps more at home in folk songs, in popular tales and in the ritual dramas of films.
paras.zh: 但它们放在民歌、通俗故事和电影这种仪式化的戏剧里，或许更为适得其所。

w.m: 在……中适得其所；在……中自在

paras.en: When we sit in the darkness of the cinema to watch the bold deeds of bandits like Ned Kelly we are caught up in admiration for their strong individuality, their simple gesture of protest, their passion for justice and their confidence that they cannot be beaten.
paras.zh: 当我们坐在漆黑的电影院里，观看内德·凯利这类盗匪的大胆事迹时，会沉浸在对他们的钦佩之中：钦佩他们鲜明的个性、简单的抗议姿态、对正义的热忱，以及认定自己不会被打败的那份自信。

paras.en: This sustains us nearly as much as it did the almost hopeless people from whom they sprang.
paras.zh: 这带给我们的支撑，几乎不亚于当年带给那些近乎绝望的百姓的支撑——盗匪正是从这些百姓中走出来的。

w.m: 几乎和……一样；几乎不亚于
adj. 绝望的；没有希望的

passages.name: 2018年 Passage One
passages.title: 澳大利亚招揽移民的努力与隐忧
passages.genre: 说明文 · 移民与社会
passages.summary: 澳大利亚人深知，没有大量移民进入劳动力队伍，经济就不太可能按设想的速度发展；加上失业率已经很低，政府急于吸引更多熟练劳动力。英国一直是主要的移民来源，意大利、希腊、德国等欧洲国家也提供了大量移民。欧洲大陆移民往往更难融入，而政府的目标是维持一个基本同质的社会，因此总体上仍然偏爱英国移民。但比各民族群体壮大更令人担忧的，是返回原籍国的移民越来越多；文中提到的回流原因包括流动性更强、经济状况、气候、思乡、孤独、房租高、职业资格难获认可以及当地人不友好等。

paras.en: “Britain’s best export,” I was told by the head of the Department of Immigration in Canberra, “is people.”
paras.zh: “英国最好的出口品，”堪培拉移民部的负责人对我说，“是人。”

paras.en: Close on 100,000 people have applied for assisted passages in the first five months of this year, and half of these are eventually expected to migrate to Australia.
paras.zh: 今年头五个月，已有近10万人申请了移民旅费资助，预计其中一半最终会移居澳大利亚。

paras.en: The Australians are delighted.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚人非常高兴。

paras.en: They are keenly aware that without a strong flow of immigrants into the workforce the development of the Australian economy is unlikely to proceed at the ambitious pace currently envisaged.
paras.zh: 他们深知，如果没有大批移民源源不断地进入劳动力队伍，澳大利亚经济就不太可能像目前雄心勃勃的设想那样高速发展。

w.m: adj. 雄心勃勃的；要求很高的

paras.en: The new mineral discoveries promise a splendid future, and the injection of huge amounts of American and British capital should help to ensure that they are properly exploited, but with unemployment in Australia down to less than 1.3 percent, the government is understandably anxious to attract more skilled labor.
paras.zh: 新发现的矿藏预示着辉煌的前景，大量美国和英国资本的注入也应该有助于确保这些矿藏得到妥善开发；但由于澳大利亚的失业率已降至不足1.3%，政府急于吸引更多熟练劳动力，也就在情理之中了。

w.m: adv. 可以理解地；理所当然地

paras.en: Australia is roughly the same size as the continental United States, but has only twelve million inhabitants.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚的面积与美国本土大致相当，但居民只有1200万。

paras.en: Migration has accounted for half the population increase in the last four years, and has contributed greatly to the country’s impressive economic development.
paras.zh: 过去四年里，人口增长有一半来自移民，移民还为这个国家令人瞩目的经济发展作出了巨大贡献。

w.m: adj. 令人瞩目的；令人印象深刻的

paras.en: Britain has always been the principal source—ninety percent of Australians are of British descent, and Britain has provided one million migrants since the Second World War.
paras.zh: 英国一直是主要来源——90%的澳大利亚人是英国后裔，第二次世界大战以来，英国已经输送了100万移民。

paras.en: Australia has also given great attention to recruiting people elsewhere.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚也十分重视从其他地方招募人员。

paras.en: Australians decided they had an excellent potential source of applicants among the so-called “guest workers” who have crossed their frontier to work in other parts of Europe.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚人认定，那些越过自己国家的边境、到欧洲其他地区打工的所谓“客籍工人”，是潜在申请人的绝佳来源。

paras.en: There were estimated to be more than four million of them, and a large number were offered subsidized passages and guaranteed jobs in Australia.
paras.zh: 据估计，这些人有400多万，澳方为其中很多人提供了旅费补贴，并保证他们在澳大利亚有工作。

w.m: adj. 有补贴的；受资助的
adj. 有保障的；得到保证的

paras.en: Italy has for some years been the second biggest source of migrants, and the Australians have also managed to attract a large number of Greeks and Germans.
paras.zh: 几年来，意大利一直是第二大移民来源国，澳大利亚人还设法吸引到了大量希腊人和德国人。

paras.en: One drawback with them, so far as the Australians are concerned, is that integration tends to be more difficult.
paras.zh: 就澳大利亚人而言，这些移民有一个缺点：他们往往更难融入。

paras.en: Unlike the British, continental migrants have to struggle with an unfamiliar language and new customs.
paras.zh: 与英国人不同，欧洲大陆移民不得不努力应对陌生的语言和新的习俗。

paras.en: Many naturally gravitate towards the Italian or Greek communities, which have grown up in cities such as Sydney and Melbourne.
paras.zh: 很多人自然而然地投奔意大利人或希腊人社区，这些社区已经在悉尼、墨尔本等城市发展起来。

paras.en: These colonies have their own newspapers, their own shops, and their own clubs.
paras.zh: 这些聚居地有自己的报纸、自己的商店和自己的俱乐部。

paras.en: Their inhabitants are not Australians, but Europeans.
paras.zh: 这些聚居地的居民不是澳大利亚人，而是欧洲人。

paras.en: The government’s avowed aim, however, is to maintain “a substantially homogeneous society into which newcomers, from whatever sources, will merge themselves.”
paras.zh: 然而，政府公开宣称的目标是维持“一个基本同质的社会，无论新来者来自何处，都将融入其中”。

w.m: adj. 公开宣称的；公开承认的
adj. 同质的；由同类成分组成的

paras.en: By and large, therefore, Australia still prefers British migrants, and tends to be rather less selective in their case than it is with others.
paras.zh: 因此，总的来说，澳大利亚仍然偏爱英国移民，对英国移民的挑选往往也比对其他移民宽松不少。

w.m: adj. 严格挑选的；有选择性的

paras.en: A far bigger cause of concern than the growth of national groups, however, is the increasing number of migrants who return to their countries of origin.
paras.zh: 然而，比各民族群体的壮大令人担忧得多的，是返回原籍国的移民人数日益增多。

w.m: adj. 越来越多的；日益增加的

paras.en: One reason is that people nowadays tend to be more mobile, and that it is easier than in the past to save the return fare, but economic conditions also have something to do with it.
paras.zh: 原因之一是，如今人们往往流动性更强，而且攒够回程路费也比过去容易了；不过，经济状况也与此有一定关系。

w.m: adj. （人）流动性强的；容易迁居的

paras.en: A slower rate of growth invariably produces discontent—and if this coincides with greater prosperity in Europe, a lot of people tend to feel that perhaps they were wrong to come here after all.
paras.zh: 增长速度一放慢，总会引起不满——如果这时又恰逢欧洲更加繁荣，很多人往往就会觉得，也许当初到这里来终究是错了。

paras.en: Several surveys have been conducted recently into the reason why people go home.
paras.zh: 最近已就人们回国的原因开展了几项调查。

paras.en: One noted that “flies, dirt, and outside lavatories” were on the list of complaints from British immigrants, and added that many people also complained about “the crudity, bad manners and unfriendliness of the Australians”.
paras.zh: 其中一项调查指出，“苍蝇、尘土和户外厕所”都在英国移民的抱怨清单上，还补充说，很多人也抱怨“澳大利亚人的粗俗、无礼和不友好”。

paras.en: Another survey gave climate conditions, homesickness, and “the stark appearance of the Australian countryside” as the main reasons for leaving.
paras.zh: 另一项调查把气候条件、思乡之情以及“澳大利亚乡间荒凉的景象”列为离开的主要原因。

w.m: v. 把……列为（give A as B：把 A 列为 B）

paras.en: Most British migrants miss council housing, the national health scheme, and their relatives and former neighbors.
paras.zh: 大多数英国移民都怀念市政公房、国民医疗保健制度，还有亲戚和以前的邻居。

paras.en: Loneliness is a big factor, especially among housewives.
paras.zh: 孤独是一大因素，在家庭主妇当中尤其如此。

paras.en: The men soon make new friends at work, but wives tend to find it much harder to get used to a different way of life.
paras.zh: 男人们很快就会在工作中交到新朋友，而妻子们往往会觉得，要适应另一种生活方式难得多。

paras.en: Many are housebound because of inadequate public transport in most outlying suburbs, and regular correspondence with their old friends at home only serves to increase their discontent.
paras.zh: 由于大多数偏远郊区的公共交通不够完善，她们当中许多人只能困在家里；而与国内老朋友定期通信，只会加深她们的不满。

w.m: adj. 困在家中的；出不了门的
结果只会；只会起到……作用

paras.en: One housewife was quoted recently as saying: “I even find I miss the people I used to hate at home.”
paras.zh: 最近有报道援引一位家庭主妇的话说：“我甚至发现，自己想念起了以前在老家讨厌的那些人。”

paras.en: Rents are high, and there are long waiting lists for Housing Commission homes.
paras.zh: 房租很高，住房委员会公房的轮候名单很长。

w.m: （澳大利亚州政府的）住房委员会

paras.en: Sickness can be an expensive business and the climate can be unexpectedly rough.
paras.zh: 生病可能是件很花钱的事，气候也可能出人意料地恶劣。

paras.en: The gap between Australian and British wage packets is no longer big, and people are generally expected to work harder here than they do at home.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚和英国的工资差距已经不大了，而且一般来说，人们在这里需要比在国内工作得更卖力。

paras.en: Professional men over forty often have difficulty in finding a decent job.
paras.zh: 四十岁以上的男性专业人士往往很难找到一份像样的工作。

w.m: adj. 专业的；从事专门职业的

paras.en: Above all, perhaps, skilled immigrants often find a considerable reluctance to accept their qualifications.
paras.zh: 也许最重要的是，有技能的移民常常发现，人们相当不愿意认可他们的职业资格。

paras.en: According to the journal Australian Manufacturer, the attitude of many employers and fellow workers is anything but friendly.
paras.zh: 据《澳大利亚制造商》杂志称，许多雇主和同事的态度一点也不友好。

paras.en: “We Australians,” it stated in a recent issue, “are just too fond of painting the rosy picture of the big, warm-hearted Aussie.
paras.zh: “我们澳大利亚人，”该杂志在最近一期中写道，“实在太喜欢把澳洲佬描绘成高大、热心肠的美好形象了。

paras.en: As a matter of fact, we are so busy blowing our own trumpets that we have not got time to be warm-hearted and considerate.
paras.zh: 事实上，我们忙着自吹自擂，忙得都没工夫热心待人、体贴别人了。

w.m: adj. 体贴的；考虑周到的

paras.en: Go down ‘heart-break alley’ among some of the migrants and find out just how expansive the Aussie is to his immigrants.”
paras.zh: 到一些移民当中去，走一走那条‘伤心巷’，看看澳洲佬对自己的移民究竟有多么热情豪爽吧。”

w.m: adj. 热情豪爽的；开朗健谈的

passages.name: 2018年 Passage Two
passages.title: 双语者为何换种语言感觉就不同
passages.genre: 议论文 · 语言与心理
passages.summary: 许多会说多种语言的人表示，说不同的语言时，自己会有不同的性格。作者认为，产生这种感觉有两个很充分的原因：大多数人两种语言的能力并不对称；对兼具两种文化背景的双语者来说，选用哪种语言本身就会产生强烈的启动效应。至于认为语法等语言内在特性会影响说话者性格的说法，作者持怀疑态度，指出这类说法都有把语言异域化的倾向，也与民族刻板印象有所重合；有人把希腊人爱打断别人归因于希腊语动词居首、承载大量信息，可世界上许多语言也是如此，威尔士语就是一例，威尔士人却并不以说话咄咄逼人著称。

paras.en: Some of the advantages of bilingualism include better performance at tasks involving “executive function” (which involves the brain’s ability to plan and prioritize), better defense against dementia in old age and—the obvious—the ability to speak a second language.
paras.zh: 双语能力的一些好处包括：在涉及“执行功能”（关乎大脑规划事务、分清主次的能力）的任务中表现更好；老年时更能抵御痴呆；还有显而易见的一点——会说第二语言。

w.m: n. 双语能力；使用双语
v. 排定优先次序；分清主次

paras.en: One purported advantage was not mentioned, though.
paras.zh: 不过，有一个所谓的好处并没有提到。

paras.en: Many multilinguals report different personalities, or even different worldviews, when they speak their different languages.
paras.zh: 许多会说多种语言的人表示，说不同的语言时，自己会有不同的性格，甚至不同的世界观。

w.m: n. 会说多种语言的人

paras.en: It’s an exciting notion, the idea that one’s very self could be broadened by the mastery of two or more languages.
paras.zh: 这是一个令人兴奋的观念：掌握两种或更多语言，可能会拓展一个人的自我本身。

paras.en: In obvious ways (exposure to new friends, literature and so forth) the self really is broadened.
paras.zh: 在一些显而易见的方面（接触新的朋友、文学等等），自我确实会得到拓展。

w.m: adj. 显而易见的；明显的

paras.en: Yet it is different to claim—as many people do—to have a different personality when using a different language.
paras.zh: 然而，像许多人那样，声称自己使用另一种语言时就有另一种性格，则是另一回事了。

paras.en: A former Economist colleague, for example, reported being ruder in Hebrew than in English.
paras.zh: 例如，《经济学人》的一位前同事就说，自己说希伯来语时比说英语时更粗鲁。

paras.en: So what is going on here?
paras.zh: 那么，这是怎么回事呢？

paras.en: Benjamin Lee Whorf, an American linguist who died in 1941, held that each language encodes a worldview that significantly influences its speakers.
paras.zh: 1941年去世的美国语言学家本杰明·李·沃尔夫认为，每种语言都蕴含着一种世界观，深刻影响着说这种语言的人。

w.m: 本杰明·李·沃尔夫（美国语言学家）

paras.en: Often called “Whorfianism”, this idea has its skeptics, including The Economist, which hosted a debate on the subject in 2010.
paras.zh: 这一观点常被称作“沃尔夫主义”，也不乏怀疑者，其中就包括《经济学人》——该刊曾在2010年就这一话题举办过一场辩论。

paras.en: But there are still good reasons to believe language shapes thought.
paras.zh: 但仍有充分的理由相信，语言会塑造思维。

paras.en: This influence is not necessarily linked to the vocabulary or grammar of a second language.
paras.zh: 这种影响未必与第二语言的词汇或语法有关。

paras.en: Significantly, most people are not symmetrically bilingual.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，大多数人的两种语言能力并不对称。

w.m: adv. 值得注意的是；重要的是
adj. 双语的；能说两种语言的

paras.en: Many have learned one language at home from parents, and another later in life, usually at school.
paras.zh: 许多人在家里跟父母学会了一种语言，后来又学了另一种，通常是在学校里学的。

w.m: 后来；在人生较晚的时候

paras.en: So bilinguals usually have different strengths and weaknesses in their different languages—and they are not always best in their first language.
paras.zh: 因此，双语者在不同的语言上通常各有长处和短处——而且他们并不总是在第一语言上表现最好。

paras.en: For example, when tested in a foreign language, people are less likely to fall into a cognitive trap (answering a test question with an obvious-seeming but wrong answer) than when tested in their native language.
paras.zh: 例如，与用母语接受测试相比，人们用外语接受测试时，落入认知陷阱（用一个看似显而易见、实则错误的答案来回答试题）的可能性更小。

paras.en: In part this is because working in a second language slows down the thinking.
paras.zh: 这在一定程度上是因为，用第二语言做事会让思考变慢。

paras.en: No wonder people feel different when speaking them.
paras.zh: 难怪人们说这些语言时会感觉不一样。

paras.en: And no wonder they feel looser, more spontaneous, perhaps more assertive or funnier or blunter, in the language they were reared in from childhood.
paras.zh: 也难怪他们说从小伴随自己长大的那种语言时，会觉得更放松、更随性，或许还更敢于表达自己、更风趣或更直率。

w.m: adj. 放松的；无拘无束的
adj. 坚定自信的；敢于表达自己的
adj. 直率的；直言不讳的
v. 抚养；养育（be reared in：在……中长大）

paras.en: What of “crib” bilinguals, raised in two languages?
paras.zh: 那么，在两种语言环境中长大的“摇篮”双语者又如何呢？

paras.en: Even they do not usually have perfectly symmetrical competence in their two languages.
paras.zh: 即便是他们，两种语言的能力通常也并不完全对称。

paras.en: But even for a speaker whose two languages are very nearly the same in ability, there is another big reason that person will feel different in the two languages.
paras.zh: 但即使一个人的两种语言能力几乎完全相同，也还有另一个重要原因，会让他说这两种语言时感觉不一样。

w.m: n. 说话者；说（某种语言）的人

paras.en: This is because there is an important distinction between bilingualism and biculturalism.
paras.zh: 这是因为双语能力和双文化背景之间有一个重要区别。

w.m: n. 双文化（背景）；兼具两种文化

paras.en: Many bilinguals are not bicultural.
paras.zh: 许多双语者并不兼具两种文化背景。

w.m: adj. 兼具两种文化（背景）的；双文化的

paras.en: But some are.
paras.zh: 但也有一些人兼具两种文化背景。

paras.en: And of those bicultural bilinguals, we should be little surprised that they feel different in their two languages.
paras.zh: 而这些兼具两种文化背景的双语者说这两种语言时感觉不一样，我们也就不必感到意外了。

w.m: adj. 兼具两种文化（背景）的；双文化的
adj. 感到意外的；惊讶的

paras.en: Experiments in psychology have shown the power of “priming”—small unnoticed factors that can affect behavior in big ways.
paras.zh: 心理学实验已经证明了“启动效应”的威力——未被察觉的微小因素可能会对行为产生重大影响。

w.m: adj. 未被注意的；未被察觉的

paras.en: Asking people to tell a happy story, for example, will put them in a better mood.
paras.zh: 例如，请人们讲一个快乐的故事，就会让他们心情变好。

w.h: put sb in a good mood

paras.en: The choice between two languages is a huge prime.
paras.zh: 选择两种语言中的哪一种，本身就是一个强大的启动因素。

w.m: n. 启动因素；启动刺激

paras.en: Speaking Spanish rather than English, for a bilingual and bicultural Puerto Rican in New York, might conjure feelings of family and home.
paras.zh: 对纽约一位兼通两种语言、兼具两种文化背景的波多黎各人来说，说西班牙语而不说英语，可能会唤起亲情和家的感觉。

w.m: adj. 双语的；能说两种语言的
adj. 兼具两种文化（背景）的；双文化的
v. 唤起；使浮现于脑海

paras.en: Switching to English might prime the same person to think of school and work.
paras.zh: 而改用英语，则可能会促使同一个人联想到学校和工作。

w.m: v. 启动；促使（想到某事）

paras.en: So there are two very good reasons (asymmetrical ability, and priming) that make people feel different speaking their different languages.
paras.zh: 因此，人们说不同的语言时之所以会感觉不一样，有两个非常充分的原因（语言能力不对称和启动效应）。

paras.en: We are still left with a third kind of argument, though.
paras.zh: 不过，我们还剩下第三类论点。

paras.en: An economist recently interviewed here at Prospero, Athanasia Chalari, said, for example: “Greeks are very loud and they interrupt each other very often.
paras.zh: 例如，本博客Prospero最近采访过的一位经济学家阿塔纳西娅·哈拉里就说：“希腊人说话嗓门很大，而且动不动就互相打断。

paras.en: The reason for that is the Greek grammar and syntax.
paras.zh: 原因就在于希腊语的语法和句法。

paras.en: When Greeks talk they begin their sentences with verbs and the form of the verb includes a lot of information so you already know what they are talking about after the first word and can interrupt more easily.”
paras.zh: 希腊人说话时，句子都以动词开头，而动词的形式包含了大量信息，所以听到第一个词，你就已经知道他们在说什么了，也就更容易打断他们。”

paras.en: Is there something intrinsic to the Greek language that encourages Greeks to interrupt?
paras.zh: 希腊语是否有某种内在的东西，促使希腊人去打断别人？

w.m: 促使某人做；鼓励某人做

paras.en: Consider Johnson skeptical.
paras.zh: 约翰逊（即本专栏作者）对此表示怀疑。

paras.en: People seem to enjoy telling tales about their languages’ inherent properties, and how they influence their speakers.
paras.zh: 人们似乎很喜欢讲一些故事，说自己的语言有哪些固有特性，这些特性又如何影响说这种语言的人。

w.m: n. 故事；（未必属实的）说法

paras.en: A group of French intellectual worthies once proposed, rather self-flatteringly, that French be the sole legal language of the EU, because of its supposedly unmatchable rigor and precision.
paras.zh: 一群法国知识界名流曾颇为自吹自擂地提议，让法语成为欧盟唯一的法律语言，理由是法语据说具有无与伦比的严谨性和精确性。

w.m: adj. 知识界的；知识分子的
n. 名流；要人（常含戏谑意味）
adv. 自我吹捧地；自吹自擂地

paras.en: Some Germans believe that frequently putting the verb at the end of a sentence makes the language especially logical.
paras.zh: 一些德国人认为，经常把动词放在句末，使得德语特别有逻辑性。

w.m: adj. 有逻辑性的；合乎逻辑的

paras.en: But language myths are not always self-flattering: many speakers think their languages are unusually illogical or difficult—witness the plethora of books along the lines of “Only in English do you park on a driveway and drive on a parkway; English must be the craziest language in the world!”
paras.zh: 但语言神话并不总是自我吹捧的：许多人觉得自己所说的语言格外不合逻辑或格外难——看看那些多得数不清、内容大致如下的书就知道了：“只有在英语里，你才会在driveway（私家车道）上park（停车），在parkway（林荫大道）上drive（开车）；英语一定是世界上最疯狂的语言！”

w.m: n. （流传甚广的）错误观念；神话
v. 可以……为证；看看……就知道
n. 林荫大道；景观大道

paras.en: What such pop-Whorfian stories share is a (natural) tendency to exoticize languages.
paras.zh: 这类通俗版沃尔夫主义故事的共同之处，在于都（自然而然地）倾向于把语言异域化。

w.m: adj. 通俗版沃尔夫主义的
v. 使异域化；赋予……异国情调

paras.en: We also see some unsurprising overlap with national stereotypes and self-stereotypes: French, rigorous; German, logical; English, playful.
paras.zh: 我们还看到，这些说法与民族刻板印象和自我刻板印象有一些重合，这并不令人意外：法语严谨，德语有逻辑，英语俏皮。

w.m: adj. 不足为奇的；不出所料的
adj. 有逻辑性的；合乎逻辑的
adj. 俏皮的；爱开玩笑的

paras.en: Of course.
paras.zh: 当然如此。

paras.en: In this case, Ms. Chalari, a scholar, at least proposed a specific and plausible line of causation from grammar to personality: in Greek, the verb comes first, and it carries a lot of information, hence easy interrupting.
paras.zh: 在这个例子中，学者哈拉里女士至少提出了一条从语法到性格的具体而说得通的因果链：在希腊语中，动词放在最前面，而且承载了大量信息，因此很容易打断别人。

w.m: 在这个例子中；在这种情况下
adj. 可信的；貌似合理的

paras.en: The problem is that many unrelated languages all around the world put the verb at the beginning of sentences.
paras.zh: 问题在于，世界各地有许多彼此没有亲缘关系的语言，都把动词放在句首。

w.m: adj. 没有亲缘关系的；无关的

paras.en: Many languages all around the world are heavily inflected, encoding lots of information in verbs.
paras.zh: 世界各地有许多语言屈折变化丰富，在动词里编码了大量信息。

w.m: adv. 高度地；在很大程度上
v. 编码；（以编码形式）承载

paras.en: It would be a striking finding if all of these unrelated languages had speakers more prone to interrupting each other.
paras.zh: 如果所有这些彼此没有亲缘关系的语言，其使用者都更容易互相打断，那将是一个惊人的发现。

w.m: adj. 惊人的；引人注目的
adj. 没有亲缘关系的；无关的

paras.en: Welsh, for example, is also both verb-first and about as heavily inflected as Greek, but the Welsh are not known as pushy conversationalists.
paras.zh: 例如，威尔士语也是动词居首，屈折变化的丰富程度也和希腊语差不多，但威尔士人并不以说话咄咄逼人著称。

w.m: adv. 高度地；在很大程度上
adj. 强势的；咄咄逼人的

passages.name: 2018年 Passage Three
passages.title: 初次求职的胆怯与挫折
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与经历
passages.summary: 一位从没找过工作的姑娘来到批发区求职，却因羞怯不敢进门，一路走过许多商号，两次走近门口都没敢进去。她终于犹犹豫豫地走进一家鞋业批发公司，一位老先生和气地告诉她眼下不需要人手，让她下周再来，这让她颇感意外，也多少受到了鼓舞。可在一家服装公司，迎上来的男人冷冷一问就让她勇气全无，被一口回绝后，她走出门去，没入人群，刚刚愉快起来的心情又遭到了沉重的打击。

paras.en: Once across the river and into the wholesale district, she glanced about her for some likely door at which to apply.
paras.zh: 一过河，进入批发区，她便四下张望，想找一扇看上去有希望的门，进去求职。

paras.en: As she contemplated the wide windows and imposing signs, she became conscious of being gazed upon and understood for what she was—a wage-seeker.
paras.zh: 她端详着那些宽大的橱窗和气派的招牌，意识到有人在注视她，而且看出了她的身份——一个找工作挣工钱的人。

w.h: understand sb for what they are

w.m: n. 找工作挣工钱的人；求职者

paras.en: She had never done this thing before, and lacked courage.
paras.zh: 她以前从没做过这种事，缺乏勇气。

paras.en: To avoid a certain indefinable shame she felt at being caught spying about for a position, she quickened her steps and assumed an air of indifference supposedly common to one upon an errand.
paras.zh: 被人撞见自己在到处探头探脑地找工作，她会感到某种说不清的羞耻；为了避开这种羞耻，她加快脚步，装出一副漠不关心的神气，想来出门办事的人通常都是这副样子。

w.m: adj. 说不清的；难以名状的
v. 撞见；发现（某人正在做某事）
四处窥探；探头探脑地打探
装出……的样子；摆出……的神气

paras.en: In this way she passed many manufacturing and wholesale houses without once glancing in.
paras.zh: 就这样，她走过了许多家制造厂商和批发商号，一次也没有朝里面瞥一眼。

paras.en: At last, after several blocks of walking, she felt that this would not do, and began to look about again, though without relaxing her pace.
paras.zh: 走了几个街区之后，她终于觉得这样下去不行，便又开始四处张望，只是脚步并没有放慢。

paras.en: A little way on she saw a great door which, for some reason, attracted her attention.
paras.zh: 再往前走了没多远，她看见一扇大门，不知为什么，这扇门引起了她的注意。

w.m: 不知为什么；出于某种原因

paras.en: It was ornamented by a small brass sign, and seemed to be the entrance to a vast hive of six or seven floors.
paras.zh: 门上饰有一块小小的黄铜招牌，看上去像是一座六七层高的巨大蜂巢的入口。

w.m: n. 蜂巢；（比喻）熙熙攘攘的地方

paras.en: “Perhaps,” she thought, “they may want someone,” and crossed over to enter.
paras.zh: “也许，”她心想，“他们会要人。”于是她走到街对面，准备进去。

paras.en: When she came within a score of feet of the desired goal, she saw through the window a young man in a grey checked suit.
paras.zh: 她走到离那个一心向往的目标不到二十英尺的地方，透过窗户看见一个身穿灰色格子西装的年轻人。

w.m: adj. 格子图案的；方格的

paras.en: That he had anything to do with the concern, she could not tell, but because he happened to be looking in her direction her weakening heart misgave her and she hurried by, too overcome with shame to enter.
paras.zh: 那人和这家商行有没有关系，她说不准；可是他恰好朝她这边望着，她那颗越来越虚的心便发起慌来，于是从门前匆匆走过，羞愧得进不了门。

w.m: adj. 越来越弱的；渐渐动摇的
（因某种情绪）不能自已；被……压垮

paras.en: Over the way stood a great six-story structure, labelled Storm and King, which she viewed with rising hope.
paras.zh: 街对面矗立着一座六层高的大楼，上面标着“斯托姆与金”，她望着这座楼，心中的希望越来越大。

w.m: adj. 越来越强的；上升的

paras.en: It was a wholesale dry goods concern and employed women.
paras.zh: 那是一家布匹批发商行，雇有女工。

paras.en: She could see them moving about now and then upon the upper floors.
paras.zh: 她不时能看见她们在楼上几层走来走去。

paras.en: This place she decided to enter, no matter what.
paras.zh: 这一家，她决定无论如何都要进去。

paras.en: She crossed over and walked directly toward the entrance.
paras.zh: 她走到街对面，径直朝入口走去。

paras.en: As she did so, two men came out and paused in the door.
paras.zh: 她正这样走着，有两个男人走了出来，在门口停住了脚。

paras.en: A telegraph messenger in blue dashed past her and up the few steps that led to the entrance and disappeared.
paras.zh: 一个身穿蓝衣的电报投递员从她身旁冲过，奔上通往入口的那几级台阶，不见了踪影。

paras.en: Several pedestrians out of the hurrying throng which filled the sidewalks passed about her as she paused, hesitating.
paras.zh: 人行道上挤满了匆匆赶路的人群，她停下脚步犹豫不决时，人群中有几个行人从她身旁绕了过去。

w.m: adj. 匆匆赶路的；匆忙的

paras.en: She looked helplessly around, and then, seeing herself observed, retreated.
paras.zh: 她无助地环顾四周，接着发觉有人在看自己，便退了回来。

w.m: adv. 无助地；无可奈何地

paras.en: It was too difficult a task.
paras.zh: 这件差事太难了。

w.m: （too + 形容词 + a + 名词）太……的一个

paras.en: She could not go past them.
paras.zh: 她没法从他们身边走过去。

paras.en: So severe a defeat told sadly upon her nerves.
paras.zh: 如此惨重的挫败，令她精神上大受打击。

w.m: （so + 形容词 + a + 名词）如此……的一个

paras.en: Her feet carried her mechanically forward, every foot of her progress being a satisfactory portion of a flight which she gladly made.
paras.zh: 她的双脚机械地带着她往前走；她很乐意这样逃开，每前进一英尺，都是这场逃离中令人满意的一段。

paras.en: Block after block passed by.
paras.zh: 一个又一个街区过去了。

paras.en: Upon streetlamps at the various corners she read names such as Madison, Monroe, La Salle, Clark, Dearborn, State, and still she went, her feet beginning to tire upon the broad stone flagging.
paras.zh: 在各个街角的路灯上，她看到麦迪逊街、门罗街、拉萨尔街、克拉克街、迪尔伯恩街、州街之类的街名，她仍旧往前走着，踩在宽阔的石板路上，双脚开始累了。

paras.en: She was pleased in part that the streets were bright and clean.
paras.zh: 街道明亮整洁，这让她多少有些高兴。

paras.en: The morning sun, shining down with steadily increasing warmth, made the shady side of the streets pleasantly cool.
paras.zh: 早晨的太阳照下来，热度不断增强，街道背阴的一侧便显得凉爽宜人。

w.m: adj. 不断增强的；越来越多的
adv. 宜人地；令人愉快地

paras.en: She looked at the blue sky overhead with more realization of its charm than had ever come to her before.
paras.zh: 她望着头顶的蓝天，比以往任何时候都更深切地领略到它的魅力。

paras.en: Her cowardice began to trouble her in a way.
paras.zh: 她开始为自己的怯懦感到几分不安了。

paras.en: She turned back, resolving to hunt up Storm and King and enter.
paras.zh: 她掉头往回走，决心找到斯托姆与金商行，走进去。

paras.en: On the way, she encountered a great wholesale shoe company, through the broad plate windows of which she saw an enclosed executive department, hidden by frosted glass.
paras.zh: 途中，她碰到一家很大的鞋业批发公司，透过宽大的平板玻璃窗，她看见里面隔出了一个经理部，用磨砂玻璃遮着。

paras.en: Without this enclosure, but just within the street entrance, sat a grey-haired gentleman at a small table, with a large open ledger before him.
paras.zh: 这个隔间外面，紧靠临街入口的里侧，一位头发花白的先生坐在一张小桌旁，面前摊着一本大账簿。

w.m: n. 隔间；围起来的地方

paras.en: She walked by this institution several times hesitating, but, finding herself unobserved, faltered past the screen door and stood humbly waiting.
paras.zh: 她在这家公司门前犹犹豫豫地走过好几回，后来发觉没人注意自己，便迟迟疑疑地走进纱门，谦恭地站着等候。

w.m: 发觉自己（处于某种状态）
adj. 没人注意的；未被看见的
adv. 谦恭地；低声下气地

paras.en: “Well, young lady,” observed the old gentleman, looking at her somewhat kindly, “what is it you wish?”
paras.zh: “嗯，姑娘，”老先生说道，带着几分和善看着她，“你想办什么事？”

paras.en: “I am, that is, do you—I mean, do you need any help?” she stammered.
paras.zh: “我是，也就是说，你们是不是——我是说，你们需要人手吗？”她结结巴巴地说。

paras.en: “Not just at present,” he answered smiling.
paras.zh: “眼下还不需要，”他笑着回答。

paras.en: “Not just at present.
paras.zh: “眼下还不需要。

paras.en: Come in sometime next week.
paras.zh: 下周什么时候再来吧。

paras.en: Occasionally we need someone.”
paras.zh: 我们有时会需要人的。”

paras.en: She received the answer in silence and backed awkwardly out.
paras.zh: 她一声不吭地听完这个答复，局促地退了出去。

paras.en: The pleasant nature of her reception rather astonished her.
paras.zh: 人家接待她时态度这样和气，倒让她颇为吃惊。

w.m: adj. 和气的；令人愉快的

paras.en: She had expected that it would be more difficult, that something cold and harsh would be said—she knew not what.
paras.zh: 她原以为会更难，以为人家会说些冷冰冰、严厉的话——至于说什么，她也不知道。

paras.en: That she had not been put to shame and made to feel her unfortunate position, seemed remarkable.
paras.zh: 人家既没有让她难堪，也没有让她觉得自己处境不幸，这似乎很不寻常。

paras.en: Somewhat encouraged, she ventured into another large structure.
paras.zh: 她多少受到了些鼓舞，便大着胆子走进了另一座大楼。

w.m: adj. 受到鼓舞的；更有信心的
大着胆子进入；冒险进入

paras.en: It was a clothing company, and more people were in evidence—well-dressed men of forty and more, surrounded by brass railings.
paras.zh: 那是一家服装公司，里面看得见的人更多——都是些衣着考究、四十岁往上的男人，四周围着黄铜栏杆。

paras.en: An office boy approached her.
paras.zh: 一个办公室勤杂工朝她走了过来。

paras.en: “Who is it you wish to see?” he asked.
paras.zh: “你想见谁？”他问。

paras.en: “I want to see the manager,” she returned.
paras.zh: “我想见经理，”她答道。

paras.en: He ran away and spoke to one of a group of three men who were conferring together.
paras.zh: 他跑开了，那边有三个男人正聚在一起商议事情，他过去跟其中一个说了话。

paras.en: One of these came towards her.
paras.zh: 其中一个朝她走了过来。

paras.en: “Well?” he said coldly.
paras.zh: “什么事？”他冷冷地说。

paras.en: The greeting drove all courage from her at once.
paras.zh: 这一声招呼，一下子把她的勇气全赶跑了。

paras.en: “Do you need any help?” she stammered.
paras.zh: “你们需要人手吗？”她结结巴巴地问。

paras.en: “No,” he replied abruptly, and turned upon his heel.
paras.zh: “不需要，”他生硬地回答，转身就走。

w.m: 转身就走；猛然转身离开

paras.en: She went foolishly out, the office boy deferentially swinging the door for her, and gladly sank into the obscuring crowd.
paras.zh: 她傻乎乎地走了出去，那个勤杂工毕恭毕敬地替她推开门；她庆幸地没入人群，人群遮住了她的身影。

w.m: adv. 毕恭毕敬地；恭敬地
adj. 遮掩的；使人看不清的

paras.en: It was a severe setback to her recently pleased mental state.
paras.zh: 这对她刚刚愉快起来的心情是一次严重的打击。

passages.name: 2017年 Passage One
passages.title: 阿连特茹：静谧乡野与鲜为人知的海岸
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 旅行与自然
passages.summary: 作者六月带着儿子在葡萄牙阿连特茹地区旅行了两周，一路上游人稀少。这里生活节奏缓慢，到此旅行就像回到了四五十年前。作者认为，从阿连特茹延伸到阿尔加维的一段100公里长的海岸线是全欧洲最壮美的，却似乎鲜为人知，部分是因为交通不便，部分则与海滩边缺少住处有关。他们住在内陆一座偏僻的庄园里，或在庄园里散步，或去海边游玩、品尝新鲜海鲜，享受这里的自然与宁静。

paras.en: It’s 7pm on a balmy Saturday night in June, and I have just ordered my first beer in I Cervejaria, a restaurant in Zambujeira do Mar, one of the prettiest villages on Portugal’s south-west coast.
paras.zh: 现在是六月一个和暖的周六晚上7点，我刚在I Cervejaria餐馆点了第一杯啤酒，这家餐馆位于赞布热拉杜马尔，那是葡萄牙西南海岸最漂亮的村庄之一。

w.m: adj. （天气）温和宜人的；和煦的

paras.en: The place is empty, but this doesn’t surprise me at all.
paras.zh: 店里空荡荡的，不过我一点也不意外。

paras.en: I have spent two weeks in this area, driving along empty roads, playing with my son on empty beaches, and staying in B&Bs where we are the only guests.
paras.zh: 我已经在这一带待了两个星期，开车行驶在空荡荡的公路上，和儿子在空无一人的海滩上玩耍，住的民宿里也只有我们这一拨客人。

w.m: n. 提供住宿和早餐的家庭旅馆；民宿

paras.en: No doubt the restaurant, run by two brothers for the past 28 years, is buzzing in July and August, when Portuguese holidaymakers descend on the Alentejo coast.
paras.zh: 七、八月间，葡萄牙的度假者纷纷涌向阿连特茹海岸，那时这家由两兄弟经营了28年的餐馆想必热闹非凡。

w.m: v. （地方）热闹非凡；熙熙攘攘

paras.en: But for the other 10 months of the year, the trickle of diners who come to feast on fantastically fresh seafood reflects the general pace of life in the Alentejo: sleepy, bordering on comatose.
paras.zh: 但在一年中其余的10个月里，只有零零星星的食客来这里大啖新鲜至极的海鲜，这反映出阿连特茹总体的生活节奏：昏昏欲睡，近乎昏迷。

w.m: n. 稀稀落落的人（或物）；涓涓细流
adj. 昏昏欲睡的；（地方）冷清的
adj. 昏迷的；不省人事的

paras.en: One of the poorest, least-developed, least-populated regions in western Europe, the Alentejo has been dubbed both the Provence and the Tuscany of Portugal.
paras.zh: 阿连特茹是西欧最贫穷、最不发达、人口最稀少的地区之一，它既被称作“葡萄牙的普罗旺斯”，也被称作“葡萄牙的托斯卡纳”。

paras.en: Neither is accurate.
paras.zh: 这两种说法都不准确。

paras.en: Its scenery is not as pretty and, apart from in the capital Evora, its food isn’t as sophisticated.
paras.zh: 这里的风景不如那两处秀美；除了首府埃武拉，这里的饮食也不如那两处讲究。

paras.en: The charms of this land of wheatfields, cork oak forests, wildflower meadows and tiny white-washed villages are more subtle than in France’s or Italy’s poster regions.
paras.zh: 这片土地上有麦田、栓皮栎林、开满野花的草甸，还有一座座刷成白色的小村庄；与法国或意大利那些招牌地区相比，这里的魅力更为含蓄。

w.m: adj. 含蓄的；不易察觉的
n. 海报；（作定语）招牌式的

paras.en: To travel here is to step back in time 40 or 50 years.
paras.zh: 到这里旅行，就如同让时光倒流四五十年。

paras.en: Life rolls along at a treacly pace; there’s an unnerving stillness to the landscape.
paras.zh: 这里的日子过得像糖浆流淌一般缓慢；四下的景致透着一种令人心慌的寂静。

w.m: （平稳缓慢地）向前推进；（日子）一天天过去
adj. 糖浆般（黏稠缓慢）的
（there is A to B）B 带有 A（这种特点或气氛）
adj. 令人不安的；使人心慌的

paras.en: But that stillness ends abruptly at the Atlantic Ocean, where there is drama in spades.
paras.zh: 但这份寂静到了大西洋边便戛然而止，那里有的是动人心魄的景象。

w.m: n. 激动人心的场面；戏剧性

paras.en: Protected by the South West Alentejo and Costa Vicentina national park, the 100km of coastline from Porto Covo in the Alentejo to Burgau in the Algarve is the most stunning in Europe.
paras.zh: 从阿连特茹的波尔图科武到阿尔加维的布尔高，这100公里海岸线受西南阿连特茹与维森蒂娜海岸国家公园保护，是全欧洲最壮美的海岸线。

w.m: adj. 令人惊艳的；极美的

paras.en: And yet few people seem to know about it.
paras.zh: 可是，似乎很少有人知道这段海岸。

paras.en: Walkers come to admire the views from the Fisherman’s Way, surfers to ride the best waves in Europe, but day after day we had spectacular beaches to ourselves.
paras.zh: 徒步者来这里，在渔夫小径上欣赏风景；冲浪者来这里，驾驭欧洲最好的海浪；可我们日复一日独享着一片片壮观的海滩。

paras.en: The lack of awareness is partly a matter of accessibility (these beaches are a good two hours’ drive from either Faro or Lisbon airports) and partly to do with a lack of beachside accommodation.
paras.zh: 这段海岸鲜为人知，部分是因为交通不便（这些海滩无论离法鲁机场还是里斯本机场，都有足足两个小时的车程），部分则与海滩边缺少住处有关。

w.m: n. 可达性；交通便利程度
adj. （用于数量前）足足的；整整的

paras.en: There are some gorgeous, independent guesthouses in this area (see below), but they are hidden in valleys or at the end of dirt tracks.
paras.zh: 这一带有一些独立经营的精美小旅馆（见下文），但都藏在山谷里或土路尽头。

w.m: adj. 精美的；非常漂亮的
adj. 独立经营的；独立的

paras.en: Our base was Herdade da Nespereira, a beautiful 600-acre estate of uncultivated land covered in rock-rose, eucalyptus and wild flowers 13km inland from Zambujeira.
paras.zh: 我们的落脚点是内斯佩雷拉庄园，这座美丽的庄园占地600英亩，位于赞布热拉往内陆13公里处，土地未经开垦，长满了岩蔷薇、桉树和野花。

w.m: adj. 未开垦的；未耕作的

paras.en: Our one-bedroom home, Azenha, was once home to the miller who tended the now-restored watermill next to it.
paras.zh: 我们住的是一套一居室的房子，名叫阿泽尼亚，从前是磨坊主的家；当年他照看的那座水磨坊就在旁边，如今已经修复。

w.m: adj. 一居室的；只有一间卧室的

paras.en: A kilometre away from the main house, pool and restaurant, it is gloriously isolated.
paras.zh: 小屋离主楼、泳池和餐厅有一公里远，偏僻得妙不可言。

w.m: adv. 极好地；令人愉快地
adj. 偏僻的；与世隔绝的

paras.en: If Julian Assange ever leaves the Ecuadorian embassy in London, I suggest he hotfoots it to an Alentejo hideaway.
paras.zh: 要是朱利安·阿桑奇哪天离开了厄瓜多尔驻伦敦大使馆，我建议他火速赶往阿连特茹的某个藏身之所。

w.m: adv. （用于条件句）在任何时候；哪天

paras.en: He’d be safe for months.
paras.zh: 在那里他好几个月都会安然无恙。

w.m: adj. 安全的；安然无恙的

paras.en: Stepping out of the house in the morning to greet our neighbours—wild horses on one side, donkeys on the other—with nothing but birdsong filling the air, I felt a sense of adventure you normally only get with wild camping.
paras.zh: 清晨走出屋子，跟邻居们打个招呼——一边是野马，另一边是驴——空中回荡的只有鸟鸣，我体会到一种通常只有野外露营时才有的冒险感。

w.m: （声音、气味等）弥漫在空中；回荡在空中
野外露营（不在营地内的露营）

paras.en: “When people first arrive, they feel a little anxious wondering what they are going to do the whole time,” Sarah Gredley, the English owner of Nespereira, told me.
paras.zh: “大家刚来的时候，会有点焦虑，不知道待在这儿的这段时间里都要干些什么。”内斯佩雷拉庄园的主人、英国人萨拉·格雷德利对我说。

paras.en: “But it doesn’t usually take them long to realise that the whole point of being here is to slow down, to enjoy nature.”
paras.zh: “不过，他们通常用不了多久就会明白，待在这里的全部意义就在于放慢脚步，享受大自然。”

w.m: 某人花很长时间（才）做某事

paras.en: We followed her advice, walking down to the stream in search of terrapins and otters, or through clusters of cork oak trees, their branches hairy with lichen like the ancient trees of a fairytale forest.
paras.zh: 我们听从她的建议，或是往下走到小溪边，寻找水龟和水獭，或是穿过一丛丛栓皮栎，枝条上长满地衣，毛茸茸的，宛如童话森林里的古树。

w.m: n. 童话；（作定语）童话中的

paras.en: On some days, we tramped uphill to the windmill, now a romantic house for two, for panoramic views across the estate and beyond.
paras.zh: 有几天，我们一路跋涉上坡，走到风车磨坊——如今那里是一座供两人入住的浪漫小屋——去饱览整个庄园乃至更远处的全景。

w.m: v. 步履沉重地走；长途跋涉

paras.en: When we ventured out, we were always drawn back to the coast—the gentle sands and shallow bay of Farol beach close to Vila Nova de Milfontes, the rock pools of Almograve or the cove at Carvalhal.
paras.zh: 每次出门探索，我们总会被吸引回海边：新米尔丰特斯附近的法罗尔海滩，沙滩平缓，海湾水浅；阿尔莫格拉维的礁石潮池；或者卡尔瓦利亚尔的小海湾。

paras.en: At the end of the day, we would head, sandy-footed, to the nearest restaurant, knowing that at every one there would be a cabinet full of fresh seafood to choose from—bass, bream, salmon, lobster, prawns, crabs, goose barnacles, clams … We never ate the same thing twice.
paras.zh: 一天下来，我们会带着满脚的沙子去最近的餐馆，心里知道每一家都会有满满一柜新鲜海鲜供人挑选——鲈鱼、鲷鱼、三文鱼、龙虾、大虾、螃蟹、鹅颈藤壶、蛤蜊……我们从来没有吃过重样的菜。

w.h: at the end of the day
w.m: 一天结束时（此处为字面意思）

paras.en: A kilometre or so from I Cervejaria, on Zambujeira’s idyllic natural harbour is O Sacas, originally built to feed the fishermen but now popular with everyone.
paras.zh: 距离I Cervejaria一公里左右，在赞布热拉田园诗般的天然港湾边，坐落着O Sacas餐馆；它最初是为了给渔民供应饭食而建的，如今却深受大家欢迎。

w.m: adj. 田园诗般的；宁静优美的

paras.en: After scarfing platefuls of seafood on the terrace, we wandered down to the harbour where two fishermen, kitted out in wetsuits, were setting out by boat across the clear turquoise water to collect goose barnacles.
paras.zh: 在露台上狼吞虎咽地吃完一盘又一盘海鲜后，我们信步走到港湾边，那里有两个身穿潜水服的渔民正乘船出发，要穿过清澈的碧绿海水去采鹅颈藤壶。

w.m: adj. 绿松石色的；碧绿的

paras.en: Other than them, the place was deserted—just another empty beauty spot where I wondered for the hundredth time that week how this pristine stretch of coast has remained so undiscovered.
paras.zh: 除了他们，那里空无一人——又是一处空荡荡的美景胜地；在这里，那一周里我第一百次纳闷：这段原始纯净的海岸怎么至今仍如此鲜为人知。

w.m: adj. 空无一人的；荒无人烟的
风景胜地；风景优美的地方
第一百次（极言次数之多）
adj. 原始的；未受污染的
adj. 未被发现的；鲜为人知的

passages.name: 2017年 Passage Two
passages.title: 拓展阅读教学：让学生成为创造性读者
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与阅读
passages.summary: 作者回顾十年前的情形：大多数英语教师对教育部的拓展阅读挑战不以为然，这项工作只是走走过场。作者与英国文化协会葡萄牙分部、葡萄牙教师协会APPI一起，以三条原则为出发点（人人都是讲故事的人；阅读与写作一样可以是创造性的过程；要让学生作为真正意义上的读者投入阅读），形成了一种新方法：最重视读前活动，以供教师自行取舍的“套件”形式提供材料，并用后续活动把阅读与教学大纲的要求联系起来。作者认为，这种创造性阅读能让学生比以前更接近语言，形成有效得多的学习互动，但一些教师会因看似失去控制而感到受到威胁。

paras.en: I can still remember the faces when I suggested a method of dealing with what most teachers of English considered one of their pet horrors, extended reading.
paras.zh: 我至今还记得自己提出一种方法来应对拓展阅读时大家脸上的表情——大多数英语教师都把拓展阅读视为自己最头疼的事情之一。

paras.en: The room was full of tired teachers, and many were quite cynical about the offer to work together to create a new and dynamic approach to the place of stories in the classroom.
paras.zh: 屋里满是疲惫的教师，许多人对这项提议相当怀疑：大家一起合作，开创一种全新而富有活力的方法，来看待故事在课堂上的地位。

w.m: adj. 怀疑的；愤世嫉俗的
adj. 富有活力的；充满生气的

paras.en: They had seen promises come and go, and mere words weren’t going to convince them, which was a shame as it was mere words that we were principally dealing with.
paras.zh: 他们见惯了各种承诺许下又落空，光凭言辞是说服不了他们的。这就可惜了，因为我们主要打交道的恰恰只是言辞。

paras.en: Most teachers were unimpressed by the extended reading challenge from the Ministry, and their lack of enthusiasm for the rather dry list of suggested tales was passed on to their students and everyone was pleased when that part of the syllabus was over.
paras.zh: 大多数教师对教育部提出的拓展阅读挑战不以为然；那份推荐故事的书目相当枯燥，他们对此缺乏热情，这种情绪也传给了学生；等教学大纲里这一部分结束了，人人都很高兴。

w.m: adj. 不以为然的；无动于衷的
n. （政府的）部；此处指教育部

paras.en: It was simply a box-ticking exercise.
paras.zh: 那只不过是一件打钩了事、走走过场的差事。

w.m: adj. 打钩了事的；走过场的
n. （有特定目的的）活动；差事

paras.en: We needed to do something more.
paras.zh: 我们需要再多做点什么。

paras.en: We needed a very different approach.
paras.zh: 我们需要一种截然不同的方法。

paras.en: That was ten years ago.
paras.zh: 那是十年前的事了。

paras.en: Now we have a different approach, and it works.
paras.zh: 如今我们有了一种不同的方法，而且很管用。

paras.en: Here’s how it happened.
paras.zh: 下面就讲讲事情的经过。

w.m: 下面就是……的经过；事情是这样的

paras.en: (Or, as with most good stories, here are the main parts.
paras.zh: （或者说，就像大多数好故事一样，下面是其中的主要部分。

paras.en: You have to fill in some of it yourself, employing that underused classroom device, the imagination.)
paras.zh: 有些内容你得自己补全，运用想象力——这个在课堂上未得到充分利用的手段。）

paras.en: We—that is, the British Council in Portugal and the Portuguese teachers’ association APPI—started with three main precepts:
paras.zh: 我们——也就是英国文化协会葡萄牙分部和葡萄牙教师协会APPI——从三条主要原则出发：

paras.en: First, it is important to realise that all of us are storytellers, tellers of tales.
paras.zh: 第一，重要的是要认识到，我们所有人都是讲故事的人，都是故事的讲述者。

paras.en: We all have our own narratives—the real stories such as what happened to us this morning or last night, and the ones we have been told by others and we haven’t experienced personally.
paras.zh: 我们每个人都有自己的叙事：既有真实的故事，比如今天早上或昨晚我们身上发生了什么；也有别人讲给我们听、我们并未亲身经历过的故事。

paras.en: We could say that our entire lives are constructed as narratives.
paras.zh: 可以说，我们的整个人生都是以叙事的形式构建起来的。

paras.en: As a result, we all understand and instinctively feel narrative structure.
paras.zh: 因此，我们都理解叙事结构，也能本能地感知它。

paras.en: Binary opposites—for example, the tension created between good and bad together with the resolution of that tension through the intervention of time, resourcefulness and virtue—is a concept understood by even the youngest children.
paras.zh: 二元对立——例如善与恶之间产生的张力，以及这种张力借助时间、机智和美德的介入而得到化解——是一个连最小的孩子都理解的概念。

paras.en: Professor Kieran Egan, in his seminal book ‘Teaching as Story Telling’, warns us not to ignore this innate skill, for it is a remarkable tool for learning.
paras.zh: 基兰·伊根教授在其影响深远的著作《教学即讲故事》中告诫我们，不要忽视这种与生俱来的技能，因为它是一种非凡的学习工具。

w.m: adj. 影响深远的；开创性的
adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: We need to understand that writing and reading are two sides of the same coin: an author has not completed the task if the book is not read: the creative circle is not complete without the reader, who will supply their own creative input to the process.
paras.zh: 我们需要明白，写作和阅读是一枚硬币的两面：书如果没人读，作者就没有完成任务；没有读者，创作的循环就不完整，读者会为这一过程作出自己的创造性贡献。

w.h: two sides of the same coin
w.m: 一枚硬币的两面；一体两面
n. 循环；环（周而复始的过程）

paras.en: Samuel Johnson said: ‘A writer only begins a book.
paras.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊说过：“作者只是开了一本书的头，

w.m: 塞缪尔·约翰逊（英国作家、词典编纂者）

paras.en: A reader finishes it.’
paras.zh: 读者则把它完成。”

paras.en: In teaching terms, we often forget that reading itself can be a creative process, just as writing is, and we too often relegate it to a means of data collection.
paras.zh: 从教学的角度来说，我们常常忘记，阅读本身也可以是一个创造性的过程，就像写作一样；而且我们动不动就把阅读降格为收集资料的手段。

paras.en: We frequently forget to make that distinction when presenting narratives or poetry, and often ask comprehension questions which relate to factual information—who said what and when, rather than speculating on ‘why’, for example, or examining the context of the action.
paras.zh: 我们在讲授叙事作品或诗歌时，经常忘了做这种区分，而且常常提一些涉及事实信息的理解题——谁在什么时候说了什么，而不是去推测诸如“为什么”之类的问题，或者审视情节发生的背景。

paras.en: The third part of the reasoning that we adopted relates to the need to engage the students as readers in their own right, not simply as language learners; learning the language is part of the process, not the reason for reading.
paras.zh: 我们所采纳的思路，第三部分涉及的是：需要让学生作为真正意义上的读者投入阅读，而不仅仅是作为语言学习者；学习语言是这一过程的一部分，而不是阅读的理由。

w.m: v. 吸引（某人）参与；使投入
凭自身的资格；本身就是

paras.en: What they read must become theirs and have its own special and secret life in their heads, a place where teachers can only go if invited.
paras.zh: 学生读的东西必须变成他们自己的，在他们的脑海中拥有自己独特而隐秘的生命；那是教师只有受到邀请才能进入的地方。

paras.en: We quickly found that one of the most important ways of making all the foregoing happen was to engage the creative talents of the class before they read a word of the text.
paras.zh: 我们很快发现，要让上述一切得以实现，最重要的途径之一，就是在全班学生连文本的一个字都还没读的时候，就调动起他们的创造才能。

w.m: n. 上述内容；前面提到的事

paras.en: The pre-reading activities become the most important part of the teaching process; the actual reading part can almost be seen as the icing on the cake, and the principal aim of pre-reading activities is to get students to want to read the text.
paras.zh: 读前活动成为教学过程中最重要的部分；实际阅读的部分几乎可以看作锦上添花，而读前活动的主要目的是让学生想要阅读文本。

w.m: 锦上添花；（蛋糕上的）糖霜

paras.en: We developed a series of activities which use clues or fragments from the text yet to be read, and which rely on the student’s innate knowledge of narrative, so that they can build their own stories before they read the key text.
paras.zh: 我们设计了一系列活动，这些活动利用待读文本中的线索或片段，并依靠学生天生具备的叙事知识，好让他们在阅读核心文本之前构建出自己的故事。

w.m: adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: They have enough information to generate ideas but not so much that it becomes simply an exercise in guided writing; releasing a free imagination is the objective.
paras.zh: 他们得到的信息足以激发想法，但又不至于多到让活动变成单纯的引导式写作练习；目标是释放自由的想象力。

w.m: adj. 有指导的；引导式的

paras.en: Moving from pre-reading to reading, we may introduce textual intervention activities.
paras.zh: 从读前阶段进入阅读阶段后，我们可能会引入文本干预活动。

paras.en: ‘Textual Intervention’ is a term used by Rob Pope to describe the process of questioning a text not simply as a guide to comprehension but as a way of exploring the context of the story at any one time, and examining points at which the narrative presents choices, points of divergence, or narrative crossroads.
paras.zh: “文本干预”是罗布·波普使用的一个术语，用来描述这样一个过程：对文本提出疑问，不仅仅把提问当作理解的指引，更把它当作一种方式，借以探究故事在任一时刻的背景，审视叙事在哪些节点上呈现出选择、分岔点或叙事的十字路口。

paras.en: We don’t do this for all texts, however, as the shorter ones do not seem to gain much from this process and it simply breaks up the reading pleasure.
paras.zh: 不过，我们并不是对所有文本都这样做，因为较短的文本似乎从这一过程中获益不多，而且这样做只会破坏阅读的乐趣。

paras.en: Follow-up activities are needed, at the least, to round off the activity, to bring some sense of closure, but they also offer an opportunity to link the reading experience more directly to the requirements of the syllabus.
paras.zh: 需要有后续活动，最起码用来给活动收尾，带来某种完结感；不过，后续活动还提供了一个机会，能把阅读体验更直接地同教学大纲的要求联系起来。

paras.en: Indeed, the story may have been chosen in the first place because the context supports one of the themes that teachers are required to examine as part of the syllabus—for example, ‘families’, ‘science and technology’, ‘communications’, ‘the environment’ and all the other familiar themes.
paras.zh: 事实上，当初选择这个故事，可能就是因为它的背景契合教学大纲中要求教师探讨的某个主题——比如“家庭”“科学技术”“交流”“环境”以及其他所有熟悉的主题。

paras.en: There are very few stories that can be explored without some part of the syllabus being supported.
paras.zh: 能够拿来探讨、却又不配合教学大纲任何部分的故事少之又少。

paras.en: For many teachers this is an essential requirement if they are to engage in such extensive reading at all.
paras.zh: 对许多教师来说，这是一项必不可少的要求，不然他们根本不会去开展这样的泛读。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；必要的
（用于条件句，加强语气）真的；（否定时）根本

paras.en: The whole process—pre-, while- and post-reading—could be just an hour’s activity, or it could last for more than one lesson.
paras.zh: 整个过程——读前、读中和读后——可能只是一个小时的活动，也可能持续不止一节课。

paras.en: When we are designing the materials for exploring stories, clearly it isn’t possible for us to know how much time any teacher will have available, which is why we construct the activities into a series of independent units which we call kits.
paras.zh: 我们在设计探讨故事的材料时，显然无法知道任何一位教师会有多少时间可用，正因如此，我们把这些活动编排成一系列独立的单元，并称之为套件。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此

paras.en: They are called kits because we expect teachers to build their own lessons out of the materials we provide, which implies that large amounts may be discarded.
paras.zh: 之所以称为套件，是因为我们希望教师用我们提供的材料搭建自己的课，这就意味着可能会有大量材料被舍弃。

paras.en: What we do ask, though, is that the pre-reading activities be included, if nothing else.
paras.zh: 不过，我们确实有一个要求：哪怕别的都不用，也要把读前活动包括进去。

paras.en: That is essential for the process to engage the student as a creative reader.
paras.zh: 要让这一过程吸引学生作为创造性的读者投入阅读，读前活动必不可少。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；必要的

paras.en: One of the purposes of encouraging a creative reading approach in the language classroom is to do with the dynamics we perceive in the classroom.
paras.zh: 在语言课堂上提倡创造性阅读方法，目的之一与我们在课堂上感知到的互动关系有关。

paras.en: Strategic theorists tell us of the social trinity, whereby three elements are required to achieve a dynamic in any social situation.
paras.zh: 战略理论家向我们介绍了社会三位一体：在任何社会情境中，都需要三个要素才能形成互动。

paras.en: In the language classroom these might be seen as consisting of the student, the teacher and the language.
paras.zh: 在语言课堂上，这三个要素或许可以看作由学生、教师和语言构成。

paras.en: Certainly from the perspective of the student—and usually from the perspective of the teacher—the relationship is an unequal one, with the language being perceived as placed closer to the teacher than the student.
paras.zh: 无疑，从学生的角度看——而且通常从教师的角度看也是如此——这种关系是不平等的：在他们看来，语言离教师比离学生更近。

paras.en: This will result in less dynamic between language and student than between language and teacher.
paras.zh: 这会导致语言与学生之间的互动少于语言与教师之间的互动。

paras.en: However, if we replace ‘language’ with ‘narrative’ and especially if that is approached as a creative process that draws the student in so that they feel they ‘own’ the relationship with the text, then this will shift the dynamic in the classroom so that the student, who has now become a reader, is much closer to the language—or narrative—than previously.
paras.zh: 然而，如果我们把“语言”换成“叙事”，尤其是如果把叙事当作一个创造性的过程来对待，吸引学生投入其中，让他们觉得与文本之间的关系“属于”自己，那么这就会改变课堂上的互动，让此时已成为读者的学生比以前离语言——或者说叙事——近得多。

paras.en: This creates a much more effective dynamic of learning.
paras.zh: 这就形成了一种有效得多的学习互动。

paras.en: However, some teachers feel threatened by this apparent loss of overall control and mastery.
paras.zh: 然而，这看上去意味着教师失去了对全局的控制和主导，一些教师因此感到受到了威胁。

paras.en: Indeed, the whole business of open-ended creativity and a lack of boxes to tick for the correct answer is quite unsettling territory for some to find themselves in.
paras.zh: 事实上，开放式的创造，再加上没有方框可以给正确答案打钩，这一整套做法会让一些人觉得自己置身于一片相当令人不安的领域。

w.m: adj. 开放式的；无固定答案的
n. 创造性；创造力（此处指创造性的活动）

passages.name: 2017年 Passage Three
passages.title: 以国民服役化解城市动荡
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与政策
passages.summary: 作者认为，洛杉矶骚乱提醒人们：除非美国致力于推行各项计划，帮助城市贫困人口过上有所作为、体面的生活，否则将继续付出社会和族群动荡的高昂代价。作者主张推行类似军事训练的国民服役计划，利用现有的军事基地和设施，培养少数族裔青年的纪律意识和技能，为他们提供第一份工作，使他们与社会重新联系起来。作者呼吁两党放下成见，果断行动，预防今后的城市动荡。

paras.en: Once again, seething, residual anger has burst forth in an American city.
paras.zh: 郁积未消、翻腾不已的怒火，又一次在一座美国城市爆发了。

w.m: adj. 翻腾的；（怒火）郁积的

paras.en: And the riots that overtook Los Angeles were a reminder of what knowledgeable observers have been saying for a quarter-century.
paras.zh: 而席卷洛杉矶的这场骚乱，让人想起见多识广的观察人士二十五年来一直在说的话。

w.m: n. 提醒；使人想起……的事物
adj. 见多识广的；知识渊博的
n. 二十五年；四分之一世纪

paras.en: America will continue paying a high price in civil and ethnic unrest unless the nation commits itself to programs that help the urban poor lead productive and respectable lives.
paras.zh: 除非美国致力于推行各项计划，帮助城市贫困人口过上有所作为、体面的生活，否则就将继续付出社会和族群动荡的高昂代价。

w.m: adj. 有所作为的；富有成效的
adj. 体面的；值得尊敬的

paras.en: Once again, a proven program is worth pondering: national service.
paras.zh: 有一项行之有效的计划再次值得认真斟酌：国民服役。

w.m: adj. 经过验证的；行之有效的

paras.en: Somewhat akin to the military training that generations of American males received in the armed forces, a 1990s version would prepare thousands of unemployable and undereducated young adults for quality lives in our increasingly global and technology-driven economy.
paras.zh: 20世纪90年代版的国民服役有点类似于一代代美国男性在军队中接受的军事训练，它将让成千上万无法就业、受教育不足的年轻人做好准备，以便在我们这个日益全球化、由技术驱动的经济中过上高质量的生活。

w.m: adj. 无法就业的；不适合雇用的

paras.en: National service opportunities would be available to any who needed it and, make no mistake, the problems are now so structural, so intractable, that any solution will require massive federal intervention.
paras.zh: 国民服役的机会将向一切有需要的人开放；而且，毫无疑问，如今这些问题已是如此根深蒂固的结构性问题，又如此棘手，以至于任何解决办法都将需要联邦政府大规模干预。

w.m: adj. 结构性的；结构上的
adj. 难以解决的；棘手的

paras.en: In his much-quoted book, “The Truly Disadvantaged,” sociologist William Julius Wilson wrote that “only a major program of economic reform” will prevent the riot-prone urban underclass from being permanently locked out of American economic life.
paras.zh: 社会学家威廉·朱利叶斯·威尔逊在其广为引用的著作《真正的穷人》中写道，“只有一项重大的经济改革计划”才能防止容易发生骚乱的城市底层阶级被永远排斥在美国经济生活之外。

w.m: adj. 处境不利的；贫困的
n. 底层阶级；下层社会
被排斥在……之外；被关在……外面

paras.en: Today, we simply have no choice; the enemy within and among our separate ethnic selves is as daunting as any foreign foe.
paras.zh: 如今，我们根本别无选择；敌人就在我们各自隔绝的族群内部和族群之间，和任何外敌一样令人生畏。

w.m: adj. 令人生畏的；使人畏缩的

paras.en: Families who are rent apart by welfare dependency, job discrimination and intense feelings of alienation have produced minority teenagers with very little self-discipline and little faith that good grades and the American work ethic will pay off.
paras.zh: 因依赖福利、就业歧视和强烈的疏离感而四分五裂的家庭，造就了一批自律能力极差的少数族裔青少年，他们也几乎不相信好成绩和美国式的敬业精神会有回报。

w.m: 被撕裂；四分五裂（rent 是 rend 的过去分词）
n. 少数族裔；少数民族

paras.en: A military-like environment for them with practical domestic objectives could produce startling results.
paras.zh: 为他们提供一种类似军队、有着切实国内目标的环境，可能会产生惊人的效果。

w.m: adj. 惊人的；令人吃惊的

paras.en: Military service has been the most successful career-training program we’ve ever known, and American children born in the years since the all-volunteer Army was instituted make up a large proportion of this targeted group.
paras.zh: 兵役一直是我们迄今所知最成功的职业培训计划；而自陆军实行全志愿兵役制以来出生的美国孩子，在这一目标群体中占了很大比例。

w.m: adj. 全志愿兵制的；全部由志愿者组成的
adj. 作为目标的；目标的

paras.en: But this opportunity may disappear forever if too many of our military bases are summarily closed and converted or sold to the private sector.
paras.zh: 但如果我们有太多军事基地被草草关闭、改作他用或卖给私营部门，这个机会就可能永远消失。

paras.en: The facilities, manpower, traditions, and capacity are already in place.
paras.zh: 设施、人力、传统和能力都已经到位。

paras.en: Don’t dismantle it: rechannel it.
paras.zh: 不要拆掉它，而要给它改换用途。

w.m: v. 改变……的用途；使改道

paras.en: Discipline is a cornerstone of any responsible citizen’s life.
paras.zh: 对任何一个负责任的公民来说，纪律都是其生活的基石。

paras.en: I was taught it by my father, who was a policeman.
paras.zh: 我父亲是一名警察，是他教会了我守纪律。

paras.en: Many of the rioters have never had any at all.
paras.zh: 许多参与骚乱的人从来就没有过一丁点纪律。

paras.en: As an athlete and former Army officer, I know that discipline can be learned.
paras.zh: 作为一名运动员和前陆军军官，我知道纪律是可以学会的。

paras.en: More importantly, it must be learned or it doesn’t take hold.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，纪律必须靠学习得来，否则就扎不下根。

paras.en: A precedent for this approach was the Civilian Conservation Corps that worked so well during the Great Depression.
paras.zh: 这种做法有一个先例，那就是大萧条时期成效卓著的民间资源保护队。

w.m: 民间资源保护队（美国罗斯福新政时期的就业项目）

paras.en: My father enlisted in the CCC as a young man with an elementary school education and he learned invaluable skills that served him well throughout his life.
paras.zh: 我父亲加入民间资源保护队时，还是个小学文化程度的年轻人；他在那里学到了极其宝贵的技能，这些技能让他终身受益。

w.m: n. 教育；（受教育的）程度
对某人很有用；使某人受益

paras.en: The key was that a job was waiting for him when he finished.
paras.zh: 关键在于，他结业时就有一份工作在等着他。

paras.en: The certainty of that first entry-level position is essential if severely alienated young minority men and women are to keep the faith.
paras.zh: 要让严重疏离社会的少数族裔青年男女保持信念，就必须确保他们一定能得到那第一份入门级的工作。

w.m: adj. 至关重要的；必不可少的
n. 少数族裔；少数民族

paras.en: We all know these are difficult times for the public sector, but here’s a chance to add energetic and able manpower to America’s workforce.
paras.zh: 我们都知道，如今公共部门正处于困难时期，但眼前就有一个机会，可以为美国的劳动力队伍增添精力充沛、能干的人手。

paras.en: They could be prepared for the world of work or college—an offer similar to that made to returning GIs after World War II.
paras.zh: 他们可以为进入职场或上大学做好准备——这和第二次世界大战后向归来的美国大兵提供的机会相似。

paras.en: It would be a chance for 16- to 21-year-olds to live among other cultures, religions and races and in different geographical areas.
paras.zh: 这将让16岁到21岁的年轻人有机会生活在其他文化、宗教和种族的人群之中，生活在不同的地区。

paras.en: And these young people could be taught to rally around common goals and friendships that evolve out of pride in one’s squad, platoon, company, battalion—or commander.
paras.zh: 而且还可以教会这些年轻人围绕共同的目标和友谊团结起来，这些目标和友谊源于对自己所在的班、排、连、营，或是对指挥官的自豪感。

w.m: 团结在……周围；围绕……团结起来

paras.en: We saw such images during the Persian Gulf War and during the NCAA Final Four basketball games.
paras.zh: 我们在海湾战争期间和NCAA篮球联赛四强赛期间都看到过这样的画面。

w.m: （美国大学篮球联赛的）四强赛

paras.en: In military life and competitive sports, this camaraderie doesn’t just happen; it is taught and learned in an atmosphere of discipline and earned mutual respect for others’ capabilities.
paras.zh: 在军队生活和竞技体育中，这种同袍情谊不会自然而然地产生，而是在纪律严明、彼此凭能力赢得尊重的氛围中教出来、学出来的。

w.m: n. 同袍情谊；同志情谊

paras.en: A national service program would also help overcome two damaging perceptions held by America’s disaffected youth: that society just doesn’t care about minority youngsters and that one’s personal best efforts will not be rewarded in our discriminatory job market.
paras.zh: 国民服役计划还将有助于消除美国心怀不满的年轻人所持有的两种有害看法：一是社会根本不关心少数族裔青少年，二是在我们这个充满歧视的就业市场中，个人竭尽全力也不会得到回报。

w.m: adj. 心怀不满的；离心离德的
n. 少数族裔；少数民族

paras.en: Harvard professor Robert Reich’s research has shown that urban social ills are so pervasive that the upper 20 percent of Americans—that “fortunate fifth” as he calls them—have decided quietly to “secede” from the bottom four-fifths in particular.
paras.zh: 哈佛大学教授罗伯特·赖克的研究表明，城市社会弊病已普遍到这样的地步：最上层20%的美国人——他称之为“幸运的五分之一”——已经悄悄决定，尤其要“脱离”底层的五分之四。

w.m: adj. 普遍的；无处不在的
v. 脱离；退出（组织、国家等）

paras.en: We cannot accept such estrangement on a permanent basis.
paras.zh: 我们不能接受这种隔阂永远存在下去。

paras.en: And what better way to answer skeptics from any group than by certifying the technical skill of graduates from a national service training program?
paras.zh: 而要回应任何群体中的怀疑者，还有什么办法比认证国民服役培训计划结业学员的技术技能更好呢？

w.m: 还有什么比……更好的办法

paras.en: Now, we must act decisively to forestall future urban unrest.
paras.zh: 现在，我们必须果断行动，预防今后的城市动荡。

paras.en: Republicans must put aside their aversion to funding programs aimed at certain cultural groups.
paras.zh: 有些计划以特定文化群体为对象，共和党人必须抛开对资助这类计划的反感。

paras.en: Democrats must forget labels and recognize that a geographically isolated subgroup of Americans—their children in particular—needs systematic and substantive assistance for at least another 20 years.
paras.zh: 民主党人必须抛开标签，认识到有一部分美国人在地理上处于孤立状态，他们——尤其是他们的孩子——至少还需要20年系统而实质性的援助。

w.m: n. 子群体；（大群体中的）一部分人

paras.en: The ethnic taproots of minority Americans are deeply buried in a soil of faith and loyalty to traditional values.
paras.zh: 少数族裔美国人的族群之根，深深埋在信仰和忠于传统价值观的土壤里。

w.m: n. 少数族裔；少数民族

paras.en: With its emphasis on discipline, teamwork, conflict resolution, personal responsibility and marketable skills development, national service can provide that vital first job that will reconnect these Americans to the rest of us.
paras.zh: 国民服役注重纪律、团队合作、化解冲突、个人责任以及培养有市场需求的技能，能提供那至关重要的第一份工作，让这些美国人与我们其余的人重新联系起来。

w.m: adj. 有市场需求的；适销对路的

paras.en: Let’s do it now before the fire next time.
paras.zh: 让我们现在就行动起来，赶在下一场烈火燃起之前。

w.m: 下一场烈火（化用鲍德温的书名《下一次将是烈火》，喻指再次爆发的骚乱）

passages.name: 2016年 Passage One
passages.title: 盖茨比府上的夏夜狂欢
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 文学与社会
passages.summary: 叙述者描写了邻居盖茨比夏夜在家中举办的奢华派对：宾客往来不绝，美酒佳肴、乐队彩灯一应俱全，夜色渐深，场面越发喧闹。来客大多并未受到邀请，而是自己找上门来，有时连主人都没见到就走了。叙述者是少数真正受邀的客人之一，到场后却打听不到主人的行踪，只好悄悄走到鸡尾酒桌那边。

paras.en: There was music from my neighbor’s house through the summer nights.
paras.zh: 整个夏天，每到夜里，我邻居家都有音乐声传出。

paras.en: In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars.
paras.zh: 在他那蓝色的花园里，男人和姑娘们像飞蛾一样来来往往，穿行于窃窃私语、香槟美酒和点点星光之间。

paras.en: At high tide in the afternoon I watched his guests diving from the tower of his raft, or taking the sun on the hot sand of his beach while his two motor-boats slit the waters of the Sound, drawing aquaplanes (滑水板) over cataracts of foam.
paras.zh: 下午涨潮时，我看着他的客人从他浮台的跳台上跳水，或是躺在他那片海滩灼热的沙子上晒太阳，而他的两艘汽艇则划破海峡的水面，拖着滑水板掠过瀑布般翻腾的白沫。

paras.en: On week-ends his Rolls-Royce became an omnibus, bearing parties to and from the city between nine in the morning and long past midnight, while his station wagon scampered like a brisk yellow bug to meet all trains.
paras.zh: 每逢周末，他的劳斯莱斯就成了公共汽车，从早上九点直到午夜过后很久，把一拨拨客人从城里接来，又送回城里；而他的旅行车则像一只轻快的黄色甲虫，一溜小跑地去接每一班火车。

w.m: n. 公共汽车；公共马车
v. 蹦蹦跳跳地跑；奔跑

paras.en: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes and hammers and garden-shears, repairing the ravages of the night before.
paras.zh: 而每逢星期一，八个仆人，包括一个临时加雇的园丁，就拿着拖把、板刷、锤子和园艺剪辛苦劳作一整天，收拾前一夜留下的一片狼藉。

w.m: adj. 额外的；临时加雇的

paras.en: Every Friday five crates of oranges and lemons arrived from a fruiterer in New York—every Monday these same oranges and lemons left his back door in a pyramid of pulpless halves.
paras.zh: 每个星期五，都有五箱橙子和柠檬从纽约一家水果店送来；每个星期一，还是这些橙子和柠檬，却已成了一个个没有果肉的半边果皮，堆成金字塔，从他家后门运出去。

w.m: n. 金字塔形的一堆；金字塔

paras.en: There was a machine in the kitchen which could extract the juice of two hundred oranges in half an hour if a little button was pressed two hundred times by a butler’s thumb.
paras.zh: 厨房里有一台机器，只要男管家用大拇指把一个小按钮按上两百下，半小时内就能榨出两百个橙子的汁。

paras.en: At least once a fortnight a corps of caterers came down with several hundred feet of canvas and enough colored lights to make a Christmas tree of Gatsby’s enormous garden.
paras.zh: 一队承办宴席的人至少每两个星期来一趟，带着几百英尺长的帆布，还有许许多多的彩灯，足以把盖茨比偌大的花园装点成一棵圣诞树。

paras.en: On buffet tables, garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre (冷盘), spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold.
paras.zh: 自助餐桌上点缀着晶莹发亮的冷盘，香料烤火腿与花色斑斓的色拉、酥皮小猪和仿佛被施了魔法、变成深金色的火鸡挤在一起。

w.m: adj. 五颜六色的；杂色的
n. 酥皮点心；油酥面团
v. 施魔法于；（像施了魔法般）使变成

paras.en: In the main hall a bar with a real brass rail was set up, and stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials (加香甜酒) so long forgotten that most of his female guests were too young to know one from another.
paras.zh: 正厅里设了一个酒吧，配有真正的黄铜栏杆，备有各种杜松子酒和烈酒，还有一些被人遗忘已久的加香甜酒，久到他的女宾大多年纪太轻，分不清哪种是哪种。

paras.en: By seven o’clock the orchestra has arrived, no thin five-piece affair, but a whole pitful of oboes and trombones and saxophones and viols and cornets and piccolos, and low and high drums.
paras.zh: 到七点钟，乐队已经来了——不是什么单薄的五人小乐队，而是整整一乐池的双簧管、长号、萨克斯管、维奥尔琴、短号、短笛，还有低音鼓和高音鼓。

w.m: n. 维奥尔琴（一种古提琴）

paras.en: The last swimmers have come in from the beach now and are dressing up-stairs; the cars from New York are parked five deep in the drive, and already the halls and salons and verandas are gaudy with primary colors, and hair shorn in strange new ways, and shawls beyond the dreams of Castile.
paras.zh: 最后一批游泳的人这时已经从海滩回来，正在楼上换衣服；从纽约来的汽车在车道上停了五排，各处厅堂、客厅和游廊里已是一片花哨艳丽：满眼的原色，剪成新奇古怪样式的头发，还有连卡斯蒂利亚人做梦也想不到的披肩。

w.m: 超乎……的梦想；……做梦也想不到

paras.en: The bar is in full swing, and floating rounds of cocktails permeate the garden outside, until the air is alive with chatter and laughter, and casual innuendo and introductions forgotten on the spot, and enthusiastic meetings between women who never knew each other’s names.
paras.zh: 酒吧里正热闹非凡，一巡巡飘来荡去的鸡尾酒弥漫到外面的花园，直到空气里充满了闲谈和笑声，充满了随口而出的影射之词、当场就忘的介绍，还有女人们热情洋溢的相见——她们从来不知道彼此的姓名。

w.m: adj. 飘来飘去的；流动的
adj. 随意的；漫不经心的

paras.en: The lights grow brighter as the earth lurches away from the sun, and now the orchestra is playing yellow cocktail music, and the opera of voices pitches a key higher.
paras.zh: 随着大地踉跄着背离太阳，灯光越来越亮，此刻乐队正演奏着金黄色调的鸡尾酒会音乐，人声交织的歌剧也升高了一个调。

w.m: v. （声音）定在某一音高；定调

paras.en: Laughter is easier minute by minute, spilled with prodigality, tipped out at a cheerful word.
paras.zh: 笑声一分钟比一分钟来得容易，毫不吝惜地泼洒出来，只消一句欢快的话，便倾泻而出。

w.m: 一分钟比一分钟；每分每秒
adj. 欢快的；令人高兴的

paras.en: The groups change more swiftly, swell with new arrivals, dissolve and form in the same breath; already there are wanderers, confident girls who weave here and there among the stouter and more stable, become for a sharp, joyous moment the centre of a group, and then, excited with triumph, glide on through the sea-change of faces and voices and color under the constantly changing light.
paras.zh: 一群群人变换得更快了，新客一到就壮大起来，转眼间散而复聚；已经有人在四处游荡——那些自信的姑娘在较为壮实、稳当的人中间穿来穿去，有那么鲜明而欢快的一刻成了一群人的中心，接着又因得胜而兴奋不已，在不断变幻的灯光下，继续翩然滑过千变万化的面孔、声音和色彩。

paras.en: Suddenly one of these gypsies, in trembling opal, seizes a cocktail out of the air, dumps it down for courage and, moving her hands like Frisco, dances out alone on the canvas platform.
paras.zh: 突然，这些吉卜赛女郎中的一位，穿着一袭颤动的蛋白石色衣裙，凌空抓过一杯鸡尾酒，一口灌下去壮壮胆，然后像弗里斯科那样舞动着双手，独自跳着舞走上帆布舞台。

w.m: n. 吉卜赛人；（喻）四处漂泊的人
n. 蛋白石；蛋白石色（的衣裙）

paras.en: A momentary hush; the orchestra leader varies his rhythm obligingly for her, and there is a burst of chatter as the erroneous news goes around that she is Gilda Gray’s understudy from the Follies.
paras.zh: 片刻的寂静；乐队指挥殷勤地为她变换了节奏；一个错误的消息四处传开，说她是《富丽秀》歌舞团里吉尔达·格雷的替补演员，人群中随之爆发出一阵七嘴八舌的议论。

w.m: adv. 乐于助人地；殷勤地
n. 七嘴八舌的议论；闲谈
n. 替补演员；候补演员

paras.en: The party has begun.
paras.zh: 派对开始了。

paras.en: I believe that on the first night I went to Gatsby’s house I was one of the few guests who had actually been invited.
paras.zh: 我相信，第一次去盖茨比家的那天晚上，我是少数几个真正受到邀请的客人之一。

paras.en: People were not invited—they went there.
paras.zh: 人们并没有受到邀请——他们就那么去了。

paras.en: They got into automobiles which bore them out to Long Island, and somehow they ended up at Gatsby’s door.
paras.zh: 他们坐进汽车，汽车把他们载到长岛，不知怎么的，他们最后就到了盖茨比的家门口。

paras.en: Once there they were introduced by somebody who knew Gatsby, and after that they conducted themselves according to the rules of behavior associated with amusement parks.
paras.zh: 一到那里，就有某个认识盖茨比的人替他们作个介绍，此后他们的一举一动就按游乐园里的那一套行为规矩来。

paras.en: Sometimes they came and went without having met Gatsby at all, came for the party with a simplicity of heart that was its own ticket of admission.
paras.zh: 有时他们来了又走，压根儿没见到盖茨比；他们怀着一颗单纯的心奔着派对而来，这份单纯本身就是入场券。

paras.en: I had been actually invited.
paras.zh: 我倒是真正受到了邀请的。

paras.en: A chauffeur in a uniform of robin’s-egg blue crossed my lawn early that Saturday morning with a surprisingly formal note from his employer: the honor would be entirely Gatsby’s, it said, if I would attend his “little party” that night.
paras.zh: 那个星期六一大早，一个身穿知更鸟蛋青色制服的司机穿过我家的草坪，送来他雇主的一封短笺，正式得出人意料：上面说，如果我能光临他当晚的“小小派对”，那将完全是盖茨比的荣幸。

w.m: 知更鸟蛋青色；淡蓝绿色

paras.en: He had seen me several times, and had intended to call on me long before, but a peculiar combination of circumstances had prevented it—signed Jay Gatsby, in a majestic hand.
paras.zh: 他见过我好几次，早就打算登门拜访，只是种种情况奇特地凑在一起，使他未能如愿——落款是杰伊·盖茨比，笔迹庄严堂皇。

paras.en: Dressed up in white flannels I went over to his lawn a little after seven, and wandered around rather ill at ease among swirls and eddies of people I didn’t know—though here and there was a face I had noticed on the commuting train.
paras.zh: 我穿上一身白色法兰绒衣裤，打扮得整整齐齐，七点刚过就到他的草坪上去了，在一圈圈打着旋儿、流来涌去的陌生人群中四处走动，颇有些局促不安——不过，零零星星也有几张我在通勤火车上留意过的面孔。

w.m: n. 法兰绒；（复数）法兰绒衣裤

paras.en: I was immediately struck by the number of young Englishmen dotted about; all well dressed, all looking a little hungry, and all talking in low, earnest voices to solid and prosperous Americans.
paras.zh: 散布在各处的年轻英国人之多，一下子就让我吃了一惊；他们个个衣着考究，个个都带着几分饿相，也个个都在低声恳切地同殷实富足的美国人交谈。

w.m: 对……感到吃惊；对……印象深刻

paras.en: I was sure that they were selling something: bonds or insurance or automobiles.
paras.zh: 我敢肯定，他们是在推销什么东西：债券、保险或者汽车。

paras.en: They were at least agonizingly aware of the easy money in the vicinity and convinced that it was theirs for a few words in the right key.
paras.zh: 他们至少都焦灼地意识到，近旁就有唾手可得的钱，并且深信只要用恰到好处的调子说上几句，这钱就归他们了。

w.m: adv. 痛苦地；令人焦灼地

paras.en: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host, but the two or three people of whom I asked his whereabouts stared at me in such an amazed way, and denied so vehemently any knowledge of his movements, that I slunk off in the direction of the cocktail table—the only place in the garden where a single man could linger without looking purposeless and alone.
paras.zh: 我一到就设法寻找主人，可我向两三个人打听他在哪里，他们都那样惊愕地瞪着我，又那样激烈地否认知道他的行踪，弄得我只好悄悄溜到鸡尾酒桌那边去——整个花园里，只有在那儿，一个独自前来的男子才可以逗留下去，而不显得无所事事、孤零零的。

w.m: adj. 单独的；独自一人的
adj. 无目的的；无所事事的

passages.name: 2016年 Passage Two
passages.title: 网络空间的安全威胁与应对
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与安全
passages.summary: “网络空间”一词由科幻作家威廉·吉布森创造，如今泛指把互联网带给全世界数十亿人的各种基础设施，它给人们带来了巨大的好处，却也有阴暗的一面：数据泄露事件规模越来越大、越来越常见，网络犯罪和网上工业间谍活动迅速增长，此外还存在网络破坏的风险。保障网络空间的安全很难，因为互联网的架构是为促进互联互通而设计的，并不是为了安全；总的来说，现有防御措施的效果还算不错，但这项任务正变得越来越难。本报道将主要关注网络犯罪和网络间谍活动，并论证可以采取一些办法让每个人更安全，例如做好网络安全的基本功、提供激励措施。网络空间即将随着物联网经历又一次巨变，这也是促使科技公司更优先考虑安全的又一个理由。

paras.en: The term “cyberspace” was coined by William Gibson, a science-fiction writer.
paras.zh: “网络空间”一词是由科幻作家威廉·吉布森创造的。

paras.en: He first used it in a short story in 1982, and expanded on it a couple of years later in a novel, “Neuromancer”, whose main character, Henry Dorsett Case, is a troubled computer hacker and drug addict.
paras.zh: 他于1982年在一篇短篇小说中首次使用这个词，两年后又在长篇小说《神经漫游者》中对它作了进一步阐述；这部小说的主人公亨利·多塞特·凯斯是一个麻烦缠身的电脑黑客兼瘾君子。

w.m: n. 《神经漫游者》（吉布森的科幻小说）
adj. 麻烦缠身的；苦恼的

paras.en: In the book Mr. Gibson describes cyberspace as “a consensual hallucination experienced daily by billions of legitimate operators” and “a graphic representation of data abstracted from the banks of every computer in the human system.”
paras.zh: 吉布森在书中把网络空间描述为“数十亿合法操作者每天都在体验的一种共识幻觉”和“数据的图形化表示，这些数据抽取自人类系统中每一台电脑的存储库”。

w.m: adj. 共识的；经各方同意的

paras.en: His literary creation turned out to be remarkably prescient (有先见之明的).
paras.zh: 事实证明，他的这一文学创造有着惊人的先见之明。

paras.en: Cyberspace has become shorthand for the computing devices, networks, fibre-optic cables, wireless links and other infrastructure that bring the internet to billions of people around the world.
paras.zh: 网络空间已成为一个简称，泛指把互联网带给全世界数十亿人的计算设备、网络、光纤电缆、无线链路及其他基础设施。

paras.en: The myriad connections forged by these technologies have brought tremendous benefits to everyone who uses the web to tap into humanity’s collective store of knowledge every day.
paras.zh: 这些技术建立起的无数连接，给每天借助网络从人类集体知识宝库中汲取知识的所有人都带来了巨大的好处。

paras.en: But there is a darker side to this extraordinary invention.
paras.zh: 但这项非凡的发明也有其阴暗的一面。

paras.en: Data breaches are becoming ever bigger and more common.
paras.zh: 数据泄露事件规模越来越大，也越来越常见。

w.m: adv. （与比较级连用）越来越；愈加
