paras.en: Last year over 800m records were lost, mainly through such attacks.
paras.zh: 去年有超过8亿条记录丢失，主要是由于这类攻击。

paras.en: Among the most prominent recent victims has been Target, whose chief executive, Gregg Steinhafel, stood down from his job in May, a few months after the giant American retailer revealed that online intruders had stolen millions of digital records about its customers, including credit- and debit-card details.
paras.zh: 近来最引人注目的受害者之一是塔吉特公司：这家美国零售业巨头披露，网络入侵者窃取了数以百万计的客户数字记录，其中包括信用卡和借记卡的详细信息；几个月后，该公司首席执行官格雷格·斯坦哈菲尔于5月辞去了职务。

w.m: adj. 引人注目的；著名的
adj. 巨型的；（企业）巨头的
n. 信用（此处 credit- 指 credit-card 信用卡）

paras.en: Other well-known firms such as Adobe, a tech company, and eBay, an online marketplace, have also been hit.
paras.zh: 其他知名公司，比如科技公司Adobe和网上交易平台eBay，也遭到了攻击。

w.m: n. 易贝（美国网上交易平台）

paras.en: The potential damage, though, extends well beyond such commercial incursions.
paras.zh: 不过，潜在的危害远远超出了这类商业入侵的范围。

paras.en: Wider concerns have been raised by the revelations made by Edward Snowden, a contractor to America’s National Security Agency (NSA), about the mass surveillance carried out by Western intelligence agencies, as well as by the growing numbers of cyber-warriors being recruited by countries that see cyberspace as a new domain of warfare.
paras.zh: 美国国家安全局（NSA）的合同工爱德华·斯诺登披露了西方情报机构实施的大规模监控，而那些把网络空间视为新作战领域的国家正在招募越来越多的网络战士，这两方面都引发了更广泛的担忧。

w.m: adj. 越来越多的；日益增长的

paras.en: America’s president, Barack Obama, said in a White House press release earlier this year that cyberthreats “pose one of the gravest national-security dangers” the country is facing.
paras.zh: 美国总统巴拉克·奥巴马今年早些时候在一份白宫新闻稿中称，网络威胁“构成了”美国当前面临的“最严重的国家安全危险之一”。

paras.en: Securing cyberspace is hard because the architecture of the internet was designed to promote connectivity, not security.
paras.zh: 保障网络空间的安全很难，因为互联网的架构是为促进互联互通而设计的，并不是为了安全。

paras.en: Its founders focused on getting it to work and did not worry much about threats because the network was affiliated with America’s military.
paras.zh: 互联网的创建者们专注于让它运转起来，并不怎么担心威胁，因为这个网络隶属于美国军方。

paras.en: As hackers turned up, layers of security, from antivirus programs to firewalls, were added to try to keep them at bay.
paras.zh: 随着黑客陆续出现，人们加上了一层又一层安全防护，从杀毒程序到防火墙，试图把黑客挡在门外。

paras.en: Gartner, a research firm, reckons that last year organisations around the globe spent $67 billion on information security.
paras.zh: 研究公司高德纳估计，去年全球各机构在信息安全上花了670亿美元。

w.m: n. 高德纳（美国信息技术研究与咨询公司）

paras.en: On the whole, these defences have worked reasonably well.
paras.zh: 总的来说，这些防御措施的效果一直还算不错。

paras.en: For all the talk about the risk of a “cyber 9/11” or a “cybergeddon”, the internet has proved remarkably resilient.
paras.zh: 尽管人们大谈发生“网络9·11”或“网络末日”的风险，事实证明，互联网的韧性出奇地强。

w.m: n. 网络末日；网络大灾难
adj. 有韧性的；恢复力强的

paras.en: Hundreds of millions of people turn on their computers every day and bank online, shop at virtual stores, swap gossip and photos with their friends on social networks and send all kinds of sensitive data over the web without ill effect.
paras.zh: 每天都有数以亿计的人打开电脑，在网上办理银行业务、在虚拟商店购物、在社交网络上与朋友交换八卦和照片，并通过网络发送各种敏感数据，都没有受到不良影响。

paras.en: Companies and governments are shifting ever more services online.
paras.zh: 企业和政府正把越来越多的服务转移到网上。

paras.en: But the task is becoming harder.
paras.zh: 但保障网络空间安全这项任务正变得越来越难。

paras.en: Cyber-security, which involves protecting both data and people, is facing multiple threats, notably cybercrime and online industrial espionage, both of which are growing rapidly.
paras.zh: 网络安全既涉及保护数据，也涉及保护人，目前正面临多重威胁，尤其是网络犯罪和网上工业间谍活动，两者都在迅速增长。

paras.en: A recent estimate by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), a think-tank, puts the annual global cost of digital crime and intellectual-property theft at $445 billion—a sum roughly equivalent to the GDP of a smallish rich European country such as Austria.
paras.zh: 智库战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）最近估计，数字犯罪和知识产权盗窃每年给全球造成的损失为4450亿美元，这一数额大致相当于奥地利这类规模偏小的欧洲富国的国内生产总值。

paras.en: To add to the worries, there is also the risk of cyber-sabotage.
paras.zh: 更令人担忧的是，还存在网络破坏的风险。

paras.en: Terrorists or agents of hostile powers could mount attacks on companies and systems that control vital parts of an economy, including power stations, electrical grids and communications networks.
paras.zh: 恐怖分子或敌对国家的特工可能会对一些企业和系统发动攻击，这些企业和系统控制着一国经济的关键部分，包括发电站、电网和通信网络。

w.m: adj. 敌对的；怀有敌意的
adj. 至关重要的；关键的
n. 通信（此义常用复数 communications）

paras.en: Such attacks are hard to pull off, but not impossible.
paras.zh: 这类攻击很难得手，但并非不可能。

paras.en: One precedent is the destruction in 2010 of centrifuges (离心机) at a nuclear facility in Iran by a computer program known as Stuxnet, the handiwork of American and Israeli software experts.
paras.zh: 一个先例是：2010年，一款名为“震网”的计算机程序摧毁了伊朗一座核设施里的离心机，这款程序出自美国和以色列软件专家之手。

paras.en: But such events are rare.
paras.zh: 但这类事件很少见。

paras.en: The biggest day-to-day threats faced by companies and government agencies come from crooks and spooks hoping to steal financial data and trade secrets, so this special report will focus mainly on cybercrime and cyber-espionage.
paras.zh: 企业和政府机构日常面临的最大威胁，来自企图窃取财务数据和商业机密的犯罪分子和间谍，因此本特别报道将主要关注网络犯罪和网络间谍活动。

paras.en: Smarter, better-organised hackers are making life tougher for the cyber-defenders, but the report will argue that even so a number of things can be done to keep everyone safer than they are now.
paras.zh: 更聪明、组织更严密的黑客正让网络防御者的日子越来越难过，但本报道将论证，即便如此，仍有一些办法可以让每个人都比现在更安全。

w.m: adj. 组织严密的（此处为比较级 better-organised：组织更严密的）

paras.en: One is to ensure that organisations get the basics of cyber-security right.
paras.zh: 其中一个办法是确保各机构把网络安全的基本功做好。

w.m: n. 基础；基本要素（常用复数）

paras.en: All too often breaches are caused by simple blunders, such as failing to separate systems containing sensitive data from those that do not need access to them.
paras.zh: 安全防线屡屡因简单的失误而被攻破，比如没有把存有敏感数据的系统与无需访问这些数据的系统隔开。

w.m: 屡屡；（令人遗憾地）太经常

paras.en: Companies also need to get better at anticipating where attacks may be coming from and at adapting their defences swiftly in response to new threats.
paras.zh: 企业还需要更善于预判攻击可能来自何方，也要更善于针对新威胁迅速调整防御措施。

w.m: 在……方面变得更好；更善于

paras.en: Technology can help, as can industry initiatives that allow firms to share intelligence about risks with each other.
paras.zh: 技术能帮上忙，让企业得以相互分享风险情报的行业举措也能。

paras.en: This report will also argue that there is a need to provide incentives to improve cyber-security, be they carrots or sticks.
paras.zh: 本报道还将论证，有必要提供激励措施来改善网络安全，无论是“胡萝卜”还是“大棒”。

paras.en: One idea is to encourage internet-service providers (ISPs), or the companies that manage internet connections, to shoulder more responsibility for identifying and helping to clean up computers infected with malicious software (malware).
paras.zh: 一种思路是鼓励互联网服务提供商（ISP），即管理互联网连接的公司，在识别并帮助清理感染了恶意软件的电脑方面承担更多责任。

w.m: n. 互联网服务提供商（缩写）

paras.en: Another is to find ways to ensure that software developers produce code with fewer flaws in it so that hackers have fewer security holes to exploit.
paras.zh: 另一种思路是设法确保软件开发人员编写出缺陷更少的代码，从而让黑客可利用的安全漏洞更少。

paras.en: An additional reason for getting tech companies to give a higher priority to security is that cyberspace is about to undergo another massive change.
paras.zh: 要让科技公司更优先考虑安全，还有一个理由：网络空间即将经历又一次巨变。

paras.en: Over the next few years billions of new devices, from cars to household appliances and medical equipment, will be fitted with tiny computers that connect them to the web and make them more useful.
paras.zh: 未来几年，从汽车到家用电器再到医疗设备，数十亿台新设备将装上微型计算机，借此连上网络，变得更加有用。

paras.en: Dubbed “the internet of things”, this is already making it possible, for example, to control home appliances using smartphone apps and to monitor medical devices remotely.
paras.zh: 这被称为“物联网”，已经让一些事情成为可能，例如用智能手机应用程序控制家用电器、远程监控医疗设备。

paras.en: But unless these systems have adequate security protection, the internet of things could easily become the internet of new things to be hacked.
paras.zh: 但是，除非这些系统具备足够的安全防护，否则物联网很容易就会变成由一个个可供黑客入侵的新物件连成的网络。

w.m: v. 非法侵入（计算机系统）；黑

paras.en: Plenty of people are eager to take advantage of any weaknesses they may spot.
paras.zh: 很多人都急于利用自己可能发现的任何弱点。

paras.en: Hacking used to be about geeky college kids tapping away in their bedrooms to annoy their elders.
paras.zh: 过去，黑客行为就是一些书呆子气的大学生在自己的卧室里不停地敲键盘，好让长辈们恼火。

w.m: n. 黑客行为；非法侵入计算机系统
adj. 书呆子气的；极客的

paras.en: It has grown up with a vengeance.
paras.zh: 如今，它已经长大，而且来势汹汹。

w.m: 猛烈地；（程度）远超寻常地

passages.name: 2016年 Passage Three
passages.title: 美国高等教育并非卓越堡垒
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与社会
passages.summary: 高校声称，州预算削减和成本攀升正在掏空美国教育最后一座卓越堡垒；作者认为，对这种呼声应当持怀疑态度：高等教育臃肿浪费，学术标准松弛，教学和学术研究平庸，研究生学位近乎盲目地激增。作者主张各州做三件事：设立真正的入学要求，提高教师的授课量，削减或取消用处最小的研究生项目。作者认为，这可能意味着招生规模缩小，但毕业生人数未必下降；只要肯努力，高等教育就可能成为卓越的堡垒。

paras.en: You should treat skeptically the loud cries now coming from colleges and universities that the last bastion of excellence in American education is being gutted by state budget cuts and mounting costs.
paras.zh: 如今，各高校大声疾呼，称州预算削减和不断攀升的成本正在掏空美国教育中最后一座卓越堡垒；对这种呼声，你应当持怀疑态度。

w.m: adj. 不断攀升的；日益增加的

paras.en: Whatever else it is, higher education is not a bastion of excellence.
paras.zh: 无论高等教育还能算是什么，它都不是卓越的堡垒。

paras.en: It is shot through with waste, lax academic standards and mediocre teaching and scholarship.
paras.zh: 其中充斥着浪费、松弛的学术标准，以及平庸的教学和学术研究。

paras.en: True, the economic pressures—from the Ivy League to state systems—are intense.
paras.zh: 诚然，从常春藤盟校到州立大学系统，经济压力都很大。

paras.en: Last year, nearly two-thirds of schools had to make midyear spending cuts to stay within their budgets.
paras.zh: 去年，将近三分之二的学校不得不在年中削减开支，以免超出预算。

paras.en: It is also true (as university presidents and deans argue) that relieving those pressures merely by raising tuitions and cutting courses will make matters worse.
paras.zh: 正如大学校长和院长们所说，仅靠提高学费、削减课程来缓解这些压力，会使情况更糟，这一点同样不假。

paras.en: Students will pay more and get less.
paras.zh: 学生会花更多的钱，得到的却更少。

paras.en: The university presidents and deans want to be spared from further government budget cuts.
paras.zh: 大学校长和院长们希望能免遭政府进一步削减预算。

paras.en: Their case is weak.
paras.zh: 他们的理由站不住脚。

w.m: adj. 站不住脚的；无力的

paras.en: Higher education is a bloated enterprise.
paras.zh: 高等教育是一个臃肿的行业。

paras.en: Too many professors do too little teaching to too many ill-prepared students.
paras.zh: 太多的教授教课太少，教的又是太多准备不足的学生。

paras.en: Costs can be cut and quality improved without reducing the number of graduates.
paras.zh: 不减少毕业生人数，也能削减成本、提高质量。

paras.en: Many colleges and universities should shrink.
paras.zh: 许多高校应当缩减规模。

paras.en: Some should go out of business.
paras.zh: 有些则应当停办。

paras.en: Consider: Except for elite schools, admissions standards are low.
paras.zh: 请看：除名校外，各校的录取标准都很低。

paras.en: About 70 percent of freshmen at four-year colleges and universities attend their first-choice schools.
paras.zh: 在四年制高校，约70%的新生上的是自己的第一志愿学校。

w.m: adj. 第一志愿的；首选的

paras.en: Roughly 20 percent go to their second choices.
paras.zh: 约20%上的是第二志愿。

paras.en: Most schools have eagerly boosted enrollments to maximize revenues (tuition and state subsidies).
paras.zh: 大多数学校都急切地扩大了招生，以求收入（学费和州政府补贴）最大化。

w.m: n. 招生人数；入学人数

paras.en: Dropout rates are high.
paras.zh: 辍学率很高。

paras.en: Half or more of freshmen don’t get degrees.
paras.zh: 半数或半数以上的新生拿不到学位。

paras.en: A recent study of PhD programs at 10 major universities (including Harvard, Stanford and Yale) also found high dropout rates for doctoral candidates.
paras.zh: 最近一项针对10所知名大学（包括哈佛、斯坦福和耶鲁）博士项目的研究也发现，博士生的辍学率很高。

paras.en: The attrition among undergraduates is particularly surprising because college standards have apparently fallen.
paras.zh: 本科生的流失尤其令人意外，因为大学的标准看来已经降低了。

paras.en: One study of seven top schools (including Amherst, Duke and the University of Michigan) found widespread grade inflation.
paras.zh: 一项针对七所顶尖学校（包括阿默斯特学院、杜克大学和密歇根大学）的研究发现，分数膨胀现象普遍存在。

paras.en: In 1963, half of the students in introductory philosophy courses got a B- or worse.
paras.zh: 1963年，哲学入门课程的学生中有一半得了B-或更低的成绩。

paras.en: By 1986, only 21 percent did.
paras.zh: 到1986年，这样的学生只占21%。

paras.en: If elite schools have relaxed standards, the practice is almost surely widespread.
paras.zh: 如果名校放松了标准，那么这种做法几乎可以肯定很普遍。

paras.en: Faculty teaching loads have fallen steadily since the 1960s.
paras.zh: 自20世纪60年代以来，教师的授课量一直在稳步下降。

paras.en: In major universities, senior faculty members often do less than two hours a day of teaching.
paras.zh: 在知名大学里，资深教师每天授课的时间往往不到两小时。

paras.en: Professors are “socialized to publish, teach graduate students and spend as little time teaching [undergraduates] as possible,” concludes James Fairweather of Penn State University in a new study.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的詹姆斯·费尔韦瑟在一项新研究中总结道：教授们“所受的熏陶就是要发表论著、教研究生，并尽可能少花时间教［本科生］”。

w.m: v. 使受（环境）熏陶；使适应社会

paras.en: Faculty pay consistently rises as undergraduate teaching loads drop.
paras.zh: 教师的薪酬总是随着本科授课量的减少而上涨。

paras.en: Universities have encouraged an almost mindless explosion of graduate degrees.
paras.zh: 各大学助长了研究生学位近乎盲目的激增。

w.m: adj. 盲目的；不动脑子的

paras.en: Since 1960, the number of master’s degrees awarded annually has risen more than fourfold to 337,000.
paras.zh: 自1960年以来，每年授予的硕士学位数量增长到原来的四倍多，达到337,000个。

paras.en: Between 1965 and 1989, the annual number of MBAs (masters of business administration) jumped from 7,600 to 73,100.
paras.zh: 1965年至1989年间，每年MBA（工商管理硕士）的数量从7,600猛增至73,100。

paras.en: Even so, our system has strengths.
paras.zh: 即便如此，我们的体制也有长处。

paras.en: It boasts many top-notch schools and allows almost anyone to go to college.
paras.zh: 它拥有许多一流学校，而且让几乎任何人都能上大学。

w.m: v. 拥有（引以为豪的东西）

paras.en: But mediocrity is pervasive.
paras.zh: 但平庸现象无处不在。

w.m: adj. 无处不在的；普遍的

paras.en: We push as many freshmen as possible through the door, regardless of qualifications.
paras.zh: 我们不问资质，把尽可能多的新生推进大学校门。

paras.en: Because bachelor’s degrees are so common, we create more graduate degrees of dubious worth.
paras.zh: 由于学士学位如此普遍，我们就设立更多价值可疑的研究生学位。

paras.en: Does anyone believe the MBA explosion has improved management?
paras.zh: 有谁相信MBA的激增提升了管理水平？

paras.en: You won’t hear much about this from college deans or university presidents.
paras.zh: 你很少会听到学院院长或大学校长谈起这些。

paras.en: They created this mess and are its biggest beneficiaries.
paras.zh: 他们造成了这个烂摊子，也是其中最大的受益者。

paras.en: Large enrollments support large faculties.
paras.zh: 大规模招生支撑着庞大的教师队伍。

w.m: n. 招生人数；入学人数

paras.en: More graduate students liberate tenured faculty from undergraduate teaching to concentrate on writing and research: the source of status.
paras.zh: 研究生多了，终身教职教师就能摆脱本科教学，专心著述和研究，而这正是地位的来源。

w.m: 使摆脱；把……从……中解放出来

paras.en: Richard Huber, a former college dean, writes knowingly in a new book (“How Professors Play the Cat Guarding the Cream: Why We’re Paying More and Getting Less in Higher Education”):
paras.zh: 曾任学院院长的理查德·休伯在新书《教授们如何扮演看守奶油的猫：为什么我们在高等教育上花得更多、得到的却更少》中以深谙内情的口吻写道：

w.m: adv. 深谙内情地；内行地
看守奶油的猫（喻看管自己觊觎之物，监守自盗）

paras.en: “Presidents, deans and trustees … call for more recognition of good teaching with prizes and salary incentives.
paras.zh: “校长、院长和董事们……呼吁通过奖项和薪酬激励，让优秀的教学得到更多认可。

paras.en: The reality is closer to the experience of Harvard University’s distinguished paleontologist Stephen Jay Gould: ‘To be perfectly honest, though lip service is given to teaching, I have never seriously heard teaching considered in any meeting for promotion….
paras.zh: 实际情况却更接近哈佛大学杰出的古生物学家斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德的经历：‘说实话，虽然教学在口头上受到重视，但我从来没有在任何一次晋升会议上听到有人认真考虑过教学……

paras.en: Writing is the currency of prestige and promotion.’”
paras.zh: 著述是换取声望和晋升的通货。’”

paras.en: About four-fifths of all students attend state-subsidized systems, from community colleges to prestige universities.
paras.zh: 在全体学生中，约五分之四就读于由州政府补贴的院校系统，从社区学院到名牌大学都有。

paras.en: How governors and state legislatures deal with their budget pressures will be decisive.
paras.zh: 州长和州议会如何应对预算压力，将起决定性作用。

paras.en: Private schools will, for better or worse, be influenced by state actions.
paras.zh: 无论是好是坏，私立学校都会受到各州举措的影响。

paras.en: The states need to do three things.
paras.zh: 各州需要做三件事。

paras.en: First, create genuine entrance requirements.
paras.zh: 第一，设立真正的入学要求。

w.m: adj. 真正的；名副其实的

paras.en: Today’s low standards tell high school students: You don’t have to work hard to go to college.
paras.zh: 如今的低标准等于在告诉高中生：你不必努力学习就能上大学。

paras.en: States should change the message by raising tuitions sharply and coupling the increase with generous scholarships based on merit and income.
paras.zh: 各州应当改变这一信号，办法是大幅提高学费，同时辅以根据成绩和收入发放的丰厚奖学金。

paras.en: To get scholarships, students would have to pass meaningful entrance exams.
paras.zh: 学生要获得奖学金，就必须通过有实质意义的入学考试。

w.m: adj. 有意义的；有实质内容的

paras.en: Ideally, the scholarships should be available for use at in-state private schools.
paras.zh: 理想的情况是，这些奖学金应当能在本州的私立学校使用。

paras.en: All schools would then compete for students on the basis of academic quality and costs.
paras.zh: 这样一来，所有学校就会凭学术质量和费用来争夺生源。

paras.en: Today’s system of general tuition subsidies provides aid to well-to-do families that don’t need it or to unqualified students who don’t deserve it.
paras.zh: 如今普遍补贴学费的制度，把资助给了并不需要资助的富裕家庭，或是给了不配得到资助的不合格学生。

w.m: adj. 不合格的；不够格的

paras.en: Next, states should raise faculty teaching loads, mainly at four-year schools.
paras.zh: 其次，各州应当提高教师的授课量，主要是在四年制学校。

paras.en: (Teaching loads at community colleges are already high.)
paras.zh: （社区学院的授课量已经很高了。）

paras.en: This would cut costs and reemphasize the primacy of teaching at most schools.
paras.zh: 这样做会削减成本，并在大多数学校重新突显教学的首要地位。

w.m: v. 再次强调；重新突显

paras.en: What we need are teachers who know their fields and can communicate enthusiasm to students.
paras.zh: 我们需要的是熟悉本专业领域、能把热情传递给学生的教师。

paras.en: Not all professors can be path-breaking scholars.
paras.zh: 并非所有教授都能成为开拓性的学者。

w.m: adj. 开拓性的；开创性的

paras.en: The excessive emphasis on scholarship generates many unread books and mediocre articles in academic journals.
paras.zh: 过分强调学术研究，催生了许多无人阅读的书和学术期刊上的平庸文章。

paras.en: “You can’t do more of one (research) without less of the other (teaching),” says Fairweather.
paras.zh: 费尔韦瑟说：“多做一样（研究），就必然少做另一样（教学）。”

paras.en: “People are working hard—it’s just where they’re working.”
paras.zh: “大家都在努力工作——问题只在于他们在哪方面下功夫。”

paras.en: Finally, states should reduce or eliminate the least useful graduate programs.
paras.zh: 最后，各州应当削减或取消用处最小的研究生项目。

paras.en: Journalism (now dubbed “communications”), business and education are prime candidates.
paras.zh: 新闻学（如今改称“传播学”）、商科和教育学是首要对象。

w.m: 首要对象；最合适的人选

paras.en: A lot of what they teach can—and should—be learned on the job.
paras.zh: 它们所教的很多内容，都可以而且应该在工作中学到。

paras.en: If colleges and universities did a better job of teaching undergraduates, there would be less need for graduate degrees.
paras.zh: 如果高校在本科生教学上做得更好，对研究生学位的需求就会减少。

paras.en: Our colleges and universities need to provide a better education to deserving students.
paras.zh: 我们的高校需要为够格的学生提供更好的教育。

w.m: adj. 够格的；值得帮助的

paras.en: This may mean smaller enrollments, but given today’s attrition rates, the number of graduates need not drop.
paras.zh: 这可能意味着招生规模缩小，但考虑到当前的流失率，毕业生人数未必会下降。

w.m: n. 招生人数；入学人数

paras.en: Higher education could become a bastion of excellence, if we would only try.
paras.zh: 只要我们肯努力，高等教育就可能成为卓越的堡垒。
